A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes.
recs.abstract: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549.

Pulsed Field or Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Atrial Fibrillation in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) frequently coexist, worsening prognosis. While catheter ablation confers clinical benefits in this high-risk population, comparative data between novel non-thermal pulsed field ablation (PFA) and established cryoballoon ablation (CBA) for AF-therapy in patients with HFrEF are limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of PFA- with CBA-based pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in patients with AF and HFrEF (left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%). METHODS: This retrospective, international multicenter study included patients with HFrEF undergoing first-time PVI-only procedures between 2018 and 2025. Propensity-score matching (1:1 ratio) was applied to balance baseline characteristics. The primary efficacy endpoint was the first recurrence of any atrial tachyarrhythmia after a 3-month blanking period. Secondary measures included safety events and procedural efficiency. RESULTS: A total of 700 patients from 12 German and Canadian centers were included, with 420 patients analyzed following propensity-score matching. At 12 months, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence with PFA was comparable to CBA (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 65.0% vs. 67.8%; hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.55; P=0.61). No statistically significant differences in observed safety outcomes were detected. PFA significantly improved procedural efficiency with shorter total procedure duration (58±22min vs. 72±22min; P<0.001), left-atrial dwell time (42±16min vs. 52±17min; P<0.001) and lower contrast dye use (0 ml [IQR 0-15] vs. 47 ml [IQR 30-56], P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AF and HFrEF, PFA-based PVI achieves similar rhythm-control efficacy and safety compared with CBA, while significantly enhancing procedural efficiency.

recs.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients Considered Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation: Randomized Outcomes Through 5 Years in ASAP-TOO.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) use in atrial fibrillation is suboptimal due to real or perceived bleeding risks. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an alternative to OAC, but pivotal trials used OAC comparators. OBJECTIVES: The study sought to assess the long-term safety and effectiveness of LAAC in patients deemed unsuitable for OAC. METHODS: The ASAP-TOO trial was a multinational randomized trial of patients with atrial fibrillation, CHA2DS2-VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes mellitus, prior stroke or transient ischemic attack or thromboembolism, vascular disease, age 65-74 years, sex category) score ≥2, and OAC unsuitability; target enrollment was 888 patients. Patients were assigned 2:1 to LAAC with a Watchman device or control treatment-single antiplatelet therapy or no therapy. Device patients received dual antiplatelet therapy for 3 months and aspirin through 12 months. The primary effectiveness endpoint was ischemic stroke or systemic embolism; the primary safety endpoint was death, ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, or 7-day device/procedure-related events requiring major intervention. RESULTS: Enrollment stopped early because of slow accrual, accentuated by the COVID-19 pandemic: only 481 patients were randomized (320 LAAC, 161 control treatment) and withdrawal was significant (7.8% LAAC, 24.2% control treatment), with disparate follow-up durations (median 876 days and 440.1 total patient-years of follow-up for control patients; median 1,768 days and 1,154.6 total patient-years of follow-up for LAAC patients), reducing statistical power. Patients were 75 ± 8 years of age, the CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.6 ± 1.7, and 34% had prior intracranial/subdural hemorrhage. Implantation success was 97.8%. Only 31 of the 101 planned primary effectiveness events occurred, fewer than the 34 events required to trigger the first planned interim analysis. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 1.0% of implant-attempted patients, meeting the prespecified performance goal (P < 0.0001); there were 3 pericardial effusions requiring intervention. At up to 5 years, ischemic stroke or systemic embolism occurred in 7.8% with LAAC and 11.4% with control treatment (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.35-1.52; P = 0.39). Major bleeding was 22.1% with LAAC and 15.7% with control treatment (HR: 1.64; 95% CI: 0.96-2.81; P = 0.067), concentrated during the first 3 months. In an exploratory analysis, disabling/fatal stroke was nominally less frequent with LAAC (2.2% vs 5.7%; HR: 0.32; 95% CI: 0.10-1.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this prematurely terminated and underpowered trial, LAAC implantation was successful, with acceptable safety. Long-term estimates with LAAC were numerically favorable for thromboembolism but imprecise, while early bleeding was increased with the mandated antiplatelet regimen. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory and integrated with contemporary evidence and shared decision making. (Assessment of the WATCHMAN Device in Patients Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation [ASAP-TOO]; NCT02928497).

recs.title: Natriuretic peptides in people with pacemakers: a post hoc analysis of the OPT-PACE randomised controlled trial.
Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Postarrest Cardiac Procedures for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective postarrest care facilitates optimal outcomes for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Relatively little research has evaluated whether there may be racial or ethnic disparities in the workup and management of the patient post arrest. METHODS: We retrospectively studied out-of-hospital cardiac arrests using the TriNetX research database. We defined out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as any emergency department visit (2013-2024) with a diagnosis of cardiac arrest and included patients who survived to admission. Multivariate adjusted logistic regression was used to compare rates of the following cardiac interventions across race or ethnicity: (1) echocardiography; (2) left heart catheterization; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention; (4) ventricular assist device placement; and (5) automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement. RESULTS: A total of 58 394 cases of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest met inclusion criteria. Compared with White patients (left heart catheterization: 13.9%, percutaneous coronary intervention: 7.1%, ventricular assist device: 3.0%, automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator: 0.9%), Black patients had lower odds of receiving left heart catheterization (7.2%, adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.55-0.64]), percutaneous coronary intervention (2.6%, aOR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.42-0.53]), ventricular assist device placement (1.6%, aOR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.41-0.70]). Hispanic/Latino patients were also less likely to receive left heart catheterization (8.9%, aOR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.64-0.80]), percutaneous coronary intervention (3.7%, aOR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.53-0.74]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33-0.81]). CONCLUSIONS: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

Myocardial Responses to Eplontersen in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: The CARDIO-TTRansform CMR study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). METHODS: This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable. RESULTS: We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], -6.7 percentage points [ -8.7 to -4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( -25.9ms [-41.7 to -10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (-19.1g [-28.0 to -10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8-8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6-8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.

recs.title: Impact of Coronary Sinus Reducer on the Extent of Ischemia in Functional Stress Tests.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The coronary sinus reducer is an established therapy for patients with refractory angina due to obstructive coronary artery disease who are not candidates for further revascularization. Although symptomatic benefits are well documented, its effect on objective measures of ischemia remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between coronary sinus reducer implantation and inducible myocardial ischemia assessed by functional stress testing. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained registry of consecutive patients undergoing coronary sinus reducer implantation between 2011 and 2024. Baseline assessment included Canadian Cardiovascular Society angina class, 6-minute walk test, stress echocardiography, and dipyridamole single-photon emission computed tomography imaging, repeated at 6 months. Coprimary outcomes were changes in stress wall motion score index and in the proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography. Clinical nonresponders were defined as no improvement in Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 12 months. RESULTS: Among 153 treated patients, 118 had complete imaging data. Median stress wall motion score index improved from 1.38 to 1.23 (P<0.001), and stress left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 55% to 60% (P=0.019). The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased from 52% to 24% (P<0.001). The summed difference score, available in 45 patients, did not change significantly. Clinically, 86% improved by ≥1 Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 6 months. CONCLUSIONS: Coronary sinus reducer implantation was associated with reduced inducible ischemia on stress echocardiography and with clinical improvement. The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased following Reducer implantation.

Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity for the assessment of severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation: derivation and external validation of threshold values.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Current guidelines include tricuspid inflow E-wave (>100 cm/s by pulsed-wave Doppler) as a semiquantitative criterion for diagnosing severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), despite limited supporting evidence. We assessed its diagnostic performance for identifying severe or greater TR, deriving and externally validating practical thresholds. METHODS AND RESULTS: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity was measured by pulsed-wave Doppler in consecutive patients with at least mild TR between December 2024 and February 2026. Among 178 patients (77±13 years, 65% women), TR was mild in 44, moderate in 61, severe in 44, massive in 15, and torrential in 14. Mean tricuspid E-wave velocity was 56±16 cm/s and increased with TR severity: 47±8, 50±10, 62±16, 67±13, and 77±21 cm/s for mild, moderate, severe, massive, and torrential TR. Only three patients had E-wave velocity >100 cm/s (one with severe and two with torrential TR). Using multiparametric echocardiographic grading as the reference standard, the >100 cm/s threshold showed 5.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and kappa 0.25 for severe or greater TR. As a continuous variable, E-wave velocity discriminated severe or greater TR with an AUC of 0.81. A lower threshold of 52 cm/s yielded 81% sensitivity and 67% specificity, whereas 47 cm/s provided 90% sensitivity and 43% specificity. External validation resulted in 94% sensitivity and 47% specificity. CONCLUSION: The guideline-recommended threshold of >100 cm/s is highly insensitive for detecting severe or greater TR. Lower cut-offs, particularly 47 cm/s, may be useful for screening to trigger a comprehensive multiparametric assessment.

recs.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial.
recs.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed (P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival (P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14-28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. Understanding whether and how microbiome-targeted interventions might improve transplant outcomes will therefore require careful disentangling of these effects within each specific treatment context. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03959241 .

recs.title: High Bleeding Risk and Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary PCI in STEMI: A Post Hoc Analysis of the PREMIUM Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) at high bleeding risk (HBR) are also at increased risk of ischemic events, making the optimal antiplatelet therapy challenging. Whether HBR identifies patients who may benefit from upfront aspirin omission at the time of primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: In this study, we sought to evaluate whether HBR modifies the effect of aspirin omission in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. METHODS: The PREMIUM trial randomized patients with STEMI before primary PCI to low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin plus prasugrel. In the DAPT group, patients meeting Academic Research Consortium (ARC) for HBR criteria were permitted to discontinue aspirin at 3 months, whereas non-HBR patients were intended to continue DAPT for 12 months. This post hoc analysis assessed the primary outcome of a 12-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, or myocardial infarction and the major secondary outcome of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5 bleeding according to HBR status. RESULTS: Among 2,189 patients, 786 (35.9%) met ARC-HBR criteria. HBR patients had higher rates of the primary outcome (16.2% vs 6.2%; HR: 2.68; 95% CI: 2.05-3.52) and the major secondary outcome (10.9% vs 4.9%; HR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.65-3.14). The primary outcome occurred with monotherapy vs DAPT in 18.0% vs 14.5% of HBR patients (HR: 1.29; 95% CI: 0.91-1.82) and 7.4% vs 5.0% of non-HBR patients (HR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.01-2.37; P for interaction = 0.51). The major secondary outcome occurred in 9.2% vs 12.5% of HBR patients (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.46-1.11) and 3.8% vs 6.1% of non-HBR patients (HR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.38-1.00; P for interaction = 0.67). CONCLUSIONS: ARC-HBR identified patients with a substantially higher overall risk after primary PCI for STEMI, but did not identify a subgroup with a more favorable treatment effect of upfront aspirin omission. Clinically meaningful treatment-effect modification cannot be excluded, owing to limited precision. These findings do not support using HBR status alone to guide upfront aspirin omission and should be interpreted in the context of the low-dose prasugrel regimen used in Japan. (Prasugrel Monotherapy Following Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction [PREMIUM; NCT05709626]).

recs.title: Population Impact of the 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Dyslipidemia Guideline on Lipid-Lowering Therapy Eligibility Among US Adults.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia guideline replaces the pooled cohort equations with the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease component of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events equations for primary prevention risk estimation and modifies lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) eligibility by lowering the risk-based treatment threshold and expanding diabetes and chronic kidney disease criteria. The population-level impact of this transition is uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 participants aged 40 to 75 years without self-reported atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and with available low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Survey weights were used to generate national estimates. Guideline-supported LLT eligibility was assessed under the 2018 pooled cohort equations-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association cholesterol framework and the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia framework. Current LLT use was assessed among guideline-supported adults. RESULTS: The analytic sample included 1662 participants, representing 115.05 million US adults. LLT was supported for 42.82 million adults under the 2018 framework and 42.17 million under the 2026 framework, a net decrease of 0.65 million. Reclassification was substantial: 37.42 million remained supported, 5.40 million lost support, 4.75 million newly gained support, and 67.48 million remained unsupported. Among supported adults, current LLT use was 39.4% under the 2018 framework and 40.5% under the 2026 framework. CONCLUSIONS: Transition to the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based framework produced little net change in LLT eligibility but meaningfully changed who was supported for therapy. Persistent undertreatment remains a major implementation gap.

Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether discontinuing statin therapy in older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease affects the time to a first cardiovascular event is not well characterized. METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial that enrolled adults at least 70 years of age who were taking statins for primary prevention. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either discontinue or continue statin therapy and other lipid-lowering therapies. The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. The primary analysis assessed noninferiority on the basis of the between-group difference in restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years, with a noninferiority margin of -5.2 weeks. RESULTS: A total of 1880 participants underwent randomization: 938 were assigned to the discontinuation group and 942 to the continuation group. The mean age of the participants was 77.5 years, and 46.9% were women. The between-group difference in the restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years was -2.0 weeks (95% confidence interval, -3.7 to -0.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Over a median follow-up of 103 weeks, 119 participants (12.7%) in the discontinuation group and 87 (9.2%) in the continuation group had a primary-outcome event. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 43.0% of the participants in the discontinuation group and in 39.8% in the continuation group. CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease, discontinuation of statin therapy was noninferior to continuation with respect to major cardiovascular events or death from any cause at 2 years. (Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation; STREAM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05178420.).

zG CreERT2 Uncovers Migration and Sex-Dependent NPC1 in Aldosterone Synthesis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The adrenal zona glomerulosa (zG) is the primary site of aldosterone synthesis. Inducible genetic tools are important for investigating zG cell function and fate in adult mice. This study aimed to generate and validate a tamoxifen-inducible, zG-specific aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mouse model and investigate the zG-specific role of NPC1 (Niemann-Pick type C1) in aldosterone synthesis. METHODS: Aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mice were generated by clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat-associated 9 knock-in of P2A (porcine teschovirus-1 2A peptide)-CreERT2 into the Cyp11b2 locus. Cre specificity and efficiency were validated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction, immunofluorescence, and lineage tracing. The model was then used to conditionally delete Npc1 in the zG. RESULTS: Cre expression and activity were confined to the zG. Heterozygous aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mice showed normal adrenal morphology and hormone levels despite reduced Cyp11b2 expression. Homozygosity of the CreERT2 allele significantly reduced Cyp11b2 expression and aldosterone levels and increased renin in both sexes, indicating a gene-dosage effect. Lineage tracing confirmed the centripetal migration of zG cells to the zona fasciculata, which was faster in female mice. Strikingly, zG-specific Npc1 deletion reduced aldosterone in female mice under a normal-sodium diet, whereas increased renin and decreased aldosterone-to-renin ratio were observed in male mice under a high-sodium diet, indicating a sex-dependent effect. CONCLUSIONS: The aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mouse provides a powerful and specific platform for spatiotemporally controlled dissection of zG biology, with the heterozygous line recommended for use to avoid Cre-associated dosage effects. Using this model, we identify a sex-dependent effect of zG-specific Npc1 deletion on aldosterone regulation, providing new insight into sex differences in adrenal physiology and aldosterone-related disorders.

Impact of the 2026 Dyslipidemia Guideline on ASCVD Reclassification and Statin Recommendations in MESA.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia recommends the use of the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of cardiovascular disease EVENTs) equations to predict atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk while concurrently revising previous risk-category thresholds. The impact of these reclassifications is yet to be described. OBJECTIVES: The authors characterized ASCVD reclassification and statin recommendations under the 2026 guideline, evaluated clinical events under this reclassification, and examined risk enhancement with risk enhancers and coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden. METHODS: Adults (N = 6,098) from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) were assessed, comparing the Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) and 2013 thresholds to PREVENT with 2026 thresholds. We evaluated the degree of directional reclassification, impact on statin recommendations, and risk enhancement with biomarkers and CAC burden. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 10 years, 6.0% of participants had an ASCVD event. PREVENT reclassified 16.4% to a lower and 13.1% to a higher risk category as compared to the PCE. The statin recommendation under PREVENT was 50.4% compared to 55.2% under PCE. Of those who were no longer recommended for statin use, 4.9% went on to have an event. Individuals who were reclassified downward but had elevated CAC or any risk-enhancing factors had a higher event rate. CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to the 2026 guideline may lead to a small net downward reclassification of predicted ASCVD risk. Statin recommendations will fall modestly, however, not accompanied by a substantial number of subsequent events. Risk enhancers and elevated CAC identify higher risk subgroups than their PREVENT risk would suggest, emphasizing their supporting role in risk prediction.

Androgen Imbalance, Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages, and Mortality in Men.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Androgen measures reflect adiposity, metabolic health, and systemic illness, but their associations with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome and mortality may differ across measures and combined profiles. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to examine associations of total testosterone (TT), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), calculated free testosterone (cFT), and joint TT-SHBG phenotypes with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome and mortality. METHODS: We analyzed men aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013 to 2016 using survey-weighted logistic (odds ratio [OR]) and Cox (hazard ratio [HR]) regression models. Advanced CKM syndrome comprised determinate National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey-adapted stages 3 to 4; cFT was calculated using the Vermeulen equation. Analyses assessed adiposity adjustment and mortality robustness. RESULTS: Among 5,505 men, 4,005 had determinate CKM status. Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome (OR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.31-2.42), but the association was attenuated after adjustment for body mass index (OR: 1.27; 95% CI: 0.90-1.79) or waist circumference (OR: 1.22; 95% CI: 0.85-1.75), suggesting that adiposity may partly account for this association. Low TT and cFT measures showed no consistent association with all-cause mortality. In exploratory analyses, the low-TT/high-SHBG phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR: 2.06; 95% CI: 1.18-3.58). CONCLUSIONS: Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome, but this association was strongly adiposity-dependent. The low-TT/high-SHBG profile showed an exploratory mortality association not observed for TT or cFT alone and may represent a distinct systemic-vulnerability phenotype. These findings underscore the noninterchangeability of androgen measures and support prospective evaluation of combined TT-SHBG profiles.

recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of complete revascularization for patients with acute coronary syndrome, multivessel disease and complex nonculprit coronary lesions (NCL) remains unclear. METHODS: The BIOVASC trial randomized patients with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease to immediate complete revascularization and staged complete revascularization. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, unplanned ischemia-driven revascularization, or cerebrovascular events at 2-year follow-up. In this exploratory post hoc analysis, patients were classified as having complex NCL if at least 1 nonculprit lesion met the following criteria: true bifurcation; severe calcification; lesion length >20 mm; aorto-ostial lesion; left main lesion. We aimed to compare a strategy of immediate complete revascularization and staged complete revascularization in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease with complex NCL. Moreover, we sought to compare patients with complex and noncomplex NCLs in terms of clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Among the 1525 patients enrolled in the BIOVASC trial, 550 (36.1%) had a complex NCL. The presence of a complex NCL was associated with a significantly higher incidence of the primary end point compared with noncomplex NCL (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.11-2.02]; P=0.01), including spontaneous myocardial infarction (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.86 [95% CI, 1.12-3.09]; P=0.02). In patients with complex NCL, the cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 15.7% in the immediate complete revascularization group and 17.5% in the staged complete revascularization group (hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.57-1.31]; P=0.49). No significant interaction was observed between the presence of a complex NCL and revascularization strategy for the primary end point (P for interaction=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease, patients with complex NCL experienced worse clinical outcomes at 2-year follow-up, driven by higher rates of myocardial infarction. However, no statistically significant interaction was observed between NCL complexity and the effect of immediate complete revascularization versus staged complete revascularization. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03621501.

recs.title: 2-Year Patency as a Lightning Rod? Biological Hypotheses Linking PCSK9-Inhibition to Favorable Vein Graft Remodeling.
Life Expectancy After Incident Ischemic Stroke in a Bi-Ethnic Population: Estimates Over 2005 to 2022.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study measured 5- and 10-year life expectancy after an incident ischemic stroke using a high-quality sample of Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White patients over a recent period. METHODS: Data were from the Brain Attack Surveillance in Corpus Christi Project. The sample included 2011 Mexican American and 1262 non-Hispanic White men and women who had an incident ischemic stroke during 2005 to 2022 and were aged 45 years or older at the time of stroke. Participants were followed up to 18 years. Primary outcome was 5- and 10-year life expectancy. Discrete-time logistic regression models were implemented. RESULTS: Mean age at incident stroke was 69 years. There was no difference in the odds of dying between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White men and women after adjustment for age at stroke and sex. Among men, an incident stroke at age 70 years was associated with a 10-year life expectancy of 6.4 years (95% CI: 6.1-6.6) in Mexican Americans and 6.5 years (95% CI: 6.2-6.9) in non-Hispanic White adults. Among women, the analogous 10-year life expectancy was 6.7 years (95% CI: 6.3-6.8) in Mexican Americans and 6.8 years (95% CI: 6.4-7.0) in non-Hispanic White adults. Comparing these estimates to life expectancy at age 70 in the general US population indicates that stroke is associated with a life shortening effect of 2.1 to 2.4 years over 10 years. CONCLUSIONS: Life expectancy after an ischemic stroke did not differ between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White adults. Incident ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial life shortening effects in the recent period.

Effects of Eplontersen on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: Insights from the CARDIO-TTRansform Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In CARDIO-TTRansform, the TTR (transthyretin) silencer eplontersen did not significantly reduce the primary end point of cardiovascular death and recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, although treatment effects varied by baseline TTR stabilizer use. Whether eplontersen favorably affects cardiac structure and function is unknown. METHODS: CARDIO-TTRansform randomized 1432 patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy to eplontersen (45 mg) subcutaneously every 4 weeks or placebo. Echocardiograms were performed at baseline and weeks 61, 97, and 140. Associations of baseline echocardiographic measures with all-cause mortality and the primary end point were evaluated using Cox and semiparametric proportional rates models. Between-group differences at week 140 were analyzed with mixed models for repeated measures. RESULTS: Among 1426 participants with baseline echocardiograms (mean age, 76±7 years, 91% men, 85% wild type, 57% receiving stabilizers), baseline measures of left ventricular systolic function (LV ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, stroke volume, myocardial contraction fraction), diastolic function (E wave deceleration time, septal e', average E/e'), and right ventricular function and hemodynamics were independently associated with all-cause mortality or the primary end point. At week 140 (echocardiograms available in 554 patients in the eplontersen group and 506 in the placebo group), eplontersen attenuated increases in mean LV wall thickness (least-squares mean [LSM] difference, -0.24 mm [95% CI, -0.48 to -0.01]) and declines in LV stroke volume (LSM difference, 1.88 mL [95% CI, 0.07-3.69]), myocardial contraction fraction (LSM difference, 0.88% [95% CI, 0.25-1.57]), average E/e' (LSM difference, -0.71 [95% CI, -1.36 to -0.07]), and right ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LSM difference, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.00-0.85]) versus placebo in the overall cohort. Beneficial effects were driven almost exclusively by patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. No significant treatment effects were observed in patients receiving stabilizers. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, eplontersen modestly attenuated deterioration in prognostically important measures of LV systolic, diastolic and right ventricular function, primarily among patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. These findings complement the clinical findings of CARDIO-TTRansform and suggest that TTR silencing may attenuate progression of cardiac dysfunction in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04136171; URL: xxx; Unique identifier: 2019-002835-27.

recs.title: Case Volumes and Outcomes of Early-Career Operators Performing TAVR in the United States.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Operator experience is a key determinant of outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, whether early-career operators achieve comparable results to more experienced peers is unknown. Herein, we evaluate case volumes, patient risk profiles, and 30-day outcomes of early-career versus non-early-career operators performing TAVR in the United States. METHODS: Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry, we identified isolated TAVR procedures from October 2011 through March 2024. Early-career status was defined as ≤5 years in independent practice (based on board certification or first TAVR date); non-early-career status was >5 years. Multivariable hierarchical models adjusted for patient-, procedural-, operator-, and site-level factors, including annualized institutional TAVR volume, while accounting for clustering of procedures within operators and operators within sites. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and a composite of death, stroke, major bleeding, stage III acute kidney injury, or moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak. RESULTS: A total of 634 723 TAVR procedures were performed by 3126 operators across 847 sites, including 90 376 (14.2%) by early-career operators. Median annualized lifetime volume was lower for early-career operators (13 [interquartile range, 5-31] versus 19 [interquartile range, 7-42] cases per year; P<0.001). After adjustment, 30-day mortality was similar between early-career and non-early-career operators (2.38% versus 2.44%; risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.92-1.01]; P=0.293), whereas the composite end point was lower among early-career operators (11.19% versus 11.77%; risk ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.93-0.98]; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In a national TAVR registry, early-career operators performed fewer cases but achieved similar 30-day mortality and a modestly lower adjusted composite event rate relative to more experienced peers. These findings suggest that within the structured, team-based environment of contemporary TAVR programs, early-career status alone is not associated with inferior procedural outcomes and should not be viewed as a barrier to independent practice.

recs.title: Age-Related Differences in Physical Activity for Primary Prevention of Coronary Heart Disease: Insights From Wearable Accelerometers.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current physical activity recommendations suggest at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity for primary prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD) across ages. However, age-related disparities exist in exercise capability, engagement, and guideline adherence, and their implications for CHD prevention remain underexplored. METHODS: We included wrist-worn accelerometer data from 80 243 UK Biobank participants (aged 61.54±7.84 years, 57.3% women), classified as older (≥65 years; n=31 663) or middle-aged (<65 years; n=48 580). Cox proportional hazards models were applied to examine age-specific associations between physical activity and incident CHD. Nonlinear and dose-response relationships were assessed using restricted cubic splines, and age-related differences were tested using likelihood ratio tests. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 7.88 years, 3764 CHD events occurred. A 20% lower CHD risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.8) was observed at approximately 60 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in older adults versus 330 minutes per week in middle-aged adults (Pinteraction=0.006). Guideline adherence was associated with stronger inverse associations in older than in middle-aged adults (HR, 0.72 versus 0.85; Pinteraction=0.029). Older weekend warriors exhibited a 28% lower CHD risk, comparable with regularly active individuals, whereas the association was weaker and nonsignificant in middle-aged adults (Pinteraction=0.005). At 150 minutes per week, a 10% lower CHD risk corresponded to an acceleration threshold of 100 milligravity in middle-aged adults but approximately 55 milligravity in older adults. A possible U-shaped relationship was observed in older adults. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest potential age-related heterogeneity in wearable-measured physical activity for CHD prevention, and may help motivate activity engagement among older adults and enhance CHD prevention.

recs.title: Iron Repletion in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The IRONMET-HFpEF Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Iron deficiency is present in >50% of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and is associated with reduced exercise capacity and survival. Whether iron repletion improves exercise capacity as objectively measured by peak oxygen uptake ([Formula: see text]) is unknown. The IRONMET-HFpEF trial (Impact of Intravenous Iron Repletion on Mechanisms of Exercise Intolerance in HFpEF) sought to determine whether ferric derisomaltose (FDI) compared with placebo improves peak [Formula: see text] in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency. METHODS: This was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and iron deficiency, defined as ferritin <100 ng/mL or <300 ng/mL with transferrin saturation <20%. Participants were enrolled between December 2021 and April 2026. Single-dose ferric derisomaltose (1000 mg; n=44) or placebo (n=21) was administered once intravenously. The primary end point was the change in peak [Formula: see text] from baseline to 12 weeks with an analysis of covariance model including terms for treatment group, baseline peak [Formula: see text], and sex. Secondary end points included changes in [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, New York Heart Association class, health status assessed by the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score, and iron biomarkers at 12 weeks. RESULTS: Among 65 randomized participants (median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 58-76 years], 72% women, transferrin saturation 16.0±7.4%, ferritin 57.8±48.9 ng/mL), 64 (98.5%) completed the study. The median baseline peak [Formula: see text] was 12.7 mL·kg-1·min-1 (interquartile range, 10.6-15.8 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the FDI group and 12.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (11.6-14.6 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the placebo group. At 12 weeks, peak [Formula: see text] improved by 1.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI, 0.6-1.7) in the FDI group and was unchanged (0.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, -0.7 to 0.9]) in the placebo group (least-squares mean difference, 1.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, 0.2-1.9]; P=0.02). [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, and New York Heart Association class also improved in the FDI compared with the placebo group (all P<0.05), whereas the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score did not differ significantly between groups (FDI group, +4.4 [95% CI, -2.4 to 11.2]; P=0.20). FDI increased transferrin saturation (9.4% [95% CI, 4.9%-13.9%]) and ferritin (183 ng/mL [95% CI, 128-238]) compared with the placebo group (PLSMD<0.001 for both). There were no serious adverse events related to FDI administration. CONCLUSIONS: In the largest trial to date of iron repletion in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency, FDI improved multiple measures of exercise capacity. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04945707.

recs.title: Systemic Microvascular Endothelial Dysfunction in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Type 2 Diabetes: A Pooled Analysis of GLADIATOR-HFpEF, IRON-HFpEF, EMPA-MVD, Hoorn Diabetes Care System, and Healthy Controls.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder featuring microvascular dysfunction and metabolic comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the extent to which systemic microvascular abnormalities reflect HFpEF or coexisting T2D remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to characterize systemic microvascular dysfunction in patients with HFpEF and to evaluate the contribution of comorbid T2D. METHODS: Systemic microvascular function, defined as flow responses expressed as cutaneous vascular conductance, was assessed using laser speckle contrast analysis with iontophoresis of acetylcholine, insulin, and sodium nitroprusside. Analysis adjusted for age and sex were performed across healthy controls (n = 23), T2D (n = 138), HFpEF without T2D (n = 63), and HFpEF with T2D (n = 27). RESULTS: Insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion was reduced in participants with T2D (-0.30 arbitrary perfusion units [APU]/mm Hg; P < 0.001) and in HFpEF with T2D (-0.32 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.004) compared with controls, whereas responses in HFpEF without T2D were not different from controls. Perfusion responses to sodium nitroprusside were reduced in T2D and HFpEF with T2D, while responses to acetylcholine were preserved. No statistically detectable interaction between HFpEF and T2D was observed. Sex did not modify the relationship between HFpEF and microvascular dysfunction, but exploratory sex-stratified analyses showed reduced insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion in T2D (mean difference: -0.30 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.020) and HFpEF + T2D (mean difference: -0.51 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.002) compared with controls. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

recs.title: Normative Values for QRS Duration in Athletes aged 12-35 years undergoing Pre-participation Exams.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Due to limited data on athletic QRS duration, this cross-sectional study aims to establish normative digital reference values in asymptomatic, apparently healthy athletes ages 12 to 35 undergoing pre-participation examinations. OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that QRS duration of athletes would be longer in males, increase with age, and rarely exceed 120 ms in the absence of a bundle branch block. METHODS: We analyzed QRS duration from standardized digital ECG recordings in 9,084 athletes (58% male, age 12-35 years, mean age 18) obtained during pre-participation examinations. Sex-stratified 99th-percentile quantile-regression equations were developed and applied in an APP to demonstrate that QRS duration outliers could be easily identified. RESULTS: Females had shorter QRS durations than males (88.5 +/- 8.3 ms vs. 97.3 +/- 9.1 ms; mean difference 8.9 ms, 95% CI: 8.5-9.2 ms). QRS duration demonstrated a positive cross-sectional association with age and was greater in men than women. Female 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 106.0 ms and 108.0 ms, respectively, with range 62-130 ms. Male 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 116.0 ms and 118.3 ms, respectively, with range 70-132 ms. 7(0.2%) females and 55 (1.0%) males had QRS duration >120 ms. 99th percentile quantile regression equations were derived (Female: QRS=99.6 + 0.56 x age; Male: QRS = 104.7 + 0.74 x age). CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that defining prolonged QRS criteria necessitates adjustments according to age and sex. To facilitate future prospective research, we offer specific regression models to detect outliers.

recs.title: Initial Diabetes Therapy After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Long-Term Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is common among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but optimal post-CABG glucose-lowering therapy remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the OptumLabs Data Warehouse of adults with T2D undergoing isolated CABG from 2012-2024. Follow-up began 30 days after discharge. Glucose-lowering therapy was modeled as a time-varying exposure with patients contributing no-observed-therapy person-time until the first qualifying post-discharge fill. Pairwise comparisons used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were heart failure hospitalization, stroke, and repeat coronary revascularization. RESULTS: Among 19,237 patients, 24.9% had no observed post-discharge therapy, 42.8% received metformin, 22.9% received insulin, and 9.4% received GLP-1RA/SGLT2i therapy. All active therapies were associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy, including GLP-1RA/SGLT2i (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.87), metformin (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.66), and insulin (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.67-0.84). Among active therapies, metformin was associated with lower mortality than insulin (HR, 0.61 [0.54-0.70]); GLP-1RA/SGLT2i comparisons with metformin and insulin were less precise. Metformin was also associated with lower cumulative incidence of heart failure hospitalization than no observed therapy and insulin, and lower stroke incidence than insulin. CONCLUSIONS: Observed glucose-lowering therapy initiation after CABG was associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy across all active treatment groups. These findings highlight a potential care gap and suggest that proper initiation of diabetes therapy after CABG represents an important opportunity to improve long-term outcomes following surgical revascularization.

recs.title: First-in-Human Experience With a Novel Monorail Microcatheter for Instantaneous Coronary Pressure and Flow Velocity Measurements.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Invasive coronary physiology enables comprehensive assessment of epicardial and microvascular disease, but its routine use is limited by technical complexity and prolonged acquisition time. OBJECTIVES: The PyCath system is a rapid-exchange microcatheter engineered to simultaneously measure intracoronary pressure and thermoconvection-based flow velocity. METHODS: First-in-human, prospective, single-arm study evaluating the safety and performance of the PyCath system in patients with a clinical indication for coronary physiology assessment. The microcatheter was advanced over a standard coronary guidewire to acquire simultaneous pressure and flow velocity at baseline and during hyperemia. The primary objectives were procedural safety, defined as device-related major adverse cardiac events, and device performance, defined as successful acquisition of pressure and velocity signals. Data were analyzed by an independent core laboratory. RESULTS: Seventeen patients (mean age 59.3 ± 9.4 years, 76.5% males) referred for invasive coronary physiology assessment were included. Intracoronary pressure and velocity measurements were feasible in 100% and 88% of cases, respectively. The mean time required to obtain both measurements was 70.6 ± 23.6 seconds. The mean fractional flow reserve, coronary flow velocity reserve, and hyperemic microvascular resistance were 0.84 ± 0.12, 2.28 ± 0.79, and 1.46 ± 0.77, respectively. There were no device-related major adverse cardiac events. Test-retest reproducibility was good-to-excellent with intraclass correlation coefficients for fractional flow reserve, coronary flow velocity reserve, and hyperemic microvascular resistance of 0.979 (0.934-0.993), 0.798 (0.477-0.933), and 0.759 (0.397-0.919). CONCLUSIONS: In this first-in-human experience, the PyCath microcatheter enabled safe and reproducible measurements of intracoronary pressure and flow velocity with excellent reproducibility.

recs.title: ZEUS has spoken: lessons for IL-6 inhibition and the road ahead.
SCORE2 for Latin America and the Caribbean: adding another piece to the global puzzle of cardiovascular risk prediction.
HOPO 14-1, an Oral Actinide Chelator: A Phase 1 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Current treatments approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for internal actinide contamination (pentetate calcium trisodium and pentetate zinc trisodium) require intravenous injection or nebulized inhalation under medical supervision and have limited radionuclide coverage. HOPO 14-1, an oral form of 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO), is the first shelf-stable, broad-spectrum actinide chelator in clinical development that does not require intravenous access or trained personnel. In preclinical models, 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) removed a broad range of actinides, and its oral route supports scalable emergency medical use. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic parameters, and excretion of a single dose of HOPO 14-1 in healthy adults. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a phase 1 nonrandomized clinical trial including 42 healthy adults (6 per dose level) with evaluations for 14 days after administration of a single dose and conducted at a single site in the US. Participants were recruited and screened between March 2023 and July 2025 and follow-up was completed in August 2025. INTERVENTION: Single oral dose of HOPO 14-1 administered at 1 of 7 dose levels (100 mg, 200 mg, 500 mg, 1200 mg, 2500 mg, 5000 mg, or 7500 mg) with follow-up through day 14 after dose administration. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the incidence and severity of adverse events, drug-related adverse events, and serious adverse events. The secondary outcomes were plasma pharmacokinetic parameters and cumulative urinary and fecal excretion. RESULTS: Of the 42 healthy adults enrolled (median age, 43 [IQR, 34-51] years; 64% female), all received a single dose of HOPO 14-1 (administered across all dose levels as assigned). There were no serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxic effects. The drug-related adverse events included diarrhea (31%), vomiting (14%), headache (12%), and fatigue (7%); all were mild to moderate in severity. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the principal tolerability findings and most evident at the highest doses. The plasma pharmacokinetic parameters demonstrated rapid absorption (median time of maximum plasma concentration, 0.86 [range, 0.53-1.60] hours to 1.90 [range, 1.40-2.90] hours) and dose-dependent increases in systemic exposure, with greater than proportional increases at higher doses. Fecal excretion was the primary route of elimination; urinary excretion was minimal. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Single oral doses of HOPO 14-1 up to 7500 mg were administered without dose-limiting toxicity or serious adverse events in healthy adults. Gastrointestinal tolerability defined the practical single-dose ceiling. These findings establish the first human safety and pharmacokinetic profile of a novel, orally administered actinide chelator and support further clinical evaluation of HOPO 14-1 as a countermeasure for internal radionuclide and heavy metal contamination. Development of a deployable and population-level emergency intervention addresses a long-standing unmet need with important implications for public health preparedness. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05628961.

Tailoring Early Interventional Approach in Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis: When Might Early AVR Be Too Late?
CaMKIIδ-TRPC6 Activates an RyR-BKCa Feedback Axis in Aging Arteries.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: TRP (transient receptor potential) cation channels play a crucial role in maintaining normal blood pressure and flow. We hypothesize that, during aging, TRPC6 (transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily C member 6)-mediated Ca2+ influx promotes sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ refilling and RyR (ryanodine receptor) Ca2+ sparks, thereby activating BKCa (large-conductance Ca2+-activated K+) channels to limit myogenic arterial tone. METHODS: Using vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) from resistance-sized small mesenteric arteries, we tested selective TRPC6 inhibitors (SH045 and SAR7334) and smooth muscle-specific TRPC6 knockout mice. Ca2+ sparks, BKCa currents, and myogenic tone were measured in young (3-4 months) and old (12-14 months) mice. CaMKIIδ (Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IIδ) signaling was assessed pharmacologically and with a proteolysis-targeting chimera peptide degrader targeting CaMKIIδ. RESULTS: Inhibiting TRPC6 with SH045 or SAR7334 suppressed RyR-mediated Ca2+ spark generation in VSMCs from old mice but not young mice. Similar results were found in smooth muscle-specific TRPC6 knockout mice. SH045 or SAR7334 also suppressed BKCa currents and elicited constriction in mesenteric arteries from old mice. These effects were due to increased translocation of TRPC6 channels to the VSMC plasma membrane, mediated by CaMKIIδ signaling. Using a proteolysis-targeting chimera peptide degrader targeting CaMKIIδ, we demonstrated the impact of CaMKIIδ on TRPC6 externalization and RyR activation in old VSMCs. CONCLUSIONS: Together, our findings identify age-dependent CaMKIIδ upregulation as a key regulator of TRPC6 membrane trafficking, thereby indirectly enhancing RyR-BKCa signaling through sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ handling and promoting VSMC hyperpolarization and vasodilation in aging.
