Atherosclerotic plaque healing: mechanisms and clinical relevance.
recs.abstract: Atherosclerotic plaque healing is a dynamic biological mechanism that occurrs after plaque disruption and represents an endogenous reparative response within the atherosclerotic lesion. This process unfolds through three partially overlapping phases: endogenous thrombus lysis, granulation tissue formation, and re-endothelialization. Through the coordinated interaction of circulating cells, vascular wall components, and soluble mediators, plaque healing promotes fibrous repair and structural stabilization of the disrupted plaque. For many years, plaque healing remained primarily a histopathological observation described in post-mortem studies. The advent of high-resolution intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography, has enabled in vivo visualization of the characteristic layered morphology of healed plaques, providing direct clinical confirmation of these early pathological findings. These observations have significantly improved our understanding of the clinical significance of plaque healing. Healed plaques are more frequently observed in patients with chronic coronary syndromes, supporting the concept that healing contributes to plaque stabilization. At the same time, recurrent cycles of plaque disruption followed by repair may lead to progressive luminal narrowing, thereby contributing to the long-term progression of coronary atherosclerosis. This review provided an updated overview of the clinical significance and implications of healed plaques in coronary artery disease, the mechanisms underlying plaque healing, and examines emerging intracoronary and non-invasive imaging modalities that allow their in vivo identification.

recs.title: Safety and Efficacy of Apixaban Therapy for Coronary Artery Aneurysms After Kawasaki Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation combined with aspirin lowers the risk of coronary thrombosis in patients with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms following Kawasaki disease. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of apixaban in this high-risk pediatric population and compare it to conventional anticoagulant therapy. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we described our experience with the use of apixaban in patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms. In patients who were previously exposed to conventional anticoagulation, we compared rates of new coronary thrombosis or myocardial infarction (effectiveness) and clinically relevant bleeding (safety) during apixaban versus antecedent conventional therapy. All patients received concomitant antiplatelet agents. Apixaban dosing was guided by weight and anti-Xa chromogenic assays. RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2025, 28 patients with Kawasaki disease (median age 6.7 years; 75% male) with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms were prescribed apixaban. Of these, 27 (96%) had previously received vitamin K antagonists or low molecular weight heparin. The rates of new coronary thrombosis and new myocardial infarctions were not higher when patients received apixaban versus conventional anticoagulation (0.025 versus 0.041 events per person-year; incidence rate ratio [IRR], 0.61 [95% CI, 0.06-3.3] and 0.013 versus 0.041 events per person-year; IRR, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.01-2.5], respectively). Rates of clinically relevant bleeding were also not higher for apixaban versus conventional therapy (0.038 versus 0.058 events per person-year, IRR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.11-2.5]). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center series of pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms, apixaban combined with antiplatelet therapy was well tolerated and demonstrated no evidence of increased harm relative to conventional anticoagulants. Multicenter research is needed to confirm these findings and define the optimal therapeutic range for apixaban in this high-risk population.

recs.title: Temporal Trends and Racial and Geographic Variation in Left Atrial Appendage Closure Among Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
Standard versus Sheath-in-Sheath Technique for Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing: A Comparative Single-Center Analysis.
Anticoagulation in Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation: An Evidence-Based Framework for Individualized Management.
recs.abstract: The increasing use of wearable monitoring technologies and cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has led to frequent incidental detection of subclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF), yet the role of long-term anticoagulation remains uncertain. Growing evidence indicates that SCAF is a separate clinical entity on the continuous spectrum of atrial disease and not just a precursor to clinical disease. We propose that anticoagulation in SCAF should be guided by integrating arrythmia burden, baseline clinical risk and the degree of structural atrial cardiomyopathy in addition to life expectancy and patient preferences. This review synthesizes data from observational studies, randomized clinical trials, and post-hoc analyses to provide a comprehensive and practical framework for individualized anticoagulation, and risk-benefit considerations.

recs.title: A simple wave in a complex sea: tricuspid E velocity and the grading of regurgitation.
Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing. METHODS: A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The final seven-variable ARC included age >60 years, abrupt onset pain, severe pain, hypotension/shock, neurological deficit, pulse deficit, and known aortic disease. Patients were classified as positive if any ARC variable was present and negative only if all variables were absent. In the derivation cohort, ARC achieved a sensitivity of 99.2% (95% CI 99.1-99.3). In the ADvISED/PROFUNDUS cohort (4598 patients, 10.2% AAS prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100) with specificity 23.7% (95% CI 22.4-25.0). In the DAShED cohort (5346 patients, 0.3% prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 76.8-100) and specificity 36.4% (95% CI 35.1-37.7), ruling out 36.3% of patients without missing any AAS cases. CONCLUSIONS: ARC is an externally validated, pragmatic clinical rule demonstrating high diagnostic sensitivity in a large external validation cohort. When incorporated into existing diagnostic pathways, ARC has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing while maintaining diagnostic performance. Further prospective validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

recs.title: Balloon perforation of a balloon-in-basket pulsed field ablation catheter during pulmonary vein isolation.
Exercise Prescriptions Recommended for Cardiovascular Health.
Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion. METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke. RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice. CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

recs.title: Against All Odds: A New CADENCE in Cardiopulmonary Remodeling.
Impact of Smoking on Transfusion Outcomes in Anemia and Myocardial Infarction: A MINT Trial Analysis.
Right Heart Dysfunction in Valvular Heart Disease: Epidemiology, Prognosis, and Management Considerations.
recs.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is an important determinant of clinical outcomes across a wide range of cardiovascular pathologies. As the prevalence of valvular heart disease (VHD) increases with the aging population, the intersection between RV function and VHD will become all the more relevant for proper risk assessment, treatment selection, and prognostication. Even though RV dysfunction may not always be attributed to VHD, we aim to give clinicians, researchers, and regulators a deep understanding of how patients with VHD should be evaluated for RV dysfunction and treated when RV dysfunction coexists with VHD. We begin with a discussion of the epidemiology and diagnostic evaluation of RV dysfunction in patients with a variety of VHD subgroups, including right-side (ie, associated with the tricuspid valve) and left-side (ie, associated with the mitral and aortic valves) VHD. Attention is also given in that section to contemporary methods and evolving techniques for identifying and phenotyping different forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD. No single imaging test practically or comprehensively captures all degrees and forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD; therefore, the discussion emphasizes integrating evidence from different imaging modalities and hemodynamic assessments. The second component of the review discusses how RV dysfunction affects therapeutic options, including medical, transcatheter, and surgical therapies for VHD. The focus of the discussion is on the interplay between RV dysfunction in patients with right-side VHD, namely tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Unlike left-side VHD, where RV dysfunction is a marker of overall disease severity but does not necessarily indicate futility or nonresponse to therapy, right-side VHD and TR-associated RV dysfunction identifies a subset of patients where intervention may precipitate even worse RV function. The nuances of these interactions between ventricular and valvular function are the emphasis of this section, and we aim to provide a framework for understanding RV function in the context of these different forms of VHD. Finally, the review concludes with an eye to the future, discussing the ways in which RV dysfunction can be identified and managed with the use of novel techniques. This discussion is increasingly relevant as RV dysfunction and VHD frequently coexist, and accurate identification is critical to matching the right treatment for the right patient.

recs.title: Associations of Cumulative Wrist Accelerometer-Derived Physical Activity and Proxies of Sedentary Behavior With Early Cardiac Remodeling in Healthy Adolescents.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior are associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in adults, but evidence in adolescence remains limited. This study examined associations of cumulative accelerometer-derived physical activity and proxies of sedentary behavior during adolescence with early subclinical cardiac features assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance. METHODS: A total of 111 adolescents (55.9% girls) wore a wrist-worn triaxial accelerometer at ages 12, 14, and 16 years to measure physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies. A 3-Tesla cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan was performed at final follow-up to assess cardiac structure and function. Multivariable linear regression models examined associations between cumulative physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies and cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived metrics. RESULTS: Daily step counts were positively associated with indexed end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes of the left ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.90 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.42-1.37]; 0.36 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.10-0.63], respectively) and the right ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 1.03 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.44-1.61]; 0.44 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.05-0.82], respectively), and with reduced right ventricular longitudinal strain (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.53% [95% CI, 0.16-0.91]). Greater time spent in sedentary bouts and a higher number of sedentary bouts were associated with increased left atrial active emptying fraction (adjusted β per 100 min/d, 8.21% [95% CI, 0.09-16.34]; adjusted β per 1 bout/d, 1.76% [95% CI, 0.17-3.35], respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior proxies during adolescence were independently associated with early markers of ventricular and atrial remodeling. These findings highlight early cardiac adaptations related to lifestyle behaviors and underscore the importance of promoting active lifestyles from a young age.

recs.title: Longitudinal Inflammatory Trajectories and Recurrent Vascular Events After Acute Ischemic Stroke.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammation contributes to the pathophysiology of acute ischemic stroke, yet no inflammatory biomarker has been established as a standard prognostic tool. Most prior studies have relied on single baseline measurements, and the prognostic relevance of longitudinal inflammatory changes remains uncertain. We investigated whether baseline levels and longitudinal trajectories of inflammatory burden index (IBI) and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) are associated with recurrent stroke and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 374 patients with acute ischemic stroke were analyzed. IBI was calculated as hs-CRP multiplied by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Serum hs-CRP and leukocyte differentials were measured within 24 hours of admission and at 6 months (±3 months). Baseline hs-CRP was dichotomized at 2 mg/L and IBI at the median baseline value (4.03 mg/L), and longitudinal trajectories were defined as persistent low, increased, decreased, or persistent high based on changes between baseline and follow-up measurements. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 30.5 months, 58 patients (15.5%) experienced recurrent stroke and 69 (18.4%) experienced MACE. Baseline IBI and hs-CRP showed inconsistent associations with these outcomes. In contrast, persistent high IBI was associated with increased risks of recurrent stroke (hazard ratio [HR] 2.46; 95% CI, 1.26-4.78; P=0.008) and MACE (HR 2.42; 95% CI, 1.33-4.43; P=0.004) compared with persistent low IBI. Persistent high hs-CRP was associated with MACE (HR 1.92; 95% CI, 1.08-3.41; P=0.026) but not with recurrent stroke. CONCLUSIONS: Persistent high IBI trajectories were independently associated with recurrent stroke and MACE, and persistent high hs-CRP trajectories were associated with MACE. Longitudinal assessment of inflammatory biomarkers may provide prognostic information beyond a single baseline measurement after ischemic stroke.

recs.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

recs.title: Patients with ischemic stroke despite anticoagulation: outcomes after left atrial appendage occlusion in a high-risk cohort.
Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Atrial Fibrillation Patients With High Risk of Stroke and Bleeding: An Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is increasingly used as an alternative to oral anticoagulation for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. Its comparative effectiveness and safety in patients at a high risk of both stroke and bleeding remain uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the efficacy and safety of LAAC vs contemporary medical therapy in a high-risk population using individual participant data from randomized trials. METHODS: Bibliographic databases and trial registries through August 5, 2026, were searched for randomized trials comparing percutaneous LAAC with contemporary medical therapy in populations with a trial-level mean CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥4. A 1-stage common-effect analysis used Cox models stratified by trial and adjusted for age, sex, CHA2DS2-VASc score, and HAS-BLED score. Both primary outcomes were time to first stroke, systemic embolism, or cardiovascular/unknown death (efficacy) and time to first major bleeding (safety). A flexible time-varying Cox model was used for major bleeding. The protocol was submitted to PROSPERO (CRD420261335972). RESULTS: CLOSURE-AF (Left Atrial Appendage CLOSURE in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Compared to Medical Therapy) and PRAGUE-17 (Left Atrial Appendage Closure vs. Novel Anticoagulation Agents in Atrial Fibrillation) contributed 1,290 participants (647 assigned to LAAC and 643 to control). Median age was 77.3 years (Q1-Q3: 71.4-81.9 years), and 809 participants (62.7%) were men. The primary efficacy outcome occurred in 142 LAAC participants (21.9%) and 133 control subjects (20.7%) (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.77-1.24; P = 0.842). Major bleeding occurred in 86 LAAC participants (13.3%) and 80 control subjects (12.4%) (adjusted HR: 1.03; 95% CI: 0.75-1.39; P = 0.874). The treatment effect on major bleeding varied over time (P for treatment-by-time interaction < 0.001), with a cumulative major bleeding incidence of 9.4% with LAAC vs 6.0% with control (absolute risk difference, 3.4 percentage points; 95% CI: 0.4-6.3 percentage points) at 1 year and 13.2% vs 12.1% (absolute risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI: -2.8 to 5.0 percentage points) at 3 years. CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation, no statistically significant difference was detected between LAAC and contemporary medical therapy for the primary efficacy outcome or major bleeding. The major bleeding hazard varied over time, with higher early and lower later conditional hazard estimates; however, a cumulative bleeding benefit was not demonstrated by 3 years. Long-term randomized data are needed to improve the precision of later treatment-effect estimates.

recs.title: A regenerative pulse for the injured heart.
Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear. METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. RESULTS: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

recs.title: Aortic Valve Replacement for Aortic Regurgitation: A Call for Action?
Distinct Gut Microbial and Metabolic Biomarkers Related to Atrial Fibrillation in Low-Risk Patients.
Prospective in silico prediction of the Lp(a)HORIZON trial outcome prior to topline result announcement.
Assessment of Coronary Inflammatory Risk From Noncontrast Cardiac Computed Tomography.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Individuals with low or minimal coronary artery calcification (CAC) are considered at low cardiovascular risk, but a substantial absolute number of cardiovascular events occur in this population; assessment of coronary inflammation using the fat attenuation index (FAI) score may identify residual inflammatory risk beyond CAC score. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether coronary inflammation measured on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) or noncontrast cardiac CT (NCCT) identifies individuals at high cardiovascular risk independent of CAC burden. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this cohort study, a novel artificial intelligence algorithm for measuring FAI score on NCCT was trained and tested in an independent, multicenter, longitudinal cohort of consecutive individuals undergoing clinically indicated CCTA and NCCT for CAC score between 2010 and 2021, with median (IQR) follow-up of 6.7 (4.6-10.0) years. Data were analyzed from January 2010 to March 2024. EXPOSURE: Agatston CAC score and coronary inflammation from both CCTA (CCTA FAI score, established biomarker) and NCCT (NC FAI score, novel biomarker). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was cardiovascular (CV) mortality; the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising myocardial infarction, new-onset heart failure, or CV death. RESULTS: The derivation cohort included 6818 individuals (median [IQR] age, 61 [51-71] years; 3543 female participants [52.0%]), and the external validation clinical outcomes cohort included 19 110 individuals (median [IQR] age, 56.0 [48.0-64.0] years; 9289 female participants [48.6%]). During follow-up, 536 CV deaths and 1727 MACE occurred. FAI scores independently stratified CV mortality risk across CAC score categories, with the strongest associations among individuals with CAC score of 0. Adding CCTA FAI score or NC FAI score to CAC score significantly improved risk discrimination (area under the curve increased from 0.76 to 0.81 and 0.80, respectively; P < .001), reclassification (net reclassification index), and net benefit across all risk thresholds. Among 89 CV deaths in individuals with CAC score of 0 and 138 CV deaths with CAC score of 1 through 99, 44.9% and 44.2% had NC FAI score above the 75th percentile, respectively. Among individuals with CAC score of 0, CV mortality rates increased from 1.4 to 4.0 per 1000 person-years for those with NC FAI score above the 75th percentile, and MACE rates increased from 5.9 to 13.3 per 1000 person-years. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Per the results of this cohort study, NC FAI score provides prognostic performance comparable to CCTA FAI score and improves cardiovascular risk prediction and reclassification beyond CAC score. Elevated FAI score, derived from either CCTA or NCCT, should be interpreted as a risk-enhancing factor that may prompt intensification of established, evidence-based preventive measures and may serve as a potential future gatekeeper for the use of targeted anti-inflammatory treatments.

recs.title: Side Effects of Low-Dose Colchicine in Chronic Coronary Disease: A Post Hoc Analysis of the LoDoCo2 Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-dose colchicine reduces cardiovascular events in patients with chronic coronary disease. However, side effects may compromise compliance and lead to discontinuation of treatment. Therefore, we aimed to assess the incidence of side effects leading to discontinuation of treatment in the LoDoCo2 (Low-Dose Colchicine 2) trial. METHODS: The LoDoCo2 trial was a randomized controlled trial evaluating colchicine versus placebo in patients with chronic coronary disease. Participants entered a 30-day open-label run-in phase during which all participants received colchicine 0.5 mg once daily, followed by randomization to colchicine or placebo. Tolerability-related side effects leading to treatment discontinuation were evaluated at the end of the 30-day run-in phase and during the randomized phase (median follow-up, 29.5 [interquartile range, 21.6-47.4] months). Cumulative incidence of side effects was presented using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared by treatment arm using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: During the 30-day run-in phase, 618 of 6519 (9.5%) participants reported side effects. Women had a higher risk of side effects than men during the 30-day run-in phase (odds ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.23-1.89]). After randomization, 114 participants (4.2%) in the colchicine group and 120 (4.4%) in the placebo group discontinued treatment due to side effects (hazard ratio [HR], 0.95 [95% CI, 0.73-1.22]). Gastrointestinal symptoms were most common (colchicine 2.0% versus placebo 1.7%) followed by myalgia (colchicine 1.2% versus placebo 1.6%). No differences in the risk of side effects between colchicine and placebo were seen for any of the subgroups. Women did have a higher risk of reporting side effects compared with men, regardless of assigned treatment (HR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.22-2.25]). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with chronic coronary disease that tolerated initial treatment with low-dose colchicine, long-term discontinuation due to side effects was uncommon and did not differ between colchicine and placebo. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org/au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12614000093684.

recs.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in the United States, 2016-2025: Utilization, Patient Selection, and Acute Outcomes.
The lymphatic system: the new target for effective decongestion in decompensated heart failure?
The Perth Declaration to eliminate rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease.
Reply: Coronary Anatomy, Arrhythmic Substrate, and Sudden Cardiac Death.
Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty: 5-Year Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty places a circumferential tensioning loop around the base of the left ventricle to reduce mitral annular dimensions and reshape ventricular geometry in patients with functional mitral regurgitation and heart failure. Early experience demonstrated reductions in mitral regurgitation and improvements in heart failure symptoms. METHODS: The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Division of Intramural Research Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty Early Feasibility Study was an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter study. Between 1 and 5 years, vital status, serious adverse events, routine clinical documentation, and site-reported transthoracic echocardiography findings were collected. RESULTS: Nineteen procedures were attempted in 18 participants (63% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, 37% heart failure with preserved ejection fraction). Median age was 73 years, and 63% were female. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 57%. One participant underwent left ventricular assist device implantation after 2 years, and 1 participant underwent mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair after 3 years; none underwent heart transplantation. The study was suspended after complete heart block developed in 6 participants, including 4 requiring new cardiac implantable electronic devices. Among participants with available follow-up echocardiography, site-reported imaging demonstrated mitral regurgitation reduction and improved left ventricular ejection fraction through 5 years. Symptomatic improvement was most apparent during the first year and attenuated thereafter. CONCLUSIONS: Cerclage ventriculoplasty was associated with mitral regurgitation reduction and improved ventricular function among participants with available long-term follow-up. Symptomatic benefit was greatest during the first year and diminished thereafter, suggesting that favorable remodeling may not fully offset progression of the underlying cardiomyopathy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03929913.

recs.title: Antenatal inflammation drives postpartum cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
recs.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), including preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, are strongly associated with maternal cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy. We hypothesized that maternal inflammation drives persistent postpartum cardiac maladaptation after HDPs. We conducted a prospective longitudinal study assessing cardiac function and circulating inflammatory profiles during pregnancy and 3-6 months postpartum, complemented by a preclinical mechanistic mouse model recapitulating key antenatal and postpartum immune and cardiac features of HDPs. Here we show that distinct antenatal inflammatory signatures, including elevated chemokines, correlated with adverse left ventricular structure and function 3-6 months postpartum, despite resolution of systemic inflammation. Mechanistically, our preclinical HDP mouse model demonstrates that reduced antenatal progesterone, also observed in patients with HDPs, drives inflammation and postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Antenatal (embryonic day 14.5), but not postpartum (postpartum day 28), progesterone treatment prevented postpartum cardiac dysfunction, identifying both a potential mechanistic and therapeutic strategy to reduce long-term maternal cardiovascular morbidity.

recs.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization. RESULTS: Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. CONCLUSIONS: EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

recs.title: Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The COAST-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) has demonstrated modest success rates. Ablation of atrial low-voltage areas (LVA) has shown potential results, but more data are required. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether PVI plus LVA ablation is superior to PVI alone in reducing atrial arrhythmia recurrence in patients with AF. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Single-blind randomized clinical trial in 14 AF ablation centers in Canada. Adults with persistent AF of more than 3 months were enrolled between August 2018 and September 2024 and followed up for 18 to 36 months through April 2026. INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation or PVI alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond 90 days after a single catheter ablation procedure. Secondary outcomes included repeat ablation for AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia, emergency visits or hospitalization, arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months, procedure duration, total ablation delivery time, AF burden, and safety outcomes. The primary efficacy analysis was based on the modified intention-to-treat principle for patients who received the intervention. RESULTS: Among 508 enrolled patients, 253 were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation and 255 to PVI alone. Mean (SD) age was 65.2 (9.0) years, 386 (76%) were male and 268 (54%) had LVA. After a mean (SD) follow-up of 21 (15) months, 124 (49.4%) randomized to PVI plus LVA and 146 (57.5%) randomized to PVI reached the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 0.82; 95% CI, 0.65-1.04; P = .11). In the prespecified principal subgroup analysis of 268 patients with LVA, arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 68 of 138 patients (49.3%) following PVI plus LVA ablation compared with 90 of 130 patients (69.2%) following PVI alone (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.66-0.91; P = .002). Arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months (37.0% vs 56.2%; HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.92) and AF burden were lower after PVI plus LVA ablation in this group. Among patients without LVA, recurrence was similar between ablation groups (56 of 113 [49.6%] vs 51 of 113 [45.1%]; HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.90-1.32). Procedure duration and ablation delivery time were longer in the PVI plus LVA ablation group. Safety outcomes were similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, among patients with persistent AF, adjunctive LVA ablation did not significantly reduce atrial arrhythmia recurrence in the overall population over a mean 21-month follow-up. A prespecified principal subgroup analysis of patients with LVA suggested that adjunctive LVA ablation was consistent with reduced recurrence of atrial arrhythmias in this group. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT03347227.

The ESC Digital Cardiology and Artificial Intelligence Learning Pathway.
Angio-invasive mucormycosis mimicking an aortic dissection in a patient with chronic febrile aplasia.
Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge. RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6. CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

recs.title: Conduction System Pacing in Pediatric Patients: Outcomes From a Multicenter International Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) may be advantageous in children requiring lifelong ventricular pacing, but long-term durability data are limited. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate the long-term preservation, durability, and safety of CSP in pediatric patients. METHODS: This international, multicenter, retrospective study included consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing at 9 experienced centers. The primary endpoint was long-term preservation of CSP. RESULTS: Among 120 patients (mean age 12.6 ± 3.7 years), 68 (56.7%) had congenital atrioventricular block, 41 (34.2%) had congenital heart disease, and 12 (10.0%) underwent CSP for heart failure/cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Acute CSP implantation, defined as achievement of His bundle pacing, left bundle branch pacing, or left ventricular septal pacing, was successful in 116 patients (96.7%). After a median follow-up of 24 months (Q1-Q3: 10-54 months), electrical lead performance remained stable. Among 101 patients with CSP at implantation and follow-up capture assessment, CSP was preserved in 95 (94.1%). Kaplan-Meier-estimated freedom from loss of CSP was 100.0% at 1 year and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.7%-100.0%) at 2 and 3 years. CSP lead-related complications occurred in 10 patients (8.3%), and reintervention was required in 9 (7.5%). In the CRT subgroup, left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 28.8% ± 9.4% to 46.8% ± 12.0% (P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: CSP is a feasible, safe, and durable physiological pacing strategy in children, with excellent long-term CSP preservation and stable electrical performance despite ongoing somatic growth. CSP may also provide effective physiological resynchronization in pediatric patients requiring CRT.

recs.title: Mavacamten for Refractory Dynamic Intraventricular Obstruction After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Four Novel Monoclonal Antibody PCSK9 Inhibitors: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Lipid and Safety Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Four novel monoclonal antibody proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors-tafolecimab, ongericimab, ebronucimab, and recaticimab-lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in placebo-controlled trials but have never been compared head to head. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to 8 June 2026 and performed a Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials across eight lipid outcomes, analyzed by dose-interval regimen, and adverse events, analyzed by drug (PROSPERO CRD420261422519). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with CINeMA. Lipid effects are placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change from baseline with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). RESULTS: Thirteen trials were included. In the LDL-C network (4,517 patients; 16 regimens), every regimen lowered LDL-C (-45.2% to -80.2%), with concordant reductions in non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and total cholesterol. Most between-agent differences were small, but some indirect contrasts had CrIs excluding zero; most consistently, ongericimab 150 mg every 2 weeks lowered LDL-C more than the three phase 3 recaticimab regimens (differences -14.4% to -18.6%), robust to adjustment for background statin therapy and baseline LDL-C. Rank intervals were wide. The largest triglyceride and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol effects of recaticimab were confined to small phase 1b/2 regimens. No agent differed from placebo for any adverse event or serious adverse events, although information was limited; injection-site reactions were more frequent with active treatment. Certainty of evidence was moderate to very low versus placebo and very low between agents. CONCLUSIONS: All four antibodies produced substantial reductions in atherogenic lipids without a detected safety signal beyond injection-site reactions. Indirect between-agent differences are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a hierarchy; head-to-head and cardiovascular outcome trials are needed.

recs.title: HuR Inhibition Attenuates Hypertension and Fibrosis in Chronic Kidney Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Upregulation of the RNA-binding protein HuR (human antigen R) has been reported in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but its pathogenic role remains incompletely understood. We hypothesized that HuR promotes renal and vascular injury in hypertensive CKD and that pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates disease progression. We therefore investigated the role of HuR in deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) plus Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced CKD and evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of the HuR inhibitor, KH3 . METHODS: Male mice underwent uninephrectomy followed by DOCA+Ang II infusion with 1% NaCl in drinking water and were treated with KH3 or vehicle for 3 weeks. Control mice received saline without DOCA or Ang II. RESULTS: DOCA+Ang II markedly increased HuR expression in circulating exosomes and kidney tissues, which was attenuated by KH3 treatment. KH3 reduced albuminuria, improved renal function, and attenuated kidney hypertrophy, glomerular, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis. These renoprotective effects were associated with reduced podocyte and tubular injury, decreased macrophage infiltration, and suppression of NF-κB (nuclear factor-kappa B) p65, Nox2 (NADPH oxidase 2), AKT (protein kinase B) phosphorylation, TGFβ1 (transforming growth factor β1), and Wisp1 (WNT1-inducible signaling pathway protein 1) signaling. KH3 also partially lowered arterial blood pressure in DOCA+Ang II-treated mice. Further studies in vascular smooth muscle cells and mesenteric resistance arteries suggested that HuR inhibition may suppress vascular profibrotic signaling associated with SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2). CONCLUSIONS: HuR is upregulated in renal and vascular tissues in DOCA+Ang II-induced CKD and contributes to renal inflammation, oxidative stress, fibrosis, and vascular dysfunction. Pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates renal and vascular injury, supporting HuR as a promising therapeutic target for CKD.

recs.title: Is local coronary inflammation truly superior after PCI, or is the comparison driven by revascularization endpoints?
Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial.
recs.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve symptoms in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We recently demonstrated that semaglutide reduces exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) in obesity-related HFpEF, but potential effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function that may underlie these hemodynamic improvements remain unclear. In this prespecified cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy of the randomized CAMEO-SEMA trial, 49 participants (33 semaglutide, 16 placebo, 28 female) underwent CMR at baseline and 52 weeks, within 1 day of invasive exercise hemodynamic assessment. The prespecified primary CMR endpoint was change in left atrial (LA) reservoir strain; other prespecified CMR endpoints included LV filling dynamics, which were assessed by early filling rate indexed to end-diastolic volume (eFR/EDV). Compared with placebo, semaglutide improved LA reservoir strain (+5.7% [95% CI, +0.3 to +9.7]; P=0.037) and eFR/EDV (+0.64 s-1 [95% CI, +0.42 to +1.00]; P<0.0001). Improvements in LA reservoir strain and LV filling dynamics were associated with reductions in exercise PAWP (r=-0.46, P<0.001 and r=-0.65, P<0.0001, respectively). With respect to other prespecified CMR endpoints, semaglutide reduced LV mass, restored more physiologic LV geometry, and improved right ventricular function and biventricular myocardial mechanics. The results of this CMR substudy indicate that in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, semaglutide improves LA function and LV diastolic filling dynamics, identifying improvements in myocardial function that may contribute to semaglutide's improvement of hemodynamics. ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05371496.

recs.title: Beyond Coronary Artery Disease: Etiologies and Outcomes of the Shark-Fin ECG Pattern: A Systematic Review.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The shark-fin sign (SFS) is a rare, high-risk electrocardiographic pattern reported in commonly linked with obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). OBJECTIVE: To characterize the electrocardiographic patterns, etiologies, and clinical outcomes associated with the SFS. METHODS: We systematically reviewed PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane from inception through May 20, 2026, including all studies with participant-level data. RESULTS: Eighty-five papers involving 104 patients were included; 66.3% had non-obstructive etiologies. The obstructive CAD patients were predominantly male (97.1%), while other etiologies were predominantly female (60.8%). Among CAD cases, the left main coronary artery (LMCA)/proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) was the culprit in 75.0%, and SFS localization matched coronary anatomy in 91.4%. VT/VF and death each occurred in 37.1%, with adverse outcomes confined to those with LMCA/LAD lesions. Among other etiologies, Takotsubo syndrome (TTS, 31.7%), vasospasm (14.4%), myocarditis (6.7 %) and neurologic emergencies (4.8%) were the most frequently reported. VT/VF occurred in 43.4% and 27.5% died. Among patients with TTS, 63.6% experienced VT/VF or death, compared with ventricular arrhythmias in 66% of patients with vasospasm. CONCLUSION: SFS is a high-risk ECG pattern rather than a diagnosis and warrants urgent etiologic evaluation and cardiac monitoring. Most published data are derived from patients without established CAD. LMCA/LAD disease, TTS, and coronary vasospasm were associated with particularly high-risk hospitalizations. Primary non-cardiac causes should also be considered when clinically suspected.

recs.title: Association of Left Ventricular Epicardial Adipose Tissue and Lipomatous Metaplasia With Ventricular Tachycardia Circuitry and Recurrence Following Ablation in Patients With Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) have complex intramural ventricular tachycardia (VT) circuitry and relatively high postablation recurrences. OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the association of left ventricular epicardial adipose tissue (LV EAT) and lipomatous metaplasia (LM) with critical VT circuitry and postablation VT recurrence in patients with NICM. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we quantified LV EAT and LM via cardiac contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) in a cohort of consecutive patients with NICM before VT ablation. CECT image registration with VT critical sites in electroanatomic mapping was performed in a subset. Mixed-effects and subdistribution proportional hazard models were used to examine the association of image features with VT circuitry elements and outcomes, respectively. RESULTS: In 48 patients with coregistered CECT-electroanatomic mapping, segmental maximal EAT thickness was associated with critical VT sites (OR: 1.36 per mm increase; P < 0.001), and a threshold of >4.7 mm EAT achieved 72% sensitivity and 71% specificity (OR: 2.15; P = 0.006) for VT site identification. This association remained significant after adjusting for LM, with a significant EAT-LM interaction (P = 0.027). Among all 119 patients, 52 experienced VT recurrence during a median follow-up of 1.7 years (Q1-Q3: 0.7-4.0). Lower LV EAT attenuation was independently associated with time to VT recurrence (subdistribution HR: 1.04 per 1 HU decrease; P = 0.012) after multivariable adjustment including LM and a significant LM interaction (P = 0.020). CONCLUSIONS: LV EAT density and thickness are associated with VT circuitry and postablation recurrence in patients with NICM, and demonstrate a significant statistical interaction with LM.

recs.title: Insurer Coverage of Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Where is the Alignment?
Multiparametric assessment of TNNI3 variant phenotypes in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes correlates with disease severity in patients.
recs.abstract: Routine genetic testing of patients with cardiomyopathy has identified many causative genetic variants. However, in most instances, the impact of these variants on physiological function and clinical outcomes remains unclear. Here we develop a high-throughput human induced pluripotent stem-cell-based platform to measure the effects of variants in cardiac troponin I (encoded by TNNI3) on systolic and diastolic force generation and calcium handling. By integrating contractility and calcium signaling, we accurately distinguish pathogenic from nonpathogenic TNNI3 variants and characterize the pathogenic effects of variants of uncertain significance. Further, by evaluating the clinical presentations of patients with TNNI3 cardiomyopathy from a single site, we demonstrate that diastolic function in vitro correlates with age at onset (R2 = 0.6), a measure of disease severity. The ability to comprehensively characterize in vitro variant effects that correlate with clinical outcomes should help identify mechanisms underlying variable disease severity and enhance the discovery of class-targeted treatments.

Preprocedural transesophageal echocardiography before cardioversion in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-associated atrial fibrillation and thromboembolic risk.
Extravascular Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension: First-in-Human Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Catheter-based intravascular renal denervation produces modest, variable blood pressure reductions, partly because renal sympathetic nerves lie at variable depths within the periarterial adventitia and because accessory or early branching arteries are inaccessible to intraluminal catheters. We developed an extravascular renal denervation system (HyperQure) delivering circumferential radiofrequency energy from outside the artery and assessed its safety and efficacy. Here, we report the primary 3-month outcomes. METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, single-arm, first-in-human pilot trial enrolled 10 patients with resistant hypertension (office blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg and daytime ambulatory systolic blood pressure [SBP] ≥135 mm Hg despite ≥3 antihypertensive agents) across 7 Korean centers. All underwent bilateral extravascular renal denervation on stable antihypertensive regimens. The primary end point was 3-month change in 24-hour ambulatory SBP; safety outcomes were assessed through 3 months. RESULTS: All 10 patients (median age, 52.5 years; 7 men) completed follow-up. Seven patients (70%) had accessory or early branching arteries <3 mm typically ineligible for intravascular renal denervation; all were successfully ablated. Median 24-hour ambulatory SBP decreased by 25.0 mm Hg (P=0.008) and median office SBP by 39.5 mm Hg (P=0.002). Seven of 10 (70%) achieved office SBP <140 mm Hg despite a reduction in median antihypertensive burden from 6.0 to 4.5 agents. No major or procedure-related adverse events occurred; follow-up computed tomography angiography showed no vascular complications and renal function was preserved. CONCLUSIONS: Extravascular renal denervation using the HyperQure renal denervation System warrants evaluation in a larger controlled trial, particularly in patients with complex renal arterial anatomy.

recs.title: Ventricular arrhythmia-heart failure interaction and mortality in ICD recipients after myocardial infarction.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Ventricular arrhythmia (VA) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist in patients with ischaemic left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Whether VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated remains unclear. We investigated their bidirectional relationship and associations with mortality. METHODS: We analysed 1014 patients from the multicentre WICD-MI study. All received a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator after acute myocardial infarction (MI) and subsequently underwent implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation, with persistent LV ejection fraction ≤35%. Associations between ICD-treated VA, HF-events (HF hospitalization, heart transplantation, or LV assist device implantation), and all-cause mortality were assessed using time-dependent Cox models. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 2.6 years post-ICD implantation, VA was independently associated with an increased risk of HF events [aHR = 3.50 (1.66-7.38), P = .001], while HF events similarly preceded subsequent VA [aHR = 2.96 (1.59-5.50), P = .0008]. Both were independently associated with all-cause mortality, with a numerically higher aHR for HF events [aHR = 7.96 (4.71-13.47), P < .0001] than for VA [aHR = 4.43 (2.35-8.36), P < .0001]. Sensitivity analyses suggested that the VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. In exploratory analyses, VA was strongly associated with subsequent HF events in subcutaneous ICD recipients [aHR = 15.08 (4.62-49.22), P < .0001] but not in transvenous ICD recipients (P for interaction = .0002). CONCLUSION: In ICD recipients with persistent LV dysfunction following MI, VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated and independently associated with mortality. The VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. These findings highlight the potential value of integrated HF and VA management.

recs.title: Emergency Action Plans in Aquatic Sports: A Call to Action and Guide for Aquatic Leadership.
recs.abstract: With increasing participation in aquatics athletics at the youth, amateur, and professional levels, it is critical to provide sport and venue-specific emergency action plans (EAP) to ensure safe participation for athletes with and without cardiovascular disease. Current EAPs are typically geared toward land-based sports and do not address major aquatic-specific obstacles including identification of emergency, extraction, automated external defibrillator availability, emergency medical services access, and transport to hospital. This document provides guidance on creating EAP for aquatic athletes based on sport type and venue (pool-based, open-water immersion, and open-water adjacent) with guidance and proposed solutions for each. It also highlights the growing need for detailed aquatic EAPs to ensure safe athlete participation for water-based athletes. Finally, we call upon leaders in aquatic sports to involve all stakeholders and consider implementing more structured training in addition to basic life support, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and first-aid to maximize aquatic athlete safety.

recs.title: Clonal haematopoiesis across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic continuum: from risk marker to therapeutic target.
Family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding care in familial hypercholesterolaemia (Taking ACTion to Improve Care of coupleS in FH (TACTICS)): a mixed methods study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a common genetic condition causing premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding are important phases of care. We investigated awareness, knowledge and practices regarding these phases among individuals with FH, partners, and healthcare professionals (HCPs). METHODS: An exploratory mixed-methods study was conducted in the Netherlands, Norway and Australia. Interviews with individuals with heterozygous FH (HeFH) explored experiences of care related to family planning and were analysed following reflexive thematic analysis. Partners completed an anonymous survey on the impact of FH on their relationship. HCPs were surveyed on family planning and pregnancy practices. RESULTS: Twenty-six individuals with HeFH (62% women, median age 37 [IQR 33-42] years, 15% ASCVD) were interviewed. Experiences varied widely, with women reporting the greatest impact, particularly concerning pregnancy, breastfeeding and treatment interruption. Among 175 partners of subjects with FH (55% men, median age 48 [37-60] years, 82% with children), 25% reported a past and/or current negative impact of FH on their relationship. FH influenced family planning in 11% of couples, with a higher proportion among those aged 30-39 years (35%). 107 HCPs (median practice duration 21 [12-30] years, median FH-caseload 50 [15-128]) completed the survey. Most (89%) discussed family planning, mainly concerning inheritance (94%) and preconception medication advice (91%). Most HCPs recommended statin discontinuation during conception, pregnancy and breastfeeding; 46% recommended breastfeeding duration similar to that for general population. CONCLUSIONS: Substantial heterogeneity exists in counselling practices, highlighting the need for standardised care pathways to improve guidance and support individuals with FH and their partners in family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding.

recs.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure for Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation: Where Does It Fit?
Anemia and Iron Deficiency Across Renal Function in Hospitalized Heart Failure: Insights From OPPORTUNITIES Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for heart failure (HHF). Their prognostic contributions in the acute setting, particularly across kidney function, remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: We investigated the association of anemia, transferrin saturation (TSAT), and ID according to kidney function, with postdischarge outcomes in HHF patients. METHODS: Consecutive HHF patients enrolled in the OPPORTUNITIES registry with available hemoglobin and TSAT at discharge. The primary endpoint was HF-free survival, a composite of all-cause death, urgent heart transplantation, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and urgent emergency department referral for HF worsening at 12 months. Adjusted Cox regression models were applied. RESULTS: A total of 454 HHF patients were included. The median age was 77 (69-83); 37.9% were women, and 55% of patients were anemic. Anemic patients were older and exhibited a greater burden of comorbidities. Hemoglobin and TSAT showed a modest positive correlation overall (rho = 0.276, P < 0.001), which disappeared in patients with estimated glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Lower hemoglobin was independently associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.75-0.91; P < 0.001), whereas TSAT was not independently predictive. A significant interaction between hemoglobin and renal function was observed (P = 0.025), indicating that the hemoglobin effect varied according to kidney function. Among ID definitions, only TSAT <20% independently identified patients at an increased risk (HR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.03-2.03; P = 0.035). CONCLUSIONS: In HHF patients, the prognostic relevance of anemia varies according to renal function. TSAT <20% was the only ID definition independently associated with adverse outcomes.

recs.title: Trial Registration in an Era of Rapidly Evolving Technology.
Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS. METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor. INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS. FUNDING: Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

Safety and Efficacy of Transvenous Lead Extraction Using a Right-Sided Approach.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite extensive experience with transvenous lead extraction (TLE) overall, outcomes for systems implanted on the right chest remain underexplored, largely because of their low incidence. OBJECTIVES: The objective was to evaluate whether system laterality influences TLE outcomes. METHODS: Using our institutional, prospectively maintained ExTRACT registry, we analyzed all consecutive patients undergoing TLE procedures at the Cleveland Clinic between 1996 and 2022. Patients were categorized by system laterality. Baseline characteristics, procedural characteristics, and complications were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between right-sided TLE and adverse events. RESULTS: Among 4,989 patients, 494 (9.9%) had right-sided and 4,495 (90.1%) had left-sided TLE. Compared with left-sided cases, right-sided cases had longer total lead dwell times (13.83 vs 9.26 years, P < 0.001) and were more likely to be extracted because of infection (47.57% vs 39.71%, P = 0.001). Fluoroscopy time was longer (15.95 vs 12.1 minutes; P < 0.001), and femoral workstation use more frequent (7.89% vs 4.05%, P < 0.001), yet complete extraction was lower (94.53% vs 96.44%, P = 0.034). Right-sided TLE had higher rates of sternotomy (2.83% vs 1.25%, P = 0.004) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (2.49% vs 1.10%, P = 0.009). Thirty-day mortality was low and comparable (0.61% vs 0.47%, P = 0.727). Multivariable regression showed that right-sided TLE was associated with higher odds of sternotomy (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.01-3.46, P = 0.037) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.01-3.78, P = 0.037). CONCLUSIONS: Right-sided TLE is associated with a lower rate of complete extraction and increased procedural risk, particularly sternotomy and major vascular injury, compared with left-sided TLE. These findings should be carefully weighed when implanting or extracting right-sided systems.
