Orforglipron for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Results From 2 Randomized Clinical Trials (ATTAIN-OSA).
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common disorder characterized by repeated upper airway collapse during sleep that is associated with reduced quality of life and increased incidence of cardiometabolic disease. OBJECTIVE: To assess the effects of orforglipron on moderate to severe OSA in adults with obesity or overweight, compared with placebo. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Two 52-week, phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials were conducted at 66 sites in the US, Argentina, Brazil, China, Czech Republic, Germany, Japan, Mexico, and Taiwan. Adults with moderate to severe OSA and body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) of 27 or higher were enrolled between November 11, 2024, and July 23, 2025. Final follow-up occurred on July 30, 2026. Trial 1 included patients not receiving positive airway pressure treatment and trial 2 included patients receiving positive airway pressure treatment. INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either once-daily orforglipron (maximum tolerated dose: equivalent to 9-, 14.5-, or 17.2-mg tablet dose) or placebo. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, events/h) from baseline to week 52. Seven key multiplicity-controlled secondary end points included change in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Short Form Sleep-Related Impairment T-score, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein. RESULTS: A total of 363 patients were randomized in trial 1 (mean age, 48.4 years; BMI, 37.4; AHI, 50.7 events/h; 31.4% female) and 349 patients were randomized in trial 2 (mean age, 51.1 years; BMI, 38.6; AHI, 57.6 events/h; 26.9% female). For the treatment regimen estimand, in trial 1, the mean AHI change was -17.8 for orforglipron compared with -4.5 for placebo (difference, -13.2 [95% CI, -17.7 to -8.7]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. In trial 2, the mean AHI change was -17.3 for orforglipron and -5.3 for placebo (difference, -12.0 [95% CI, -17.1 to -6.9]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. Of 7 key secondary end points, 6 were statistically significant, favoring orforglipron. Gastrointestinal events were the most commonly reported adverse events, occurring in 123 (68.0%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 68 (37.4%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 1 and in 125 (70.6%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 63 (36.6%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 2. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: These results provide evidence for the potential use of oral orforglipron to improve sleep-disordered breathing in adults with moderate to severe OSA and obesity or overweight. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06649045.

recs.title: Generation of Human Cardiomyocytes With Adult-Like Metabolism by a Chemically Defined Medium for Mitochondrial Disease Modeling.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC cardiomyocytes) as a model for cardiac disease have become increasingly important, bolstered by the Food and Drug Administration's initiative to promote novel alternative methods for biomedical research. A key limitation of metabolically immature iPSC cardiomyocytes is their limited ability to accurately recapitulate mitochondria-dependent pathologies, such as Friedreich ataxia-associated cardiomyopathy. Adult cardiomyocytes are characterized by a high density of interfibrillar mitochondria, abundant respiratory complexes (I-V) that form supercomplexes, and efficient utilization of fatty acids to drive mitochondrial respiration. These unique metabolic structures and functions are largely missing in iPSC cardiomyocytes. Further, whether iPSC cardiomyocytes can efficiently utilize fatty acids for respiration in the presence of glucose, a unique adult feature, remains unclear. METHODS: We developed a chemically defined, 11-component maturation medium (MM11) designed using a bioinformatics-guided strategy that identified high-fidelity transcriptional markers of adult cardiac metabolic maturity. Human iPSC cardiomyocytes were treated with MM11 for 2 weeks and evaluated at the molecular, structural, and functional levels, with an emphasis on mitochondrial maturity. We benchmarked our results with isolated primary adult human cardiomyocytes. Last, we tested whether this method could enable us to more accurately model Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy. RESULTS: MM11 treatment increased expression of metabolic pathways, including mitochondrial respiration and fatty acid metabolism, at the transcript and protein levels. Ultrastructural analyses revealed the formation of interfibrillar mitochondria and mitochondrial respiratory supercomplexes, a feature never shown in previous reports. Functionally, MM11-treated iPSC cardiomyocytes exhibited substantially increased oxidative phosphorylation and a metabolic preference for fatty acid utilization in the presence of physiologic substrates, as determined by oxygen consumption assays and 13C isotope tracing. CONCLUSIONS: MM11 promotes robust metabolic maturation of human iPSC cardiomyocytes, enabling sophisticated mitochondrial architecture and substrate utilization. These metabolically matured cardiomyocytes more faithfully model mitochondria-dependent cardiac pathologies, including ischemia-reperfusion injury and Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy, improving the use of iPSC cardiomyocytes for mechanistic studies of human heart disease.

recs.title: Cardiovascular risk, evaluation and management in patients with hypertriglyceridaemia: a Consensus Statement from the International Atherosclerosis Society.
recs.abstract: The prevalence of hypertriglyceridaemia is increasing globally owing to high rates of obesity and diabetes mellitus. Hypertriglyceridaemia is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, mediated through the cholesterol content of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnant particles rather than through triglycerides per se. Although plasma levels of triglycerides can be measured with a simple blood test, hypertriglyceridaemia remains underdiagnosed and undertreated. Hypertriglyceridaemia can result from various primary or secondary aetiologies, the identification and management of which is an important first step. Hypertriglyceridaemia can be managed with lifestyle measures, lipid-lowering therapy with statins in indicated patients to reduce cholesterol levels and, in refractory situations, with the addition of triglyceride-specific pharmacological therapies. Emerging therapies with considerable promise for the management of hypertriglyceridaemia include those targeting apolipoprotein C-III, angiopoietin-related protein 3 or fibroblast growth factor 21. However, so far, there is no evidence from randomized clinical trials that pharmacotherapies targeting triglycerides can reduce the occurrence of cardiovascular events, suggesting that elevated levels of triglycerides serve as a marker of atherosclerotic risk that should prompt optimization of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. In this Consensus Statement, we provide clinical context and evidence for the evaluation, diagnosis and management of hypertriglyceridaemia.

recs.title: Therapeutically Targetable Th17-Derived miR-721 Drives Autoimmune Myocarditis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocarditis is an inflammatory cardiac disease in which T helper 17 (Th17) cell-driven immune responses contribute to progression toward dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Current therapies mainly rely on corticosteroids but lack specificity, while the role of miR-721, synthesized by Th17 cells, remains largely unexplored in disease pathogenesis. METHODS: We characterized the presence of mmu-miR-721 and its human homolog hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 in extracellular vesicles secreted by Th17 cells from IL-17 (interleukin-17) eGFP mice with experimental autoimmune myocarditis and from patients with myocarditis. MxCre±Ppargfl/fl mice and luciferase reporter assays were used to validate the target genes of miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, respectively. The functional role of miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis was investigated using lentiviral vectors overexpression and miRNA sponge molecules for inhibition. Th17 responses and heart inflammation were assessed, and echocardiography was performed after in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice. RESULTS: Both mmu-miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 were encapsulated in extracellular vesicles and secreted by Th17 cells of mice and patients with myocarditis. Overexpression of mmu-miR-721 in draining lymph node cells from experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice promoted Th17 differentiation via Pparg inhibition and increased RORγt and IL-17 expression. In contrast, no differences in RORγt expression were observed in the absence of Pparg, a target of miR-721, indicating that miR-721 promotes Th17 responses through Pparg repression. In addition, human PPARG was validated as a target gene of hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, as its overexpression in peripheral blood leukocytes downregulated PPARG mRNA levels, suggesting that similar pathways are involved in human pathology. Finally, in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 increased Pparg expression, reducing RORγt and IL-17 activation in T cells, leading to decreased leukocyte infiltration in the heart and improved cardiac function thereby ameliorating disease progression. CONCLUSIONS: miR-721 is released by Th17 cells in extracellular vesicles and promotes Th17 responses during myocarditis through repression of PPARγ, identifying this miRNA as both a mechanistic driver of disease and a potential therapeutic target.

Lipoprotein(a) and the first manifestation of cardiovascular disease: a US national real-world analysis.
Zero radiation is a diagnostic pathway outcome.
Novel Point-of-Care Seismocardiographic Biomarkers for Discrimination of Severe Aortic Stenosis from Cardiac Controls.
Beyond anticoagulation: defining the role of left atrial appendage closure in stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.
recs.abstract: Oral anticoagulation has a very strong evidence base for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at elevated thromboembolic risk. Direct oral anticoagulants have improved the safety and convenience of treatment, yet important limitations remain, including residual ischaemic stroke, major bleeding, treatment discontinuation, and patient refusal. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) offers an alternative strategy for selected patients by excluding the principal anatomical source of AF-related cardiac thrombi. However, the appropriate role of LAAC remains controversial, particularly in patients who can and do tolerate anticoagulation. This viewpoint argues for a more individualized approach that distinguishes absolute contraindications from modifiable bleeding risks, treatment refusal or non-persistence, and stroke occurring despite adequate anticoagulation.

recs.title: Metabolic and Renal Dysfunction Are Associated With Intraplaque Lipid Burden Assessed by Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Intravascular Ultrasound: Insights Into the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework emphasizes the interrelated contributions of metabolic and renal dysfunction to cardiovascular risk. Whether these disturbances are reflected in coronary plaque composition remains incompletely understood. We evaluated the association of metabolic and renal dysfunction with intraplaque lipid burden using near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound. METHODS: Intraplaque lipid burden was assessed by the maximum lipid core burden index (LCBI) within a 4-mm segment (maxLCBI4mm), and lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was defined as maxLCBI4mm≥324.7. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed with maxLCBI4mm as the dependent variable, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with LRP. RESULTS: Among 483 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention with pre-intervention near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound imaging, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate and higher hemoglobin A1c were independently associated with greater intraplaque lipid burden and higher odds of LRP. In analyses standardized per 1 SD, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed the strongest association with maxLCBI4mm (β=52.51; 95% CI, 27.49-77.53), followed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (β=33.38; 95% CI, 9.97-56.80) and hemoglobin A1c (β=24.71; 95% CI, 3.71-45.71). Similarly, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (odds tatio [OR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.06-1.75) and higher hemoglobin A1c (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.05-1.77) were independently associated with LRP. No significant interaction between estimated glomerular filtration rate and hemoglobin A1c was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and renal dysfunction are independently associated with intraplaque lipid burden assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound. These findings provide intracoronary imaging evidence linking the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework to plaque-level lipid accumulation.

recs.title: Ultraprocessed Food Consumption and Incident Heart Failure: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with adverse cardiometabolic outcomes and increased atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, the relationship between UPF intake and incident heart failure (HF) remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aims of this study were to examine the relationship between UPF consumption and incident HF and to evaluate potential biological mediators. METHODS: A sample of 6,531 U.S. adults 45-84 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) was analyzed. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations between UPF intake and incident HF. Phenotypes were classified as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction <50%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (ejection fraction ≥50%). Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the potential mediating role of waist-to-height ratio as a surrogate measure for central adiposity. RESULTS: Higher UPF intake was significantly associated with increased risk of incident HF across sequentially adjusted models. In the primary model (model 2), each additional daily serving of UPF was associated with a 5% higher risk of incident HF (HR: 1.052; 95% CI: 1.002-1.103). When stratified by phenotype, UPF intake remained significantly associated with HFpEF (HR: 1.096; 95% CI: 1.016-1.183) but not HFrEF. Participants in the upper 80% of UPF intake had a >2-fold higher risk for HFpEF than those in the lowest 20% (HR: 2.234; 95% CI: 1.289-3.874). In mediation analyses, waist-to-height ratio statistically accounted for ∼51% of the association between UPF intake and total HF and 49% of the association between UPF intake and HFpEF. CONCLUSIONS: Higher UPF consumption was significantly associated with an increased risk for incident HF, with associations driven primarily by the HFpEF phenotype. Central adiposity, measured by waist-to-height ratio, demonstrated a potential mediating role, suggesting that obesity-related cardiometabolic pathways may represent an important pathway linking UPF consumption to HF risk.

recs.title: Association of Site Volume and MitraClip Outcomes in Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: The COAPT PAS Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The number of sites performing transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) has increased. Despite concerns that low-volume sites may have worse outcomes, data are limited on the association between site volume and TEER outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the association between site volume and mitral TEER outcomes in SMR. METHODS: The COAPT PAS (COAPT Post-Approval Study) included patients with SMR who underwent TEER with the MitraClip device from March 2019 to September 2020 following Food and Drug Administration approval. Sites were categorized by number of patients treated: low (≤25), medium (25-50), and high (>50). RESULTS: Of 5,000 patients, 2,632 were from low-, 1,527 from medium-, and 841 from high-volume sites. High-volume sites treated sicker patients with higher Society of Thoracic Surgeons scores and prior heart failure hospitalization rates. Procedures at low-volume sites had similar device implant rates (low: 97%, medium: 99%, high: 98%), used fewer number of clips (low: 1.4 ± 0.6, medium: 1.5 ± 0.6, high: 1.6 ± 0.7 clips, P < 0.001), and had longer device (low: 68 ± 55, medium: 56 ± 53, high: 57 ± 42 min, P < 0.001) and procedure times (low: 153 ± 67, medium: 131 ± 59, high: 128 ± 56 min, P < 0.001). Technical success was comparable (low: 93%, medium: 94%, high: 95%, P = 0.92). MR reduction to ≤2+ and ≤1+ was also similar. There was no difference in heart failure hospitalization (low: 19%, medium: 18%, high: 20%, P = 0.50) or all-cause mortality (low: 23%, medium: 21%, high: 20%, P = 0.27). CONCLUSIONS: Technical success, MR reduction, and 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable across volume strata during the early adoption phase, without significant differences between low- and high-volume centers.

recs.title: Progressive Calcification and Stenosis of a Quadricuspid Aortic Valve.
Practical Management of Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: Evidence, Controversies, and the Boundaries of Guidelines.
recs.abstract: Multivessel coronary artery disease remains one of the most challenging cardiovascular diseases to manage. Selecting the optimal revascularization strategy requires multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion that incorporates coronary anatomy, clinical risk factors, and patient preferences into the decision-making process. Clinical guidelines provide a valuable framework for standardized, evidence-based care with reduced practice variability. However, many landmark trials enrolled highly selected populations and were conducted before the widespread adoption of contemporary revascularization techniques, including physiologic lesion assessment, intracoronary imaging, and modern arterial grafting strategies. Reflecting a collaborative Heart Team perspective, this state-of-the-art review from the American College of Cardiology Interventional Section Leadership Council and Cardiac Surgery Leadership Council summarizes contemporary evidence, reviews areas of ongoing controversy, and provides practical guidance for managing patients with multivessel coronary artery disease in clinical situations that extend beyond the scope of current guideline recommendations.

recs.title: Beyond Chronological Age in PCI Decision-Making.
Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sudden Cardiac Death: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Prevention.
recs.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide. Cardiovascular adverse events have long been the leading cause of death in the MASLD population, far exceeding liver-related mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) represents the most insidious and rapidly progressing extreme clinical phenotype among these cardiovascular complications. However, the relationship between MASLD and SCD has long received insufficient attention. Accumulating evidence from clinical studies indicates that MASLD is associated with elevated sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) risk independent of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors. Notably, while non-invasive clinical proxies of hepatic steatosis (such as the fatty liver index) identify individuals with heightened susceptibility to SCA, advancing liver fibrosis shows the strongest, gradient-dependent association with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, although its relation to SCA or SCD specifically requires confirmation. Sudden death in MASLD may result from primary ventricular arrhythmias or, in advanced cirrhosis, from non-shockable arrest due to hemodynamic, infectious, or metabolic decompensation. Although shared cardiometabolic risk factors account for a substantial portion of this association, proposed mechanisms include insulin resistance-related myocardial energy disturbances, inflammation-associated myocardial and electrophysiological remodeling, cirrhosis-associated circulatory dysfunction, and gut-derived endotoxemia. In clinical practice, non-invasive fibrosis scores, circulating biomarkers, and imaging parameters represent promising candidate risk markers for evaluating electrophysiological vulnerability, though a validated, MASLD-specific SCD risk prediction model remains to be established. Strategies such as lifestyle intervention, metabolic-targeted pharmacotherapy, and intensive management of cardiovascular risk factors may interrupt the progression from MASLD to SCD. This review summarizes the current evidence to inform cardiovascular risk management across the course of MASLD.

NNMT Safeguards Vascular Aging by Modulating an Endothelial LMNA-HSP Stress-Response Axis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: NNMT (nicotinamide N-methyltransferase) is a pivotal metabolic-epigenetic integrator that regulates cellular methylation balance. Although its expression and function exhibit profound, context-dependent heterogeneity in metabolic diseases and cancer, its role within the vascular system, particularly in aging endothelial cells, remains elusive. METHODS: We examined NNMT expression in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, primary mouse aortic endothelial cells, and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Using endothelial-targeted adeno-associated virus-Tie systems, we assessed the effects of NNMT restoration and knockdown on vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice. Mechanistic insights were obtained through exploratory multiomics integration. RESULTS: We established that NNMT expression exhibits an exploratory inverse association in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, a pattern mirrored by declines observed in primary mouse aortic endothelial cells and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Functional assays demonstrated that NNMT restoration improves vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice, whereas knockdown exacerbates these deficits. Mechanistically, exploratory multiomics integration, including Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation and transcriptomic analyses, suggests that NNMT-associated reduction in histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation occupancy at the LMNA (lamin A/C) promoter correlates with its transcriptional maintenance, a process influenced by S-adenosylmethionine supplementation. Downstream, we identified that NNMT-induced LMNA stabilization operates in concert with HSF1 (heat shock transcription factor 1) activation and nuclear translocation, a process accompanied by enhanced binding to HSP90 and HSP70 promoters to drive their transcription. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the vascular protective effects of the natural compound Heterophyllin B are mediated, at least in part, by NNMT, as these benefits were partially attenuated after endothelial NNMT knockdown in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: We identify a protective, age-dependent role for NNMT in vascular endothelium. Our findings reveal that NNMT maintains endothelial homeostasis through coordinated regulation of nuclear LMNA and the downstream HSP (heat shock protein) stress response, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this pathway for addressing age-related endothelial dysfunction.

Renal Insufficiency and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke With Large Infarct: A Prospective Cohort Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate whether renal insufficiency (RI) modifies the effectiveness and safety of endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct in a real-world setting. METHODS: This study was a post hoc analysis of a prospective multicenter cohort study. RI was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate <90 mL/min per 1.73 m2 on admission. Patients were treated with EVT plus standard medical treatment or standard medical treatment alone and were stratified by RI status. The primary effectiveness outcome was favorable outcome (modified Rankin scale 0-3) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and 90-day mortality. RESULTS: Among 745 patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct, 343 (46.0%) had RI and 490 (65.8%) underwent EVT. Compared with standard medical treatment, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes (modified Rankin scale 0-3) in both the RI (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 2.55 [95% CI, 1.15-5.68], P=0.022) and the non-RI group (adjusted OR 2.65 [95% CI, 1.49-4.73], P=0.001). EVT was also associated with higher risks of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage in both groups (P=0.002 and 0.007, respectively), whereas no significant difference in mortality was observed. Results were consistent in the inverse probability-weighted analyses. No statistically significant interaction was observed between RI status and treatment effect for effectiveness or safety outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes but a higher risk of hemorrhagic complications. We did not find statistically significant evidence of interaction between EVT and RI status for 90-day outcomes.

recs.title: Greenspace Exposure Reduces the Risk of Hypertension: A Large Prospective Cohort Study in Northwestern China.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The effects of greenspace on hypertension remain unconfirmed. This study aimed to validate this by performing a large prospective cohort study in China. METHODS: PEAHEN-China (Prospective Environment and Health Epidemiological Study in Northwestern China) recruited 5 484 119 adults in 2017 and followed them to 2021. Blood pressure levels and hypertension were measured and defined using recommended standards. Greenspace exposure was estimated using the normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index. Cox regression models and generalized estimating equation models were used to assess the associations of greenspace with hypertension incidence and blood pressure levels, respectively. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were also performed. RESULTS: During a median 3.21-year follow-up, 1 290 003 new hypertension cases occurred. Living in greener areas was significantly associated with a lower risk of hypertension and lower blood pressure levels. For example, in the adjusted models, compared with the first quartile of normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index within a 500-m buffer, the hazard ratios of incident hypertension in the fourth quartile of the 2 metrics were 0.871 (95% CI, 0.861-0.881) and 0.896 (95% CI, 0.885-0.906). In addition, stronger associations of greenspace exposure with hypertension risk and blood pressure levels were observed in younger, male, rural, and less educated participants than their counterparts. CONCLUSIONS: Our study indicates that neighborhood greenspace may reduce residents' odds of having hypertension, offering robust evidence for developing policies and strategies to mitigate the burden of hypertension.

In an Effort to Reduce Hypertension, Salt Substitutes Come to the Table.

Long-term outcomes of intermuscular versus subcutaneous S-ICD implantation: extended follow-up of a propensity-matched multicentre analysis.
Poorly Controlled Hypertension Alters Coronary Microvascular Contractile Response to Endothelin-1 Before and After Cardiac Surgery.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic hypertension have worse outcomes following on-pump (cardioplegia and cardiopulmonary bypass [CP/CPB]) cardiac surgery. Altered vasomotor function of the coronary microvasculature to ET-1 (endothelin-1) and other agonists may underlie these differences. METHODS: Heart samples were collected from 85 patients undergoing CP/CPB enrolled in this observational study. Ex vivo coronary microvascular responses to ET-1, adenosine diphosphate, and sodium nitroprusside were assessed using video microscopy. Immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and multiomics approaches were also used. RESULTS: Coronary microvascular contractile response to ET-1 in patients with uncontrolled hypertension was increased compared with the other 2 cohorts pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05 across ET-1 10-10 to 10-7 mmol/L). Adenosine diphosphate-induced coronary microvascular vasodilation was conversely decreased (P<0.05 for adenosine diphosphate 10-5 and 10-4 mmol/L). Post-CP/CPB microvascular responses to ET-1 and adenosine diphosphate were blunted overall (P<0.05). Antagonism of pro-vasoconstrictive endothelinA receptor diminished contractile response (P<0.05). Transcriptomics and proteomics showed wide regulation of pro-vasoconstrictive pathways. Regression showed that hypertension status and cardiac mass reliably approximated ET-1-induced coronary microvascular contraction (R2 0.95 pre-CP/CPB, R2 0.86 post-CP/CPB), which, in turn, estimated change in ejection fraction pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05). Patients with uncontrolled hypertension had -11% change in EF when compared with the other 2 groups pooled (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Altered coronary microvascular vasomotor function in patients with uncontrolled hypertension may jeopardize myocardial perfusion. Hypertension status and cardiac mass may be used to prognosticate this physiology, which, in turn, estimates change in ejection fraction postoperatively. Perioperative endothelin receptor blockers may benefit patients with uncontrolled hypertension and thus warrant further investigation.

recs.title: Multivessel Assessment by Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance in Patients With Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in the left anterior descending coronary artery, and it is unclear whether multivessel assessment can improve the diagnostic yield and prognostic value of CMD. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic implications of multivessel CMD assessment using angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD). METHODS: Angio-IMR was measured in all 3 major coronary arteries in 439 patients with NOCAD. Single-vessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in the left anterior descending coronary artery only. Multivessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in all 3 major coronary arteries. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events, comprising a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure. RESULTS: Multivessel assessment identified more patients with CMD than single-vessel assessment (46.7% vs 24.1%; P < 0.001). During a median follow-up period of 4.3 years, an increased number of vessels with CMD was associated with a higher risk for major adverse cardiovascular events after adjustment for diabetes mellitus, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and history of myocardial infarction (adjusted HR: 1.963 per vessel; 95% CI: 1.513-2.548; P < 0.001). Multivessel assessment showed superior prognostic performance compared with single-vessel assessment when added to a clinical risk factor model (area under the curve: 0.751 vs 0.707; P = 0.034). CONCLUSIONS: Multivessel assessment by angio-IMR improved the diagnostic yield of CMD and added incremental prognostic information compared with single-vessel assessment in patients with NOCAD.

recs.title: Mapping and Outcome Implications of Left Atrial Low Voltage Regions as Determined by a Novel 122-electrode Spherical Mapping and Ablation Catheter.
recs.abstract: AIMS: A novel 122-electrode spherical mapping/pulsed field ablation (PFA) device is known to effectively ablate atrial fibrillation (AF). The aim of this study is threshold optimization of LVA for the unique geometry of the Globe electrodes and the prognostic association, to evaluate if the extent of low voltage areas could predict recurrence. METHODS AND RESULTS: The PULSAR study was an IDE trial of 183 patients undergoing first-time paroxysmal AF ablation with one-year outcomes of any atrial arrhythmia. During this study, a subset of patients (n=82) had detailed pre-ablation voltage maps performed with the catheter. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was then performed with PFA. Patients were followed with weekly transtelephonic monitoring, ECG, and Holters at 3, 6, and 12 months. Recurrence was defined as any atrial arrhythmia (AA) > 30 seconds.Receiver operator curve (ROC) analysis revealed that a low voltage threshold of 1.0 mV had the highest value (0.735). The percentage LVA surface area resulting from a threshold of 1.0 mV that predicted AA recurrence was 11.6%. Univariate and multivariate analysis revealed the percentage LVA was the strongest predictor of AA recurrence. The 12-month freedom from AA was 84.6% and 52.9% for subjects under and over the low voltage area threshold respectively. CONCLUSIONS: A voltage threshold of 1.0 mV is proposed as a threshold for defining LVA using the spherical catheter, but a range of approximately 0.5-1.5 mV yielded similar performance. Increased low voltage area in the pre-ablation atrial map was associated with a higher risk of AA recurrence.

recs.title: Can Intravenous Cangrelor Protect the Myocardium in Infarction-related Cardiogenic Shock?
Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial.
recs.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial. SETTING: Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023. PARTICIPANTS: 2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality. RESULTS: 2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2000039376.

recs.title: Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Single-pill combination therapy improves medication adherence and hypertension control. However, limited evidence is available on its implementation in routine clinical practice. OBJECTIVE: To assess the long-term effectiveness, implementation, and sustainability of single-pill combination therapy through team-based care for blood pressure reduction among patients with uncontrolled hypertension in primary care settings in Colombia and Jamaica. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicountry, unblinded, pragmatic, cluster randomized clinical trial. Twenty primary care clinics in Jamaica and 20 in Colombia were randomly assigned to either the single-pill combination therapy group or the standard care group. A total of 1706 adults with uncontrolled hypertension were enrolled between February 23, 2023, and September 12, 2024. The final follow-up visit occurred on September 9, 2026. INTERVENTIONS: In the intervention group (n = 869), a team-based care approach that included physician and nurse training, health coaching, home blood pressure monitoring, and blood pressure audit and feedback was used to implement single-pill combination therapy. Single-pill combinations were purchased locally and provided to patients. In the standard care group (n = 837), patients received monotherapy or polytherapy with guideline-recommended medications covered by health insurance or government programs. The intervention lasted 18 months, with additional follow-up at 24 months. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to 18 months. Three blood pressure measurements were obtained at each of 2 visits at each time point using a standard protocol. RESULTS: Among the 1706 enrolled participants, at baseline, the mean age was 61.4 years, 69.9% of participants were female, and 98.2% were taking antihypertensive medications. Among the 1574 participants included in the primary analysis, systolic blood pressure decreased by 19.1 mm Hg, from 145.9 mm Hg at baseline to 126.8 mm Hg at 18 months, in the intervention group and by 9.0 mm Hg, from 145.0 mm Hg to 136.1 mm Hg, in the standard care group, with a between-group difference of -10.1 mm Hg (95% CI, -13.3 to -6.9 mm Hg; P < .001). At 18 months, 69.5% of patients in the intervention group and 29.2% in the standard care group achieved systolic blood pressure less than 130 and diastolic blood pressure less than 80 mm Hg. Serious adverse events (death and hospitalization) occurred at similar frequencies in the intervention (7.9%) and standard care (9.9%) groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implementing single-pill combination therapy through team-based care significantly reduced blood pressure over 18 months among adults with uncontrolled hypertension in Colombia and Jamaica. This comprehensive strategy integrating single-pill combination therapy with team-based care could be widely adopted and scaled up for hypertension control, particularly in resource-constrained settings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05405920.

recs.title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial. METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed. RESULTS: Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03042104; Unique Identifier: NCT03042104.

recs.title: From Anatomy to Tissue: Cardiac CT Finally Turns Its Attention to the Aortic Valve.
Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis: Is it Time to Refine Our Classification Before We Randomize?
Ventricular Fibrillation During Pulsed Field Ablation With Dual-Energy Focal Catheters in Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Arrhythmia induction during catheter ablation in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been reported, but the risk associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA) remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the procedural incidence of unexpected ventricular fibrillation (VF) during PFA in patients with CIEDs and describe associated clinical and device findings. METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of consecutive PFA procedures in patients with CIEDs. All procedures were reviewed for unexpected VF. RESULTS: Among 107 consecutive procedures using PFA energy in patients with CIEDs, 83 were atrial and 24 were ventricular ablations. Unexpected VF occurred in 4 patients (overall incidence 3.7%, 95% CI 1.0% - 9.3%): 1 during left atrial PFA for pulmonary vein isolation and 3 during left ventricular PFA for ventricular tachycardia ablations. VF occurred at ablation sites both near and remote from CIED lead tips. Device electrograms demonstrated prominent ablation artifact with abnormal triggered activity and mode switch behavior. Intra-procedural recordings also demonstrated local capture and R on T mechanisms. CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected VF during PFA in patients with CIEDs occurred in 3.7% of procedures. These results complement prior adverse-event reports and support systematic pre-, intra-, and post-procedure CIED management, with external defibrillation immediately available, whenever PFA or dual-energy ablation is performed in patients with cardiac devices.

recs.title: Cardio-renal-metabolic health checks: why we must act quickly.
Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline). RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121). CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

recs.title: Meet the First Authors.
Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND: Research Summary.
Molecular signatures associated with reduced renal function in aortic regurgitation and aortic stenosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) accelerates aortic valve (AV) disease, yet the molecular pathways linking declining renal function to aortic regurgitation (AR) and aortic stenosis (AS) remain poorly defined. We aimed to characterize AV phenotype-specific molecular signatures associated with reduced renal function. METHODS: We performed an observational cross-sectional study using targeted proteomic profiling (Olink) in human AV from patients with AR or AS, stratified by renal function (eGFR≥60 vs < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Pathway enrichment analyses were performed using exploratory candidate proteins. Candidate molecular signatures were subsequently examined in independent cohorts (AR: n = 215; AS: n = 325) across renal function categories using histology, immunohistochemistry, ELISA, and qPCR. RESULTS: Reduced renal function was associated with distinct molecular patterns in AR and AS. In AR, exploratory proteomic profiling suggested enrichment of neutrophil degranulation, chemotaxis/adhesion and thrombo-inflammatory signaling pathways. Tissue characterization showed progressive extracellular matrix remodeling, collagen maturation, increased neutrophil markers (NGAL, MPO) and upregulation of pro-inflammatory (IL6, IL-8, IL-32, IL-33, CCL-2, TNF-α, RANTES), pro-adhesive (ICAM-1) and pro-thrombotic mediators (PAI-1) across renal function categories. In AS, exploratory proteomics suggested matrix disassembly and osteogenic signatures, while tissue characterization showed greater valvular calcification (BMP-2, -4, -9), collagen degradation (COL1, MMP-1, -3, TIMP-1) and inflammatory infiltration with declining renal function. Shared candidate proteins showed opposite regulation in AR and AS. CONCLUSIONS: Reduced renal function is associated with distinct, phenotype-specific patterns of AV remodeling-predominantly thrombo-inflammatory in AR and osteogenic-matrix-disruptive in AS- indicating heterogeneous molecular responses across the two major forms of aortic valve disease.

recs.title: Multiomics Integration Reveals a Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Myopathy in Cardiometabolic HFpEF.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to be key components of skeletal muscle dysfunction, but comprehensive profiling of metabolic pathways has not been conducted. Elucidation of dysregulated metabolic pathways is essential to determine viable targets for the treatment of exercise intolerance in HFpEF. METHODS: Male ZSF1 Obese rats (HFpEF, n=8) and Wistar Kyoto lean normotensive controls (Control, n=8) were studied at 26 weeks of age. The gastrocnemius was analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics. Differential expression across all omics layers was determined using standard statistical modeling with thresholds of absolute fold‑change >1.5 and FDR <0.05, unless otherwise specified. Additional targeted plasma and skeletal muscle metabolomics and lipidomics were performed in HFpEF and control rats, including analyses of the soleus and the extensor digitorum longus, to validate features associated with predominantly oxidative and glycolytic muscle, respectively. RESULTS: Pathway-level analysis for RNA sequencing and proteomics revealed significant downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (natural enrichment score (NES), -2.1; P<0.005), electron transport chain (NES, -2.0; P<0.005), and tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle (-1.8; P<0.05). The most upregulated pathways were PPAR signaling (NES, 2.2; P<0.0001), tryptophan metabolism (NES, 1.8; P<0.005), and amino acid oxidation (NES, 1.8; P<0.005) pathways. Metabolomics revealed an accumulation of tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and phosphate reduction. Branched-chain amino acids were significantly increased, whereas amino acids related to tryptophan metabolism were reduced and shifted towards increased serotonin accumulation. Phospholipid species were differentially regulated with increased palmitoylated phosphatidylcholines but reduced arachidonoyl-phosphatidylcholine species. Phosphatidylethanolamines species (16:0/16:1-18:0/18:2) were increased. CONCLUSIONS: HFpEF skeletal muscle shows signatures of profound mitochondrial and peroxisomal dysfunction with lipid overload, impaired branched chain amino acid and tryptophan metabolism, and a shift in membrane phospholipid composition, supporting an acquired metabolic myopathy in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

recs.title: Characteristics and Thresholds of Coronary Lesions to Predict Acute Coronary Syndrome From Artificial Intelligence-Guided Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Characteristics of future culprit lesions according to artificial intelligence-guided quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) are unknown. OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to characterize and derive thresholds to predict future culprit lesions from coronary computed tomography angiography using AI-QCT. METHODS: A total of 2,169 patients/13,772 lesions undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography at Turku University Hospital, Finland, (derivation) and 553 patients/3,948 lesions from Amsterdam University Medical Center, the Netherlands, (validation) were analyzed with AI-QCT. Lesions from vessels undergoing early revascularization were excluded. Lesion-level total plaque volume (TPV) and noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV) thresholds were derived and externally validated to predict lesion-level and patient-level acute coronary syndrome (ACS). RESULTS: Future culprit lesions from both cohorts (n = 69 validation; n = 15 derivation) had consistently higher median TPV (101 mm3 validation; 115 mm3 derivation; P = 0.811) and NCPV (65 mm3 validation; 74 mm3 derivation; P = 0.709) compared with control lesions (P < 0.001) and were nonobstructive in 69.6% (derivation) and 40.0% (validation). Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived and associated with significantly higher adjusted rates of lesion-level (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 12.09; 95% CI: 6.95-21.04; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 10.82; 95% CI: 6.22-18.80; P < 0.001) and patient-level ACS (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 2.92; 95% CI: 1.65-5.16; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 5.11; 95% CI: 2.49-10.46; P < 0.001) with consistent results in the validation cohort. CONCLUSIONS: Future culprit lesions vs nonculprit lesions by AI-QCT demonstrated significantly higher plaque volumes and were nonobstructive in 40% to 70%. Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived to predict future culprit lesions and associated with increased rates of lesion-level and patient-level ACS in 2 independent cohorts.

recs.title: Sex-Stratified Outcomes in Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis: The BASIS Subgroup Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The BASIS (Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis) trial demonstrated that balloon angioplasty plus aggressive medical management was superior to aggressive medical management alone for symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis. However, whether sex modifies this treatment effect is unknown. METHODS: This prespecified secondary analysis of the BASIS randomized controlled trial included 501 patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis from 31 Chinese centers (November 2018 to April 2022). Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared between sexes and across treatment arms within each sex. The primary outcome was stroke or death within 30 days, or ischemic stroke in the qualifying artery territory or revascularization beyond 30 days through 12 months. RESULTS: Among 501 patients (mean age, 58 years), 158 (31.5%) were women. No significant sex-by-treatment interaction was observed for primary or key secondary outcomes (all P for interaction >0.05). In sex-stratified analyses, balloon angioplasty reduced primary outcome risk versus aggressive medical management in men (2.9% versus 11.1%; hazard ratio [HR]=0.21 [95% CI, 0.07-0.65]; P=0.01). In women, the effect favored balloon angioplasty but was not statistically significant (7.8% versus 18.5%; HR=0.37 [95% CI, 0.14-1.01]; P=0.051). CONCLUSIONS: No significant interaction between sex and treatment effect was found, suggesting balloon angioplasty's benefit relative to aggressive medical management does not clearly differ by sex. Sex-stratified results showed significant benefit in men and a nonsignificant trend in women, but the study lacked power for definitive interaction testing, so findings are exploratory. Further research is needed to confirm these findings in broader populations. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT03703635.

recs.title: 25-Hydroxyvitamin D: what is the target?
Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand. RESULTS: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2 mg, -15.0 (95% CI, -17.1 to -12.9) percentage points with ribupatide 4 mg, and -16.3 (95% CI, -18.4 to -14.2) percentage points with ribupatide 6 mg (P < .001 for all). For at least 5% body weight reduction at week 48, the multiply imputed response rates were 68.1% (95% CI, 59.9% to 75.3%) for ribupatide 2 mg (97 of 142), 88.0% (95% CI, 81.3% to 92.6%) for ribupatide 4 mg (124 of 141), 85.7% (95% CI, 78.6% to 90.7%) with ribupatide 6 mg (121 of 141), and 16.0% (95% CI, 10.8% to 23.1%) with placebo (23 of 143). Placebo-adjusted differences for ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg were 52.0 (95% CI, 42.2 to 61.9), 72.0 (95% CI, 63.7 to 80.2), and 69.7 (95% CI, 61.1 to 78.3) percentage points, respectively (all P < .001). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events with ribupatide were gastrointestinal events, occurring in 47.9%, 58.2%, and 63.1% of participants receiving ribupatide 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg, respectively, compared with 23.1% receiving placebo; most were mild to moderate in severity and few participants (0.7%) permanently discontinued study treatment because of adverse events. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide resulted in significantly greater weight loss at 48 weeks. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent tolerability findings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06396429.

recs.title: The Regulatory History of the Watchman Left Atrial Appendage Closure Device: A Long and Winding Road.
Exercise-Induced Tricuspid Regurgitation: Clinical Predictors and Hemodynamic Implications.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise-induced preload/afterload changes could affect tricuspid regurgitation (TR). OBJECTIVES: The study aims to assess exercise-induced TR (exTR+), its consequences, and predictors. METHODS: Consecutive patients underwent exercise cardiac catheterization and three-dimensional echocardiography. ExTR+ was defined as a ≥1 grade increase in TR severity. RESULTS: ExTR+ occurred in 34% of 132 patients. Patients with exTR+ were older, had more atrial fibrillation, higher natriuretic peptides/heart failure with preserved ejection fraction probability scores, higher filling pressures, and lower cardiac output (P < 0.05). ExTR+ displayed greater right ventricular dilation, right atrial pressure rise, lower cardiac output, and lower oxygen consumption (P < 0.05). Exercise rather than resting TR regurgitant volume was more associated with cardiac output and oxygen consumption. Baseline TR, atrial fibrillation, and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (OR: 1.065, 4.97, and 1.0004 per pg/mL, respectively, P < 0.05) predicted exTR+ (area under the curve: 0.91). CONCLUSIONS: ExTR+ is frequent, identifies heart failure with preserved ejection fraction-like phenotypes with a maladaptive exercise response, and adds information beyond resting TR.

recs.title: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension. METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality. CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

recs.title: Standards Defining Echocardiography Core Laboratory (ECL) in Clinical Practice and Research.
recs.abstract: Echocardiography is extensively utilized in both clinical practice and research due to its accessibility. Echocardiography core laboratories (ECLs) adhering to societal guidelines offer superior readings and interpretations compared with the on-site assessments by reducing measurement variability and enhancing study precision. In the present work, we aim to define minimum standards for clinical echocardiography laboratories and research ECLs based on recommendations from the American Society of Echocardiography and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging, as well as on expert opinion and our experience in European countries. Accurate acquisition of high-quality images is crucial for ensuring reproducibility, repeatability and reliability of the echocardiographic measurements. In addition to the commonly used workstations, an academic ECL must also possess the necessary capacities and skilled personnel to conduct sophisticated research projects. Personnel should hold advanced certification in echocardiography, indicating postgraduate training and experience beyond the basic cardiovascular ultrasound education. They should be capable of designing, performing, and interpreting complex echocardiography studies. Reproducibility of the ECL should be validated using a small, randomly selected sample, preferably in the early analytic phase. ECL readings and interpretations are superior to site-reported measurements and serve as the gold standard in observational studies and clinical trials. To ensure internal validity, an academic ECL should continuously evaluate/report reproducibility, repeatability and reliability. ECL should be formally acknowledged and accredited by an international scientific imaging society.

recs.title: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in transcatheter mitral interventions: percutaneous anterior leaflet modification.
recs.abstract: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) remains one of the most catastrophic complications of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) interventions, including TMVR in native valve, valve-in-valve, valve-in-ring, and valve-in-mitral annular calcification procedures. Its incidence varies widely across procedural types (0%-40%), with mortality rates approaching 36%, and represents a leading cause of patient ineligibility, excluding 4%-50% of candidates from TMVR. Accurate pre-procedural risk stratification relies on cardiac computed tomography, which enables annular sizing, virtual valve implantation, neo- and skirt neo-left ventricular outflow tract area quantification, and fluoroscopic projection planning. Key anatomic determinants of LVOTO include anterior mitral leaflet length, aortomitral angle, septal hypertrophy, left ventricular cavity size, and device-related factors. To mitigate LVOTO risk and expand treatment eligibility, in addition to septal modification, anterior mitral leaflet modification techniques have emerged, broadly categorized into electrosurgical laceration approaches-LAMPOON and ELASTA-and balloon-assisted translocation techniques for balloon-expandable valves-BATMAN, CLEVE, DETROIT, and ROBIN. Each strategy addresses distinct anatomic substrates and procedural scenarios, and their complementary profiles support individualized technique selection. This review aims to present an in-depth discussion of LVOTO in TMVR and anterior leaflet modification strategies.

recs.title: Preprocedural transesophageal echocardiography before cardioversion in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-associated atrial fibrillation and thromboembolic risk: A follow-up, granular study.
Smart Alerting in Smartphone-Based First Responder Systems and Arrival Before Emergency Medical Services:The ALARM Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Smartphone alerting systems (SAS) aim to increase the proportion of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) cases in which a community first responder (CFR) arrives before emergency medical services (EMS). Many use fixed-radius alerts and ignore estimated arrival times. We compared different alerting strategies to maximize CFR arrival before EMS. METHODS: In a prospective, randomized three-arm trial, smart alerting (SMA) was compared with fixed-radius strategies (600 m and 2500 m). The primary endpoint was the rate of CFR arrival before EMS. In the SMA arm, responders were dispatched based on individually estimated travel times versus expected ambulance time. Binary endpoints were analyzed using chi-square tests, reporting risk differences and 95% confidence intervals; continuous endpoints used non-parametric tests. RESULTS: Across 823 activations, 1482 CFR were dispatched. CFR arrived before EMS in 31%, 57%, and 58% of missions in the 600 m, 2500 m, and SMA groups, respectively. Compared with the 600 m strategy, SMA increased pre-EMS arrival (risk difference +26.8%, 95% CI 18.6-34.4; p < 0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed compared with the 2500 m strategy (risk difference +1.2%, 95% CI -7.0-+9.3; p = 0.80). Response rates were 56%, 83%, and 87%, respectively. In the SMA group, 31% of accepting CFR were excluded because predicted arrival exceeded EMS arrival. Response times were longer with smart alerting reflecting greater dispatch distances. CONCLUSIONS: Smart alerting increased the likelihood of CFR arriving before EMS while reducing dispatches unlikely to achieve pre-EMS arrival. Further research should evaluate its impact on patient outcomes.

recs.title: AI-Identified Reasons for Nonescalation of Lipid-Lowering Therapy for Secondary Prevention.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Despite guideline recommendations for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals in secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) remains underused. Identifying treat-to-target strategy adoption and reasons for LLT nonescalation are critical to close guideline-discordant care gaps. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether large language models (LLMs) can identify a treat-to-target strategy use and extract reasons for LLT nonescalation from clinical notes when LDL-C concentration is above goal. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients from January 1, 2019, through May 15, 2025. Notes from most recent clinical encounters were retrieved and split into development, test, and inference sets. The setting was a large, integrated health system in Northern California. Adults aged 18 to 90 years with 2 or more clinician-billed encounters for ASCVD and with LDL-C level greater than or equal to 70 mg/dL at the most recent encounter were included in note-based analyses. EXPOSURES: Documented LDL-C targets and LLT management decisions. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Model performance was evaluated on LDL-C target documentation, LDL-C target value, LLT adjustment, and reasons for nonescalation against clinical annotations. Outcome prevalence was assessed on the inference set. RESULTS: A total of 28 113 unique patients with ASCVD-related encounters were identified, of whom 13 810 (49.1%; mean [SD] age, 70.9 [11.4] years; 7904 male [57.2%]) had above-goal LDL-C level. Model-annotator and interannotator reliability were not statistically different across outcomes, and micro-weighted F1 scores ranged from 0.80 to 0.98. Of the 13 394 patients with above-goal LDL-C level and 13 354 relevant notes in the inference set, a treat-to-target strategy was identified in 3756 (28.1%) of all relevant notes, most commonly targeting an LDL-C level less than 70 mg/dL (2280 [17.1%]). LLT was not escalated in 11 842 of all relevant notes (88.7%), with 4788 (40.4%) containing at least 1 LLT nonescalation reason, most often due to patient-reported adverse effects (1683 [12.6%]), LDL-C level close to goal (922 [6.9%]), patient preference to avoid LLT (914 [6.8%]), preference for lifestyle changes (811 [6.1%]), and deferral to repeat laboratory tests (617 [4.6%]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this study show that after using a state-of-the art LLM, nearly 9 in 10 ASCVD encounters with above-goal LDL-C level did not have patient LLT escalated, most often because of adverse effects, patient preference, preference for lifestyle changes, therapeutic inertia (eg, repeat laboratory tests), and near-goal LDL-C level. These findings highlight an avenue for personalizing system-level digital health interventions to help discover and minimize guideline-discordant care gaps in secondary prevention of ASCVD.

recs.title: When and How to Consider Left Atrial Appendage Closure as a Management Option for Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: A European Perspective.
Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Heterogeneity in Clinical Evidence: JACC Evidence Review.
recs.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to long-term anticoagulation for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based on several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that collectively enrolled >7,000 participants. In this JACC Evidence Review, we interpret the major RCTs as distinct experiments, clarify what each can and cannot establish, and offer a phenotype-based framework for interpreting the evidence. The most recent RCTs, OPTION, CLOSURE-AF, and CHAMPION-AF, have prompted efforts to pool the evidence into a single summary estimate. However, these trials are not one coherent evidence base; they are distinct clinical experiments that asked different questions. They differ in patient phenotype, comparator, device generation, postprocedure antithrombotic regimen, endpoint construction, and follow-up duration. Study-level meta-analysis of published reports remains methodologically valid for estimating the broad direction of effect of a device class, but when the component trials differ materially in patient phenotype, comparator, and outcome construction, the pooled estimate does not map to a common patient group or treatment decision. Patient eligibility as well as thromboembolic and bleeding risk varied markedly across trials. In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

recs.title: Letter by Doğan et al Regarding Article, "Artificial Intelligence-Derived Volumetric High-Risk Plaque Features Are Predominantly Located Proximal to Maximal Luminal Stenosis".
Community and EMS Interventions to Improve Survival in Cardiac Arrest.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, but evidence from randomized trials about whether community-based implementation strategies improve outcomes is lacking. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based, cluster-randomized trial involving adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in North Carolina counties. The counties were grouped into clusters, which were then randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to implement a multifaceted intervention or administer usual care. The intervention included four components: training of 911 telecommunicators to improve rapid recognition of cardiac arrest, training of 911 telecommunicators to improve delivery of CPR instructions from telecommunicators to bystanders, community CPR training, and enhanced use of automated external defibrillators by first responders or bystanders before EMS arrival. Data were collected through the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2; range, 1 to 5, with higher scores indicating worse neurologic outcome). RESULTS: From July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2026, a total of 28 clusters comprising 11,615 patients were assigned to the intervention group, and 27 clusters comprising 10,844 patients were assigned to the usual-care group. The median age of the patients was 64.0 years, and 36.7% were women. The percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome was 9.0% (1048 of 11,608 patients) in the intervention group and 9.4% (1017 of 10,839 patients) in the usual-care group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.75 to 1.26; P = 0.80). CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, implementation of a multifaceted strategy involving the community and EMS did not result in a greater percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a favorable neurologic outcome than usual care. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; RACE-CARS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04660526.).
