Incidence and predictors of de novo atrial fibrillation in patients with heart failure undergoing continuous rhythm monitoring.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). The true incidence of de novo AF in HF, however, remains uncertain. Moreover, the role of clinical variables and circulating biomarkers in AF risk stratification in this population is not well established. This study aimed to determine the incidence of AF in patients with HF using long-term continuous rhythm monitoring and to identify clinical, structural, and biomarker-based predictors. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective study included patients with HF and reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Long-term rhythm monitoring was performed using implantable loop recorders or single-chamber defibrillators without atrial leads and with ventricular pacing < 20%. Serial blood samples were obtained at baseline, during follow-up, and during HF decompensation, and analyzed using a multiplex panel of selected biomarkers. Multivariable analyses were performed using both baseline biomarker levels and laboratory values closest to AF onset or HF decompensation. RESULTS: A total of 345 patients were enrolled (79% male; median age 68 years; 53% with LVEF< 40%. During a median follow-up of 756 days, 86 patients (24.9%) developed AF episodes lasting > 6 minutes, and 64 patients (18.5%) died. Hypertension, left atrial volume, beta-blocker use, CA-125, NT-proBNP, COL4A1, and AT1-AA were independently associated with AF, whereas aldosterone receptor antagonist therapy was associated with a lower risk of HF (C-index, 0.74). Patients with persistent AF as the initial manifestation had significantly higher mortality than those with paroxysmal AF or no AF. NT-proBNP and COL4A1 were associated with mortality. Clinically relevant bradyarrhythmias and ventricular tachyarrhythmias were also detected. CONCLUSION: De novo AF is a common complication in patients with HF. Integrating clinical variables, structural parameters, and biomarkers improves the identification of patients at increased risk of developing AF. Continuous monitoring enables early detection of rhythm abnormalities that may influence therapeutic management.

recs.title: FGF13 Regulates Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via PGRN Glycosylation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Macrophage polarization and complement activation play a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. FGF13 (fibroblast growth factor 13) is a critical regulator of cardiac homeostasis. However, the role and mechanism of FGF13 in myocardial I/R injury remain unclear. METHODS: FGF13 expression was detected in cardiomyocytes after hypoxia/reoxygenation and in hearts subjected to myocardial I/R. Cardiomyocyte-specific FGF13 knockout and adeno-associated virus serotype 9-mediated overexpression mice were generated. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses identified key downstream mechanisms. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, and glycoproteomics identified PGRN (progranulin) as an FGF13-interacting protein and mapped its glycosylation site. Mechanistic studies were performed using Transwell cocultures of neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes and bone marrow-derived macrophages, together with molecular and biochemical approaches. Virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations identified a small-molecule FGF13 inhibitor. RESULTS: FGF13 was upregulated in cardiomyocytes after myocardial I/R. Cardiomyocyte-specific FGF13 knockout alleviated, whereas overexpression exacerbated, cardiac dysfunction and myocardial injury after I/R. Mechanistically, FGF13, through its asparagine 121 residue, competitively occupied the asparagine 263 glycosylation site of PGRN, sterically preventing STT3A (STT3 oligosaccharyltransferase complex catalytic subunit A)-mediated glycosylation of asparagine 263 and suppressing PGRN secretion. FGF13 depletion restored PGRN glycosylation and secretion, which activated macrophage TNFR2/PI3K/AKT (tumor necrosis factor receptor 2/phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B) signaling in a paracrine manner, promoted M2 polarization while suppressing M1 polarization, and inhibited complement activation and inflammation. The small-molecule FGF13 inhibitor CWD8 (1-[2-amino-2-methylpropyl]-5,5-dimethylpiperidin-3-ol) also attenuated myocardial I/R injury. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the critical role of FGF13 in myocardial I/R injury and reveal a competitive mechanism by which FGF13 hinders STT3A-mediated PGRN glycosylation. We identify the PGRN glycosylation-PI3K/AKT axis as the key downstream pathway mediating FGF13-regulated macrophage polarization and complement activation, suggesting that small-molecule FGF13 inhibitors may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for myocardial I/R injury.

recs.title: Human Journey behind Food Is Medicine: A Participatory Study With a Lived Experience Advisory Group.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Poor diet is substantially associated with cardiometabolic diseases in the United States, yet systemic efforts to improve dietary behaviors remain limited. The American Heart Association's Health Care by FoodTM initiative seeks to advance Food Is Medicine interventions by integrating patient-centered insights into program design. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of individuals managing diet-related chronic conditions to better understand the emotional, cultural, and systemic factors influencing dietary behavior change. METHODS: Using a participatory action research approach, a diverse Lived Experience Patient Advisory Group was convened. Fourteen participants engaged in a multiphase process including surveys, daily food diaries, individual interviews, and a 2-day in-person workshop. These activities were designed to elicit personal narratives, identify barriers and motivators to dietary change, and co-develop potential solutions. Thematic analysis was used to synthesize insights across all engagement activities. RESULTS: Fifteen subthemes emerged, grouped into 3 broader themes: facing change, understanding barriers, and acting. These themes highlighted the complex interplay between identity, social norms, access, and self-efficacy in shaping food choices. Participants also proposed a framework of opportunities for intervention, emphasizing the importance of support systems, culturally relevant education, and systemic alignment across health care, community, and policy sectors. CONCLUSIONS: Behavior change in food consumption is a deeply personal and socially embedded process. Centering lived experience in Food Is Medicine program design offers critical insights for creating more inclusive, effective, and sustainable interventions. This work underscores the need for coordinated, multilevel strategies to support dietary behavior change at scale.

recs.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

recs.title: What constitutes healing after silent plaque rupture?
Iron Repletion in HFpEF: An Endpoint Is Not Yet an Indication.
Efficacy and Safety of Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists Across Geographic Regions in Heart Failure: A Patient-Level Pooled Analysis.
Defining silent plaque rupture healing in vivo: a structural approach by OCT.
Promoting integrity in collaborations between academia and the medical industry.
recs.abstract: Collaboration between academia and the medical industry has been fundamental to advances in cardiovascular diagnostics, pharmacotherapy, devices, and digital health. However, interactions among academic institutions, commercial partners, and professional societies continue to require careful governance to preserve transparency, independence, and public trust. While several professional societies have established robust conflict-of-interest policies, differences in disclosure frameworks and regulatory requirements across institutions and jurisdictions continue to affect clinical research, guideline development, and professional education. Court of Justice of the European Union (EU) rulings further indicate that disclosure alone may be insufficient for expert input within EU agencies. This conceptual article discusses a structured framework for collaboration between academia and the medical industry. Based on European and international policies, regulatory experience, and established practice models, it defines six principles-transparency, independence, accountability, equity, sustainability, and patient-centred benefit-and provides practical recommendations. These include harmonized, publicly accessible disclosure standards; separation of industrial funding from scientific decision-making; strengthened institutional accountability; and independent education and training to support integrity across stakeholders.

recs.title: Same ejection fraction, different patient: has the defibrillator outlived its own trial data?
First and Subsequent Major Cardiovascular Events With Oral Semaglutide in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes: A Secondary Analysis of the SOUL Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: In the Semaglutide Cardiovascular Outcomes Trial (SOUL), oral semaglutide reduced the risk of a first 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (3-P MACE; including nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and cardiovascular [CV] death). Total event analyses, assessing both first and subsequent events, can contribute to a better understanding of the impact of interventions on the total burden of disease; however, the effects of oral semaglutide on subsequent events are unknown. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of oral semaglutide vs placebo on total 3-P MACE. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a prespecified secondary analysis of the double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven, phase 3b SOUL randomized clinical trial, conducted from June 2019 to September 2024 with a median (IQR) follow-up of 49.5 (44.0-54.9) months at 444 centers in 33 countries. Participants had type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic CV disease and/or chronic kidney disease. Data were analyzed from December 2024 to August 2025. INTERVENTIONS: Once-daily oral semaglutide (maximal dose 14 mg) or placebo, in addition standard of care. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Occurrence of total (first and subsequent) 3-P MACE. RESULTS: Overall, 9650 participants (median [IQR] age, 66.0 [61.0-72.0] years; 6860 [71.1%] male) were randomized 1:1. In the oral semaglutide group, fewer first and subsequent 3-P MACE occurred (683 total; 579 first and 104 subsequent events) compared with placebo (791 total; 668 first and 123 subsequent events) (mean ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.76-0.97; P = .01). For the end point of 3-P MACE plus non-CV death, there were 138 fewer total events with oral semaglutide (910 events) compared with placebo (1048 events) (mean ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.79-0.95; P = .004). As previously reported, adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 749 (15.5%) and 559 (11.6%) participants receiving oral semaglutide and placebo, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Oral semaglutide reduced the risk of first plus subsequent 3-P MACE vs placebo, highlighting the benefit of oral semaglutide in reducing the total burden of clinical morbidity and mortality in this high-risk population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03914326.

recs.title: Digital readiness for cardiovascular care in high-burden US communities with cardiology workforce constraints.
recs.abstract: Digital health may extend cardiovascular care in communities with limited specialist access, but its effectiveness depends on whether communities have the infrastructure, devices, affordability, and capacity needed to use digital services. We linked national data on cardiometabolic disease burden, cardiology workforce, and digital readiness across 82,999 US census tracts. Among high-burden tracts in counties with no cardiologist or declining per-capita cardiologist supply, 4,765 (18.0%) tracts representing 19.9 million residents had higher digital readiness and were thus classified as deployment-priority tracts, whereas 21,752 (82.0%) tracts representing 74.1 million residents had lower readiness and were investment-priority tracts. Investment-priority tracts were spread across the urban-rural continuum and faced different barriers (adoption versus infrastructure). Contrasting classifications frequently occurred among neighboring census tracts within the same metropolitan area, highlighting geographic variation not captured by county-level targeting. Findings were broadly consistent across nine additional analyses with varying measures of readiness, workforce access, and classification thresholds. These findings provide a national framework for distinguishing communities where digital cardiovascular care may be deployed from those where infrastructure and adoption support may first be needed to enable equitable implementation.

recs.title: The PELICANS Registry: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Extended Longitudinal Investigation of Clinical Outcomes-Adverse Events, Nonrecovery, and Survival.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) disproportionately affects Black women, yet long-term outcome data in socially vulnerable, predominantly Black cohorts remain limited. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to characterize long-term outcomes and baseline predictors of survival, major adverse events (MAEs), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) recovery in a U.S. PPCM cohort. METHODS: This retrospective-prospective registry included 159 women with PPCM (1982-2024). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, MAEs, and LVEF recovery (≥50%). Multivariable and extended Cox models evaluated predictors, adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy. RESULTS: The cohort was 80.5% Black. Over a median 9.0-year follow-up (IQR: 3.4-15.5), 41 patients (25.8%) died and 64 (40.3%) had MAEs. Among 148 patients with echocardiographic follow-up, 69 (46.6%) had sustained LVEF recovery, though 23 (25.0% of initially recovered) declined to LVEF <50%. Independent mortality predictors included elevated creatinine (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.86; 95% CI: 1.37-5.97), lower index LVEF (aHR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.98), family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure (aHR: 3.27; 95% CI: 1.41-7.56), and non-O blood type (aHR: 2.36; 95% CI: 1.04-5.33), retaining significance after adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy (n = 62). Elevated creatinine increased MAE odds (adjusted OR: 7.09; 95% CI: 1.98-32.9), while higher LVEF, parity, and obesity reduced them. Baseline LV dilation (≥60 mm), Black race, older age, and family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure predicted lower LVEF recovery odds. CONCLUSIONS: This long-term predominantly Black PPCM cohort had high mortality, low LVEF recovery, and frequent late relapse. These findings highlight the importance of baseline risk stratification and sustained echocardiographic surveillance to guide clinical decision-making.

recs.title: Machine Learning Reveals Prognostic Value of Medical History in Suspected Coronary Artery Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Risk stratification in suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) relies on clinical history and imaging, but longitudinal medical history may provide additional prognostic information. OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data improves prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) beyond demographics and stress perfusion cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with suspected CAD. METHODS: A total of 2,159 patients (65 ± 12 years, 44% women) undergoing stress perfusion CMR were included. Models used demographics, CMR findings, and registry diagnoses and procedures from the prior 10 years. MACE was defined as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or coronary intervention. Random Forest models were used for binary prediction, and Random Survival Forests (RSF) and penalized Ridge Cox regression for time-to-event analysis. RESULTS: During 2.7 ± 0.9 years of follow-up, 212 patients (9.8%) experienced MACE. For binary prediction, the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.66 (95% CI: 0.62-0.69) using demographics and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.68-0.75; P = 0.001) after adding historical registry data. The full model achieved an AUROC of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.79-0.85) and outperformed the demographics-plus-CMR model (AUROC: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.78-0.84; ΔAUROC: 0.014; 95% CI: 0.002-0.027; P = 0.029). In time-to-event analysis, RSF and Cox regression performed similarly using demographics and CMR (concordance index [C-index] 0.80 for both; P = 0.546). After including registry data RSF achieved a C-index of 0.81 (P = 0.144), and Cox performance decreased to C-index 0.77 (P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with suspected CAD, machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data have the potential to improve prognostic risk prediction beyond demographics and stress perfusion CMR.

recs.title: Thirty-Day All-Cause Readmissions After Pregnancy-Associated Hospitalizations With Heart Failure in the United States: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmissions Database.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the United States. There is a paucity of data regarding pregnancy-associated heart failure readmissions. This study aims to characterize the 30-day heart failure readmission patterns in pregnancy-associated admissions. METHODS: The National Readmission Database from 2016 to 2021 was used to identify women aged 13 to 49 with an index hospitalization with heart failure as the primary or secondary diagnosis during a pregnancy-related admission, identified by diagnosis-related group codes and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression were used to characterize readmission patterns and identify independently associated factors. RESULTS: Among 19 452 eligible index hospitalizations, 2659 were followed by a 30-day readmission; the survey-weighted readmission rate was 13.5%. In the fully adjusted model, Medicare and Medicaid coverage, residence in a small metropolitan area, greater All Patient Refined Diagnosis-Related Group severity, discharge with home health care, and discharge against medical advice were associated with higher odds of readmission. Deficiency anemia, chronic pulmonary disease, diabetes without chronic complications, renal failure, solid tumor without metastasis, and cardiovascular or respiratory disorders complicating pregnancy were also independently associated with increased readmission. CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 7 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations complicated by heart failure was followed by a 30-day all-cause readmission. Readmission risk reflected a combination of illness severity, discharge disposition, payer status, geographic location, and selected medical and pregnancy-related comorbidities. These findings support the development and evaluation of individualized, multidisciplinary transitional-care strategies for patients at highest risk.

recs.title: Triglycerides and Risk of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease and Acute Pancreatitis: 4 Population-Based Cohorts.
Isoform-resolved sequencing uncovers a hidden code inside RNA methylation changes in heart failure.
Acute Kidney Injury Disrupts Cardiac Remodeling via SerpinA3N.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiorenal syndrome type 3 describes cardiac injury triggered by acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI caused by ischemia reperfusion injury represents a model for kidney injury during kidney transplant. It is well known that kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk to develop cardiac fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms linking renal injury to myocardial remodeling or cardiac fibrosis remain unclear. METHODS: Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of ischemia reperfusion injury-AKI, we combined proteomics and RNA seqencing transcriptomics to define early cardiac responses. We validated the proteomics and RNA sequencing data with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, ELISA, cytokine array, and western blotting for profibrotic and injury markers. We assessed SerpinA3N function using a granzyme B activity assay kit and XAV939, an inhibitor of SerpinA3N. Ingenuity pathway analysis further confirmed serine protease activity inhibition and increased expression of cardiac fibrosis-related genes after AKI. RESULTS: Successful establishment of renal ischemia reperfusion injury causing AKI, followed by significant induction of cardiac injury. AKI significantly upregulated SerpinA3N in the heart while suppressing serine protease (granzyme B) activity. Concomitantly, AKI hearts displayed elevated profibrotic genes (FN1, COL1A1, TGF-β1), mitochondrial dysfunction, and heightened inflammatory signaling. In vitro, inhibition of SerpinA3N with XAV939 restored granzyme B activity, confirming direct suppression by SerpinA3N. CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that SerpinA3N serves as a key mediator of cardiorenal syndrome type 3 pathogenesis, by inhibiting granzyme B, which promotes profibrotic remodeling in the heart following AKI. Targeting SerpinA3N could be a potential therapeutic approach that restores balanced extracellular matrix turnover and mitigates cardiac fibrosis.

recs.title: Comparative Clinical and Procedural Outcomes Among Three Pulsed Field Ablation Systems for Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Real-World Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal ablation technology for atrial fibrillation. Several PFA systems are available, with distinct catheter designs and energy delivery protocols. Direct comparisons between PFA systems remain limited. OBJECTIVE: This study compared the procedural characteristics, safety, and efficacy of three contemporary PFA technologies in routine clinical practice. METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing their first pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using the circular multielectrode array catheter (CMAC)(PulseSelectTM), the variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC)(VaripulseTM) or the lattice-tip catheter (LTC)(AfferaTM) were prospectively included. Freedom from any atrial arrhythmia (AA) was evaluated using 12-lead electrocardiography and 24-hour Holter at 3, 6 and 12 months, followed by routine clinical follow-up. RESULTS: A total of 198 patients (CMAC:91, VLCC:50, LTC: 57) were included. Acute PVI was achieved in all patients (median age, 68 [61.0, 76.0] years; 127 male (64.1%); 97 paroxysmal (49.0%)). The procedure and ablation times were longest in the LTC group. During a mean follow-up of 352.4±207.2 days, the estimated 12-month freedom from AA recurrence beyond the 8-week blanking period was comparable among the CMAC, VLCC, and LTC groups (76.9%, 71.6%, and 78.8%; log-rank p=0.72). In adjusted multivariable Cox regression, PFA system choice was not associated with AA recurrence (LTC vs. CMAC: HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.39-1.52, p=0.45; VLCC vs. CMAC: HR 1.16, 95% CI 0.58-2.34, p=0.67). One major complication (0.51%, ischemic stroke (CMAC)) occurred. CONCLUSION: In this prospective real-world study, PVI with the CMAC, VLCC, and LTC showed comparable efficacy and safety outcomes, while procedural profiles differed.

recs.title: Before Metabolic Syndrome: Moving Cardiovascular Prevention Earlier.
Reconsidering β-Blockers in HFpEF: An Urgent Priority.
Deletion of Yes-Associated Protein in Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells Alleviates Atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The migration and proliferation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) are critical processes in the development of atherosclerosis. YAP (Yes-associated protein) regulates VSMC migration and proliferation. However, its specific role in atherosclerosis remains unclear. METHODS: Atherosclerosis models were generated in mice injected with adeno-associated virus 8-mPCSK9 (murine proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) or ApoE-/- (apolipoprotein E knockout) mice by being fed a high-cholesterol diet. Primary VSMCs were used to elucidate its mechanism. RESULTS: YAP expression was elevated in VSMCs within mouse atherosclerotic plaques. Both tamoxifen-mediated YAPΔVSMC or adeno-associated virus-inducible VSMC-specific YAP knockout mice injected with adeno-associated virus 8-mPCSK9 and YAPΔVSMCApoE-/- mice exhibited alleviated atherosclerotic phenotype. Further study found that angiopoietin-2 overexpression induced VSMC phenotypic switching, migration, and proliferation in YAP knockout VSMCs stimulated with platelet-derived growth factor-BB in vitro. Furthermore, the VSMC-specific angiopoietin-2 overexpression could completely reverse VSMC YAP deficiency-alleviated atherosclerotic phenotype and the effect of YAP-mediated VSMC phenotypic switching. Mechanistically, YAP upregulated angiopoietin-2 via TEAD4 (murine TEA domain family member 4) in VSMCs. CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, our findings revealed that YAP promotes atherosclerosis by inducing angiopoietin-2-mediated VSMC phenotypic switching via TEAD4. Inhibition of VSMC YAP may be an effective therapeutic strategy for atherosclerosis.

recs.title: Prevalence, clinical implications and prognostic impact of frailty and other geriatric conditions in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to analyze the prevalence and prognostic influence of frailty and other geriatric conditions such as nutritional risk, cognitive status, depression, and dependence in patients with ATTR-CM. METHODS: We performed an observational, prospective, single-center study of 110 ATTR-CM patients who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment from October 2024 to April 2025 and were followed up to September 2026. Study endpoints were all-cause death and the combined event of all-cause death or worsening heart failure. Outcomes were assessed by the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression. RESULTS: The prevalence of frailty, based on 4 different criteria, varied from 32.7% to 62.7%. Dependence, depression, nutritional risk, and cognitive impairment were detected in up to 70.9%, 29.1%, 27.3%, and 15.5% of patients, respectively. Frailty, defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale > 4, a Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe-Frailty Instrument > 2, or a Short Physical Performance Battery < 10, was independently associated with an increased risk of both study outcomes. Dependence (Katz index < 6) and cognitive impairment (Mini Examen Cognitivo score < 23) were also independent predictors of both outcomes. Frailty diagnosis showed incremental prognostic value when added to United Kingdom National Amyloidosis Centre stages. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is frequent in patients with ATTR-CM and is associated with impaired clinical outcomes.

recs.title: Computed Tomography Angiography-Derived Carotid Plaque Features and Risk of Vascular Events in Stroke Patients With Carotid Atherosclerosis: An Imaging Substudy of the CONVINCE Randomized Trial.
Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness With Medical and Invasive Approaches-Chronic Kidney Disease), at a median follow-up of 2.2 years, the primary composite outcome of death or nonfatal myocardial infarction was similar between an initial invasive strategy (INV) compared with an initial conservative strategy (CON) in patients with moderate or severe myocardial ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease. However, the long-term outcomes comparing the 2 strategies are unknown. METHODS: Participants in the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial were randomly assigned to either INV, involving coronary angiography and revascularization when feasible, added to guideline-directed medical therapy or to CON with guideline-directed medical therapy alone and invasive procedures reserved for failure of guideline-directed medical therapy. After the active intervention trial phase, long-term vital status follow-up was conducted through participant contact by participating sites and by health record and centralized death database searches. The primary outcome for the extended follow-up phase was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were cause-specific mortality, including cardiovascular and noncardiovascular mortality. RESULTS: Among the 777 participants randomized (388 to INV and 389 to CON), over a median of 8 years of follow-up, vital status retention among survivors was 95%. There was a total of 429 deaths (55%). Cumulative all-cause mortality (57.4% versus 56.8%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.87-1.28]) or cardiovascular mortality (40.3% versus 38.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.84-1.34]) at 8 years did not differ between INV and CON. The restricted mean survival time was 1941 days (1834-2047 days) for INV versus 1990 days (1885-2094 days) for CON, with an adjusted estimated difference of -99 days (-245 to 46). The posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher death with INV at the 8-year median follow-up was 28% and 52%, respectively. Similarly, the posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher cardiovascular mortality with INV was 23% and 56%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with at least moderate ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease, there was no significant long-term benefit of an initial INV at reducing the risk of all-cause or cardiovascular mortality compared with an initial conservative strategy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01985360.

recs.title: Sex-specific clinical and psychosocial characteristics among individuals with familial hypercholesterolemia reporting side-effects of lipid-lowering therapy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Symptoms attributed to lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) may affect adherence. We explored sex-specific clinical and psychosocial characteristics associated with self-perceived side-effects of LLT in individuals with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH). METHODS: Adults (N = 2709) with FH, identified through a quality registry, were invited to a cross-sectional study. Participants completed a self-report questionnaire covering side-effects, use of LLT, muscle symptoms, pain treatment and psychosocial factors. RESULTS: Among 613 participants (22.6% response rate), median age was 55 (IQR; 43, 65) years and 56% were women. Forty-five (13%) women and 47 (17%) men reported self-perceived side-effects of LLT. In both sexes, self-perceived side-effects were associated with significantly higher perceived sensitivity to medicines, more concerns about LLT, higher ratings of muscle symptoms and pain intensity, and lower self-rated general health. Among women, those with side-effects were more frequently living alone (38% vs 20%, p = 0.017) and reported more musculoskeletal complaints (62% vs 37%, p = 0.004). Among men, those reporting side-effects had higher median LDL-cholesterol (2.5 vs 2.1, p = 0.032), and higher prevalence of depressive symptoms (30% vs 11%, p = 0.003) and insomnia (60% vs 41%, p = 0.045). Adjustment for age, cardiovascular comorbidity and BMI made only minor changes in the effect estimates in logistic regression analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Participants with FH and self-perceived side-effects reported a significant symptom burden and concerns about the use of LLT. Women with side-effects more frequently reported musculoskeletal complaints and living alone, whereas psychological distress and insomnia were more prominent among men reporting side-effects. Individual assessments of sex-specific characteristics may be valuable for improving follow-up.

recs.title: Elevated remnant cholesterol and risk of heart failure in the general population.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Elevated remnant cholesterol is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Here, we tested the hypothesis that high levels of remnant cholesterol are observationally associated with increased risk of heart failure in individuals in the general population with and without statin therapy. METHODS AND RESULTS: We included 108,500 and 428,922 individuals free of baseline heart failure from the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) and the UK Biobank, two cohort studies of the adult Danish and UK general populations started in 2003-2015 and 2006-2010. During median 9.2 and 13.7 years of follow-up, 5321(4.9%) and 21,428(4.3%) developed heart failure in the two studies. Diagnoses of heart failure were retrieved from Danish and UK national health registers. For individuals with and without statin therapy and in both the CGPS and the UK Biobank, stepwise higher remnant cholesterol were associated with stepwise increasing risk of a diagnosis of heart failure. For individuals without statin therapy, those with remnant cholesterol ≥1.5 mmol/L(≥59 mg/dL) compared to those with remnant cholesterol <0.5 mmol/L(<19 mg/dL), the multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for risk of heart failure were 1.40(95% confidence interval: 1.19-1.63) in the CGPS and 1.61(1.38-1.89) in the UK Biobank. Corresponding hazard ratios for individuals with statin therapy were 1.63(1.29-2.07) and 1.60(1.24-2.07), respectively. CONCLUSION: In 108,500 and 428,922 individuals from the general populations of Denmark and the UK, stepwise higher levels of remnant cholesterol were associated with stepwise increasing risk of heart failure in individuals with and without statin therapy.

recs.title: Safety and Efficacy of Topical Nitroglycerin for Radial Artery Dilation (The RADial Trial): A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transradial coronary catheterization is associated with a reduced risk of bleeding and vascular complications. Prior studies have evaluated nitroglycerin to improve transradial access by vasodilating the radial artery, but the optimal route of administration for preprocedural arterial dilation remains unclear. METHODS: In the RADial Trial (Radial Artery Dilatation Trial) patients undergoing transradial coronary catheterization were randomized in a double-blind fashion to receive either a placebo or topical nitroglycerin ointment (nitropaste). The primary outcome was the mean change in radial artery dimensions, assessed using paired t tests. Categorical outcomes were analyzed using odds ratio (OR) with 95% CI. RESULTS: A total of 260 patients (130 placebo, 130 nitroglycerin) were enrolled. Nitropaste significantly increased the mean diameter (2.65±0.6 versus 2.48±0.6 mm), circumference (8.37±1.63 versus 7.77±1.66) and cross-sectional area (5.63±2.28 versus 4.94±2.0 mm) of the radial artery, whereas no significant difference was observed in the placebo arm. Nitropaste was associated with a significant reduction in the number of skin punctures and risk of vasospasm (OR 0.34 [95% CI, 0.13-0.91], P=0.04). There was no significant difference between nitropaste and placebo groups in the odds of hematoma (OR, 0.32 [95% CI, 0.03-3.1], P=0.61), crossover to femoral access (OR, 2.29 [95% CI, 0.9-5.8], P=0.12), need for ultrasound-guided access (OR, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.13-1.15], P=0.13), and hypotension or headache (OR, 1.5 [95% CI, 0.24-9.2], P=1.0). CONCLUSION: Preprocedural administration of nitropaste significantly increases radial artery size and reduces the risk of vasospasm without causing headache or hypotension. REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05239013.

recs.title: Angiography-Derived vs Wire-Based Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide Revascularization: The Randomized LIPSIA-STRATEGY Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Wire-based physiological assessment is recommended to guide coronary revascularization but remains underused. Angiography-derived physiology offers a wire-free alternative; however, randomized comparisons with pressure wire fractional flow reserve (FFR) have yielded inconsistent findings. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to determine whether angiography-derived vessel fractional flow reserve (vFFR)-guided revascularization is noninferior to pressure wire FFR guidance for intermediate coronary stenoses. METHODS: The multicenter, investigator-initiated, randomized LIPSIA-STRATEGY trial included patients with acute or chronic coronary syndromes and at least 1 intermediate coronary stenosis at 8 German centers. Patients were randomized 1:1 to undergo revascularization based on vFFR or FFR. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac events, defined as a composite of cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or unplanned clinically driven revascularization within 1 year, analyzed by modified intention to treat against a noninferiority margin of 3.5 percentage points. RESULTS: Between June 2020 and February 2025, 1,053 patients (median age: 69 years) underwent randomization (vFFR, n = 528; FFR, n = 525). At 1 year, major adverse cardiac events occurred in 15 of 493 patients (3.0%) in the vFFR group and in 20 of 493 (4.1%) in the FFR group (risk difference: -1.01 percentage points; P for noninferiority <0.001); the primary outcome was ascertainable in 986 of the 1,053 randomized patients. The upper boundary of the 1-sided 97.5% CI for the risk difference was 1.29 percentage points, below the prespecified margin (relative risk: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.39-1.45). Physiological values of 0.80 or less occurred in 43.1% vs 35.9% of patients, and the study lesion was revascularized in 41.2% vs 35.5%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with intermediate coronary stenoses requiring physiological assessment, a vFFR-guided revascularization strategy met the prespecified absolute criterion for noninferiority to wire-based FFR at 1 year. Because the observed event rate was lower than anticipated, the margin was less conservative on a relative scale than intended. In a post hoc sensitivity analysis using the relative margin of 1.44 implied by the original assumptions, noninferiority was not met in the primary modified intention-to-treat population. In the corresponding post hoc per-protocol sensitivity analysis, noninferiority was met using this relative margin. Whether that additional revascularization is beneficial is not answered by similar 1-year event rates. (Comparison of Vessel-FFR Versus FFR in Intermediate Coronary Stenoses; NCT03497637; Protocol ID HRC045277.).

recs.title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

recs.title: Atherosclerotic events and acute pancreatitis incidence across the full range of plasma triglycerides in four large cohorts.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: We tested the hypothesis that triglycerides at most levels are associated with higher incidence of ASCVD than acute pancreatitis. METHODS: We examined individuals from the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS) 1976-78 (n = 14,292; a median follow-up of 24 years) and 1991-94 (n = 10,093; 20 years), the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) 2003-15 (n = 107,297; 13 years), the UK Biobank 2006-10 (n = 468,964; 14 years), and nationwide in Denmark 2008-21 (n = 3,415,915; 6 years). RESULTS: The incidence was statistically higher for ASCVD than for acute pancreatitis at any plasma triglycerides up to 30 mmol/L (2657 mg/dL) in all cohorts, while nationwide in Denmark the incidence of acute pancreatitis was nominally higher than that of ASCVD at triglycerides of 50 mmol/L (4429 mg/dL) or higher. In women, age-adjusted incidence rates per 1000 person-years per 1 mmol/L (89 mg/dL) higher plasma triglycerides across all levels were 1.8 (95% confidence interval 1.2-2.3) for ASCVD versus 0.1 (0.02-0.2) for acute pancreatitis in the CCHS 1976-78, 1.9 (1.2-2.5) versus 0.1 (0.01-0.2) in the CCHS 1991-94, 0.9 (0.7-1.0) versus 0.1 (0.1-0.1) in the CGPS, 0.6 (0.6-0.7) versus 0.2 (0.2-0.2) in the UK Biobank, and 0.4 (0.4-0.5) versus 0.05 (0.04-0.05) nationwide in Denmark. Corresponding values in men were 1.5 (1.0-2.0) versus 0.1 (0.1-0.1), 0.9 (0.5-1.3) versus 0.04 (0-0.1), 1.1 (0.9-1.3) versus 0.04 (0-0.08), 1.1 (1.0-1.2) versus 0.1 (0.1-0.1), and 0.6 (0.5-0.6) versus 0.05 (0.05-0.06), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of ASCVD was statistically higher than that of acute pancreatitis up to triglycerides of 30 mmol/L (2657 mg/dL), while acute pancreatitis was nominally higher than ASCVD at 50 mmol/L (4429 mg/dL) or higher.

recs.title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). Serious adverse events occurred in 1553 of 4166 patients (37.3%) who received pelacarsen and in 1709 of 4154 (41.1%) who received placebo. CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen did not result in a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than placebo at a median follow-up of 4.7 years. (Funded by Novartis; Lp[a]HORIZON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04023552.)See also in NEJM Evidence: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

recs.title: Safer Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation: Factor XI/XIa Inhibitors, Left Atrial Appendage Closure, or Both?
Antithrombotic Therapy Management After Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Current Regimens, Evolving Evidence, and the Control Group Dilemma.
recs.abstract: Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure is increasingly used for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation, particularly when long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) is unsuitable. Although postprocedural antithrombotic therapy is necessary to prevent device-related thrombosis (DRT), it may increase bleeding and attenuate the benefit of avoiding long-term OAC. Uncertainty over the optimal antithrombotic strategy persists, with available randomized trials being small and heterogeneous. Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) monotherapy and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) are 2 common early strategies. In ANDES, DRT was numerically less frequent with DOAC than with DAPT (1.5% vs 4.1%). In ADALA, low-dose apixaban was associated with greater net benefit than DAPT (HR: 0.19; P = 0.02), although enrollment was prematurely stopped. A meta-analysis of randomized trials found significantly lower DRT with DOAC than with DAPT (risk ratio: 0.17). Current guidelines endorse regimens largely based on device-specific trial protocols or low-certainty evidence. During the initial postimplantation period, antithrombotic therapy should primarily aim to support device healing and prevent DRT, with treatment intensity tailored according to risk profile, concomitant indications, patient preferences, and the feasibility of imaging follow-up. Reassessment at 45 to 90 days should guide de-escalation once adequate device healing has been confirmed, with no fixed treatment stop date. In the absence of device-related complications, long-term OAC or DAPT should be continued only for concomitant indications, whereas continuation of single antiplatelet therapy or complete withdrawal of antithrombotic therapy should be individualized according to thrombotic and bleeding risk. Finally, definite or probable DRT generally warrants OAC, when feasible; in contrast, treatment decisions should not be based solely on the presence or size of a peridevice leak. This review critically appraises the available evidence and guideline recommendations and discusses how treatment intensity and duration may be tailored over time according to evolving thrombotic and bleeding risks.

recs.title: Safety and Efficacy of Omecamtiv Mecarbil by QRS Duration and Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in GALACTIC-HF.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged QRS duration portends worse outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). In GALACTIC-HF, omecamtiv mecarbil (OM) reduced the primary composite endpoint of first heart failure (HF) event or cardiovascular death. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate whether QRS duration and the presence of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) modify the treatment effect of OM. METHODS: GALACTIC-HF enrolled patients with symptomatic HF, HFrEF (≤35%), and elevated natriuretic peptides. Baseline QRS duration was available in 8,089 of 8,232 participants (98.0%), who were classified into 3 groups: QRS duration <120 ms without CRT (n = 3,724), QRS duration ≥120 ms without CRT (n = 3,225), and CRT regardless of QRS duration (n = 1,140). The authors assessed whether the effect of OM on the primary composite endpoint, first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death differed across these groups. RESULTS: Patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT and those with CRT were older, had lower EF, worse health status, and higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels than those with QRS <120 ms without CRT. When modeled as a continuous variable, baseline QRS duration was associated with clinical outcomes among patients without CRT but not among those with CRT. Among patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT, OM appeared to confer less benefit for the primary composite endpoint (Pinteraction = 0.072), for cardiovascular death (Pinteraction = 0.003), and for all-cause death (Pinteraction = 0.009). In contrast, among patients treated with CRT, OM was beneficial regardless of QRS duration. CONCLUSIONS: In GALACTIC-HF, OM appeared less effective in patients with prolonged QRS duration who did not have CRT, whereas it remained beneficial in CRT-treated patients. (Global Approach to Lowering Adverse Cardiac Outcomes Through Improving Contractility in Heart Failure [GALACTIC-HF]; NCT02929329).

recs.title: Alcohol and cardiovascular disease: inter-organ crosstalk, microvascular dysfunction, and cardiovascular ageing.
recs.abstract: Alcohol-related cardiovascular risk is being fundamentally reappraised. Observational associations suggesting cardioprotection with light-to-moderate drinking have been challenged by contemporary cohort analyses, Mendelian-randomization studies, biomarker-informed investigations, and updated public-health guidance. Uncertainty nevertheless persists at very low exposure levels and for selected coronary or all-cause outcomes. Alcohol is therefore best viewed as a dose-, pattern-, and host-dependent cardiovascular stressor. Acute or binge drinking, sustained heavy intake, chronic intake with episodic binges, and withdrawal produce overlapping but distinct phenotypes, including hypertension, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden death, alcohol-associated cardiomyopathy, heart failure, stroke, and vascular disease. A systems-cardiology framework is presented in which direct myocardial injury, electrical instability, haemodynamic and autonomic stress, vascular and microvascular dysfunction, and disrupted inter-organ signalling interact. Ethanol and acetaldehyde toxicity, redox imbalance, microbial and inflammatory mediators, neurohumoral activation, and metabolic or electrolyte disturbances can impair endothelial signalling, mitochondrial energetics, excitation-contraction coupling, electrical stability, and repair. Pathway dominance varies across exposure patterns and susceptible hosts; coronary microvascular dysfunction may represent a convergence pathway rather than an obligatory mediator. Cumulative injury can diminish perfusion, contractile, electrical, autonomic, and exercise reserve. Alcohol-related cardiovascular ageing is proposed as a unifying cumulative phenotype encompassing mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, inflammageing, senescence, impaired repair, circadian and epigenetic dysregulation, fibrosis, and ventriculo-arterial uncoupling, although direct human evidence remains incomplete. Age, biological sex, genetics, comorbidities, sleep-circadian disruption, nutrition, medications, and polysubstance misuse may modify pathway dominance and reversibility. Structured exposure assessment and alcohol reduction or abstinence, when indicated, are actionable components of cardiovascular prevention and care.

recs.title: Anatomy-Guided Energy Selection With the Sphere-9 Catheter: Implications for Procedural Safety.
Differential half-life of major titin isoforms in normal and remodeling mouse hearts.
Ten commandments for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease.
Heart Failure Presenting With Concurrent Chylothorax and Chylous Ascites Resolved by Revascularization in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: A Case Report and Review.
Peri-aortic fat imaging: a window to vascular ageing.
Effects of Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair on Right Heart Dimension and Function.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has developed as a treatment option for patients experiencing severe tricuspid regurgitation. T-TEER consistently reduces tricuspid regurgitation, but data on subsequent right heart remodeling remain limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate changes in right heart dimension and function after T-TEER using extended echocardiographic follow-up. METHODS: The study was based on the international EuroTR (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation), including patients undergoing T-TEER between 2016 and 2024 at 18 European centers. Eligible were patients with available baseline and follow-up (≥90 days postprocedure) echocardiographic assessment. RESULTS: A total of 699 patients (mean age, 78±8 years; 56% women) were included in the analysis. Echocardiographic follow-up was performed at a median of 407 days (interquartile range, 205-801 days). Right heart dimensions significantly decreased: right ventricular (RV) midventricular diameter from 40.2±8.9 to 37.1±8.4 mm (P<0.001) and end-diastolic area from 28.7±9.0 to 26.2±9.6 cm2 (P<0.001). Procedural success was significantly associated with positive RV remodeling (odds ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.07-3.09]). For RV function, a decline of fractional area change from 37.8%±10.2% to 33.3%±10.1% (P<0.001), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion from 17.4±4.7 to 16.6±4.7 mm (P<0.001) was observed. CONCLUSIONS: In the subset of surviving patients with available echocardiographic follow-up, treatment with T-TEER led to favorable long-term changes with reduced RV dimension, associated with procedural success. RV function modestly decreased, likely reflecting normalization after volume unloading.

recs.title: Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion. RESULTS: Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy. Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

recs.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure. CONCLUSIONS: In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

recs.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. RESULTS: A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099). CONCLUSION: In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

recs.title: A selective vasodilator targeting pericytes reverses capillary no-reflow in ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
Hemodynamic effects of semaglutide in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial.
recs.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide improves symptoms in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) through unclear mechanisms. Here, in this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 81 patients (47 women) with HFpEF and obesity to semaglutide (2.4 mg weekly) or placebo for 52 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in invasively measured pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), a direct measure of cardiac congestion, during low-intensity exercise. Additional mechanistic outcomes included other hemodynamic measures and hemodynamic HFpEF remission (defined as normal PAWP under conditions of both rest and exercise at 52 weeks). At baseline, PAWP was 17.5 ± 4.3 mmHg at rest and 31.7 ± 5.2 mmHg during exercise. After 52 weeks, the mean change in PAWP during exercise was -9.8 (95% confidence interval (CI): -11.3 to -8.2) mmHg with semaglutide and +0.9 (95% CI: -1.3 to 3.0) mmHg with placebo (estimated difference, -10.6 mmHg; 95% CI: -13.3 to -8.0; P < 0.0001). As compared to placebo, semaglutide also decreased resting PAWP (estimated difference, -7.1 mmHg; 95% CI: -9.8 to -4.4; P < 0.0001), and semaglutide-treated patients were more likely to experience hemodynamic remission (53.7% versus 7.4%, odds ratio = 14.1, 95% CI: 3.0-134.6, P < 0.001). The results from this trial indicate that, in patients with HFpEF and obesity, treatment with semaglutide reduced left heart filling pressures during exercise and at rest and was associated with hemodynamic HFpEF remission in over half of treated patients. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05371496 .

recs.title: It Takes a Cell Village to Map Individual Cardiotoxicity Risk.
Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Closure vs Anticoagulation: More Shared Decision-Making or More Randomized Data?
Temporal Changes in Lipoprotein(a) Following Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor generally considered stable over an individual's lifetime. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may transiently alter Lp(a) concentrations, complicating interpretation. We systematically evaluated temporal changes in Lp(a) following ACS. METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review searched MEDLINE and Embase from database inception to February 2026. Eligible studies reported serial Lp(a) measurements at two or more time points after index ACS event. Exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of percent change in mean Lp(a) was performed. RESULTS: Of 3,811 records, 16 studies comprising 1,396 patients met inclusion criteria. Lp(a) demonstrated a dynamic post-ACS trajectory. Using initial post-ACS measurements as the reference, pooled percent change in mean Lp(a) was non-significant at 24 hours post-ACS (+2.5%, 95% CI -6.8 to 11.7; p=0.602). Lp(a) was significantly higher at 7-14 days (+44.0%, 95% CI 4.0-84.1; p=0.031), 1 month (+28.3%, 95% CI 2.7-54.0; p=0.030), and 3-6 months (+22.2%, 95% CI 2.4-42.0; p=0.028). Across two studies, absolute Lp(a) increases >25 nmol/L occurred in 17% and 22% of patients by 3 and 6 months, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Lp(a) is not static post-ACS. Early post-ACS measurements may underestimate long-term concentrations and risk. Repeat measurement weeks to months later is most informative when initial post-ACS Lp(a) values are near clinical decision thresholds or would influence eligibility for emerging Lp(a)-lowering therapies.

Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.
recs.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes. DESIGN: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial. SETTING: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China. PARTICIPANTS: 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume. RESULTS: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

recs.title: Practice changing trials: focus on prevention, heart failure, interventional cardiology, and rehabilitation.
Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI. METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved). RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77). CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

recs.title: Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Electrocardiographic analysis aided by artificial intelligence (AI) may identify atrial electrical vulnerability during sinus rhythm. The objective of this study was to determine whether AI-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) is effective for detecting atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter (AFl), or prespecified pre-AF atrial findings in a randomized trial. METHODS: In this single-center, open-label trial, 14 665 adults 40 to 85 years of age without previous AF/AFl were randomized to an AI-ECG-guided strategy or usual care. Participants randomized to AI-ECG who were then identified by AI as having a high-risk sinus-rhythm ECG in the preceding year were offered Holter monitoring for ≤7 days. Each monitored high-risk intervention participant was paired with an age- and sex-matched control selected before control ECGs underwent AI analysis. Matched controls received identical monitoring to reduce ascertainment bias. Reporting cardiologists were blinded to AI results and randomized assignment. The primary outcome was a composite of newly detected AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings within 90 days. Pre-AF atrial findings comprised frequent premature atrial complexes, short runs of premature atrial complexes, or nonsustained AF/AFl. RESULTS: Among 7337 intervention and 7328 control participants, 84 (1.1%) and 78 (1.1%), respectively, were classified as high risk. Of the 84 high-risk intervention participants, 48 (57.1%) underwent monitoring, as did 48 matched controls. The primary outcome occurred in 54 intervention participants (0.74%) versus 35 control participants (0.48%; odds ratio, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.01-2.37]; P=0.046). Hypothetical reclassification of 1 intervention event to a nonevent changed the primary analysis P value to 0.057. The intervention effect on detection of the primary composite outcome differed by baseline AI-ECG risk (Pinteraction<0.001): 32.1% versus 2.6% among high-risk participants and 0.4% versus 0.5% among low-risk participants. AF/AFl detection (0.3% versus 0.2%) and antiarrhythmic therapy initiation at 180 days (2.3% versus 2.4%) did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. Participant-reported monitoring-related adverse events, including skin reactions and discomfort, occurred in 22.9% of monitored intervention participants versus 18.8% of matched controls. CONCLUSIONS: AI-ECG-guided monitoring resulted in a modest increase in the detection of new AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings. However, these findings were fragile statistically and sensitive to reclassification of 1 event. LATENT (Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development) demonstrates the clinical application of AI-ECG risk stratification to guide targeted rhythm surveillance, providing a foundation for larger trials evaluating its impact on patient outcomes. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06847932.

recs.title: LAAC for Atrial Fibrillation: Overhyped Device or Reasonable Alternative to Oral Anticoagulants?
Liver radiomics on routine cardiac CT identifies hepatic stress states that predict heart failure.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Heart failure (HF) prevention remains limited because early multisystem cardiometabolic dysfunction is not captured by conventional risk tools. We evaluated whether liver radiomic phenotypes derived opportunistically from coronary artery calcium computed tomography (CAC-CT) identify imaging-defined hepatic stress states associated with incident HF. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 59 237 individuals undergoing CAC-CT (CLARIFY: 46 028; Houston Methodist: 13 209). Liver regions were segmented and radiomic features extracted to derive a Liver Radiomics Score (LRS). The model was trained in a CLARIFY derivation cohort (Dtr, n = 9205), validated in a hold-out cohort (Dts, n = 36 823), and externally evaluated in Houston Methodist (Dext, n = 13 209). The mean follow-up was 1411 days (SD 760.1) in the pooled Dtr and Dts cohorts (1144 HF events) and 470 days (SD 596) in Dext (212 HF events). Continuous LRS was associated with incident HF [Dts: hazard ratio (HR) 1.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-1.74; P < 0.001; Dext: HR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P = 0.004] and remained significant after multivariable adjustment in Dts. Increasing LRS quartiles showed progressively adverse hepatic, haemodynamic, and cardiometabolic profiles and higher HF risk. Among 17 806 Dts participants with PREVENT data, adding LRS modestly improved discrimination across CAC- and PREVENT-based models (P < 0.001) and improved reclassification metrics (7-year net reclassification improvement up to 0.25; including integrated discrimination improvement up to 0.015). High LRS identified elevated risk in low-risk groups: among participants with CAC=0, high LRS conferred ∼2.5-fold higher 5-year HF incidence, and ∼2.9-fold in PREVENT-low individuals. CONCLUSION: In this large multicentre cohort, liver radiomics from CAC-CT captured hepatic stress states linked to HF risk and modestly improved risk stratification beyond CAC and PREVENT scores.

Cardiac and vascular involvement in protein misfolding diseases.
recs.abstract: Protein misfolding diseases impose a substantial and often under-recognized burden on both the heart and vasculature. In this Review, we outline how the failure of proteostasis drives oligomer toxicity, amyloid deposition and inflammation in cardiovascular tissues as well as microvascular injury and thrombosis, which culminate in cardiovascular dysfunction. We define the cardiovascular hallmarks of protein misfolding diseases, focusing on transthyretin amyloidosis and immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis, and the disease-specific organ tropisms. We examine neurodegenerative proteinopathies affecting the heart-vascular-brain axis, highlighting how amyloid-β and α-synuclein accumulation contribute to dysautonomia, vascular dysfunction and adverse outcomes. We summarize diagnostic pathways and clinical indicators for early diagnosis of cardiovascular involvement in protein misfolding diseases and review established and emerging biomarkers of vascular stress and proteotoxic load. We also map the current therapeutic landscape for protein misfolding diseases, including strategies to reduce the synthesis of precursor proteins or promote the stabilization of mature proteins as well as fibril-directed therapies, and discuss remaining challenges, such as residual cardiovascular risk, that support the development of mechanism-informed therapeutic approaches. Finally, we propose a research roadmap that prioritizes systematic cardiovascular screening in at-risk populations, harmonized methods for vascular phenotyping, biomarker-anchored mechanistic clinical trials across protein misfolding diseases, and artificial intelligence-based approaches and precision medicine frameworks that integrate genotype or distinct protein conformational strain patterns, organ tropism and dynamic proteostasis measures.

recs.title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR.
