METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs). RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies. CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

recs.title: Impact of Statin and Aspirin Use on Dementia Diagnosis Stratified by Cardiovascular Risk.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia share common risk factors. However, the role of ASCVD prevention therapies in AD dementia prevention is not fully understood. We examined the effect of LLT and antiplatelets with dementia and AD dementia diagnoses across ASCVD risk profiles. METHODS: We used data from primary prevention registry derived from a large healthcare network. Multivariable Cox proportional models were generated to study dementia and AD dementia diagnoses, stratified by ASCVD risk profiles. Impact of aspirin and LLT use on dementia and AD dementia diagnoses was assessed in adjusted models. RESULTS: Among n= 347,128, 2.4% developed dementia and 2.0% developed AD dementia over a median follow-up of 7.94 years. In adjusted models, dementia (HR, 2.59; 95% CI [2.29-2.92]) and AD dementia (HR, 2.85; 95% CI [2.49-3.25]) was higher in high risk patients. Low and high-dose aspirin among high ASCVD risk had lower dementia (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, [0.77-1.00] and HR, 0.83; 95% [CI 0.77-0.90]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.83; 95% CI [0.77-0.91] and HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.73-0.97]). Similarly, moderate- to high-dose LLT use among high ASCVD risk groups was associated with lower dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.79-0.93]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.78-0.93]). CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline ASCVD risk was associated with increased risk of dementia and AD dementia diagnoses. Aspirin and moderate- to high-dose LLT use among patients with high ASCVD risk was associated with lower dementia and AD dementia risk.

recs.title: Percutaneous Pulmonary Thrombectomy for Massive Fat Embolism Syndrome Following Abdominoplasty: The Dark Side of Esthetic Surgery.
Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups. RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

recs.title: Decoding genetic cardiomyopathy through functional phenotyping.
Beyond Sex: Addressing High-Risk Groups with Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy to Improve the Cardiovascular Health of Women.
Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Direct Oral Anticoagulation in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion With Watchman FLX.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion remains uncertain. METHODS: We studied 2817 patients undergoing left atrial appendage occlusion at 8 hospitals from 2016 to 2023 using registry data linked to Medicare claims. Among 2448 Watchman FLX recipients, the primary exposure was time-varying dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) versus pooled direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based therapy. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major bleeding, and device complications. The primary instrumental-variable analysis used operator FLX preference; overlap weighting was secondary and pairwise regimen comparisons exploratory. RESULTS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE (absolute risk difference [ARD], -1.5% [95% CI, -1.9% to -1.0%]; number needed to treat, 67) and major bleeding (ARD -1.6% [95% CI, -2.0% to -0.9%]; number needed to treat, 63) than pooled DOAC-based therapy, without increased device complications. Overlap-weighted associations with MACE and major bleeding were nonsignificant. In exploratory pairwise analyses, DAPT did not differ significantly from DOAC monotherapy for MACE or major bleeding; lower major bleeding was limited to DAPT versus DOAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (ARD, -0.6% [95% CI, -1.1% to -0.2%]; P=0.008). Most estimated benefit accrued within 6 months. CONCLUSIONS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE and major bleeding than pooled DOAC-based therapy after Watchman FLX implantation. The safety benefit was concentrated in the comparison with DOAC + single antiplatelet therapy, whereas DAPT and DOAC monotherapy did not clearly differ in either outcome. These findings support randomized trials comparing DAPT with DOAC monotherapy.

recs.title: Response by Heil et al to Letter Regarding Article, "Artificial Intelligence-Derived Volumetric High-Risk Plaque Features Are Predominantly Located Proximal to Maximal Luminal Stenosis".
Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Dialysis Patients: Insights from a Nationwide Registry Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Trans-radial intervention (TRI) has become the standard of care for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, in patients on dialysis, trans-femoral intervention (TFI) remains predominant to preserve upper-limb vessels for arteriovenous fistula despite heightened hemorrhagic risk. This study aimed to compare TRI and TFI in dialysis patients undergoing PCI. METHODS: We used the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry to compare patients on dialysis who underwent PCIs with TRI versus TFI from January 2018 to June 2025. An instrumental variable analysis with the institutional proportion of TRI use was performed to assess the risk of access-site bleeding and other peri-procedural outcomes. RESULTS: Among 137,702 dialysis patients who underwent PCI, 28.3% of patients underwent TRI (n=38,901), while 71.7% patients underwent TFI (n=98,801). TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding at the access site (adjusted risk difference [aRD]: -0.35%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.56% to -0.15%). Overall bleeding (aRD: -1.38%; 95% CI: -1.89% to -0.87%), access-site hematoma (aRD: -0.86%; 95% CI: -1.13% to -0.60%), myocardial infarction (aRD: -0.21%; 95% CI: -0.39% to -0.03%), and mortality (aRD: -1.07%; 95% CI: -1.64% to -0.51%) were also less frequently observed in TRI. Conversely, TRI was associated with a higher risk of stroke (aRD: 0.23%; 95% CI: 0.001% to 0.45%), driven primarily by ischemic stroke. CONCLUSIONS: TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding events, but the effect size was modest. The higher observed stroke risk highlights a potential ischemic trade-off and warrants further study.

recs.title: Worsening renal function during diuretic therapy: success or failure? A matter of context.
Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: Research Summary.
Coronary angiography in heart transplants from donors older than 40: a Eurotransplant study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The increasing age of heart donors in Europe raises concerns about undetected coronary artery disease (CAD), a contributor to early graft dysfunction and long-term complications. This study examined the association between donor coronary angiography (CA) and heart transplant utilization, particularly in donors aged >40 years. METHODS: A total of 20 681 donor heart offers reported to Eurotransplant between 2004 and 2020 were analysed. The use of CA, donor characteristics, and acceptance rates were assessed. CAD status was imputed for donors without angiography using logistic regression based on clinical risk factors. Transplantation probabilities were modelled using observed and imputed CAD severity to explore potential differences under a scenario of broader CA availability. RESULTS: CA was performed in 23.5% of cases, predominantly in older donors and those with cardiovascular risk factors. Among donors with CA, 37.5% had CAD, which was significantly associated with age, male sex, hypertension, and smoking. Donors with normal CA findings had lower odds of rejection compared with those without CA (odds ratio 0.36, P < .0001). In a counterfactual model, broader CA availability in donors aged >40 years was associated with a higher estimated transplant utilization (56.4%-67.1%), corresponding to a model-based increase of ∼535 transplants. CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.

recs.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: A major challenge in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) care is the identification and management of individuals at risk before disease manifestation. An artificial intelligence (AI) model applied to electrocardiography (ECG) was developed to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype (left ventricular dilatation with systolic dysfunction) and was evaluated for its ability to stratify the risk of incident DCM in familial cohorts. METHODS: A deep learning model was trained to detect the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and to predict its future onset, using more than 330 000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston. Model performance was validated in cohorts from the UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital, and Antwerp University Hospital, and compared with models based on traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits. To assess performance in familial DCM, genetically predisposed individuals identified through cascade screening at the cardiogenetics clinics of Antwerp University Hospital (n = 166, 18% DCM positive) and Maastricht University Medical Center (n = 177, 18% DCM positive) were evaluated. RESULTS: The AI-ECG model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of .87-.97 for diagnosing the prevalent DCM phenotype, outperforming traditional ECG parameters. AI-ECG was comparable to echocardiography for predicting future DCM (C-index .80-.87 and .80-.90, respectively). In familial cohorts, 5-year negative predictive values were 95.5% (Antwerp) and 91.5% (Maastricht), with corresponding positive predictive values of 42.4% and 39.4%, while high-risk scores were associated with a 5.1-6.4-fold increased risk of incident DCM. CONCLUSIONS: The explainable AI-ECG model detects the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and predicts future disease, and supports the exclusion of short- to mid-term disease in genetically at-risk individuals. This low-cost tool could help reduce surveillance burden and facilitate earlier intervention.

recs.title: The Cost of Control in Cardiometabolic Prevention: Insights from Sleep and Circadian Disruption.
Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation revisited: Early entrenchment of AF episodes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 7-day threshold defining persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is clinically entrenched but biologically arbitrary. Whether episode termination follows scale-free dynamics or time-dependent entrenchment remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the probability of spontaneous termination and assess its dependence on episode duration using large-scale pacemaker monitoring. METHODS: Continuous pacemaker monitoring data from the ACaSA study were analyzed. Device-detected AF episodes were reconstructed from daily burden using predefined continuity rules. Termination was modelled as the conditional probability that an ongoing episode would terminate within the subsequent 24 hours. Duration dependence was assessed using a shared frailty Weibull survival model, and episode duration distributions were compared using the Vuong likelihood-ratio test. RESULTS: After excluding patients with single-chamber devices or 100% baseline AF burden, 251 of 281 pacemaker recipients contributed 204,775 patient-days. Device-detected AF occurred in 154 patients, who contributed 7002 reconstructed episodes. Termination probability declined from 91.1% at 1 hour to 72.1% at 12 hours, 33.3% at 24 hours, and 4.3% at 7 days. Episode durations were better described by a lognormal distribution than by a scale-free power-law model. CONCLUSION: Device-detected AF episodes show marked early entrenchment, with spontaneous termination becoming progressively less likely as episode duration increases. These findings support the concept that "AF begets AF" even at short timescales and suggest that persistence beyond 24 hours identifies a state with a substantially reduced likelihood of near-term spontaneous termination. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05127720. GOV ID: NCT05127720.

recs.title: Incremental yield of genetic retesting in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Modern genetic testing in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) includes newly described HCM-associated genes and full intronic regions of certain classic sarcomeric genes. This study evaluated genetic retesting in HCM patients with a prior negative test and identified predictors of a positive result to guide retesting. METHODS: This multicentre study included patients with HCM who previously had negative next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based genetic testing at four centres. Subjects were retested using an updated NGS-based HCM panel. RESULTS: Of 508 retested HCM patients (median age 70 years; 66.9% male; median maximal left ventricular wall thickness 18 mm; median interval from initial genetic test 6.6 years), 46 (9%) had 48 HCM-related variants: 14 in new HCM-associated genes, 3 in deep intronic MYBPC3 regions, 18 intermediate-effect variants, and 13 (8 reclassified) in classic HCM-associated genes. In multivariable analysis, the presence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) [odds ratio (OR) 3.52; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.38-10.25], the Mayo HCM score (OR 1.46 per 1 point increase; 95% CI 1.08-2.01), and the Toronto HCM score (OR 1.18 per 1 point increase; 95% CI 1.08-1.30) were independent predictors of detecting HCM-related variants at retesting. The diagnostic yields in patients with LGE and a high Toronto score (≥13 points), and with LGE and a high Mayo score (≥4 points), were 80% and 50%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HCM and prior negative genetic testing, retesting identified HCM-related variants in 9% of individuals, allowing counselling and risk stratification. Late gadolinium enhancement, combined with the Mayo and Toronto scores, may be used to guide which patients should be prioritized for genetic retesting.

recs.title: Growth of Improper Medicare Payments for Cardiac Procedures: 2018 to 2024.
Seven hundred scientists, one network: inside CIBER-CV.
Cardiovascular outcomes with survodutide in adults with obesity at increased cardiovascular risk (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Survodutide, a glucagon receptor and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, improved markers of cardiometabolic health in people with obesity, but cardiovascular safety for this new class remains to be established. METHODS: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT was a global, phase 3, randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multicentre, event-driven, cardiovascular safety trial conducted at 524 clinical sites in 34 countries. We included participants aged 18 years or older with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater and established cardiovascular disease or at least two obesity complications or risk factors for cardiovascular disease; participants with chronic kidney disease were eligible if they also had a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater. Participants were randomly assigned by interactive response technology (1:1:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide (up-titrated to 3·6 mg or 6·0 mg) or placebo. The primary endpoint was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event (targeting 189 primary endpoint events). We assessed the non-inferiority of pooled survodutide compared with placebo with a margin of 1·65 for the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI of the hazard ratio (HR). Efficacy and safety analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of survodutide or placebo. The primary analysis was performed according to the treatment-regimen estimand, which assessed treatment effects regardless of any early discontinuation of survodutide or placebo, temporary stop, the use of protocol-prohibited obesity medications, or a prolonged dose-escalation period. This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06077864. FINDINGS: From Nov 20, 2023, to Nov 8, 2024, we screened 7753 participants, of whom 5530 (71·3%) participants were recruited and randomly assigned to treatment. 23 (0·4%) participants were not treated; 1836 (33·3%) of 5507 participants received survodutide 3·6 mg, 1835 (33·3%) received 6·0 mg, and 1836 (33·3%) received placebo; 2194 (39·8%) were female, 3313 (60·2%) were male, and 4332 (78·7%) were White. Median time in study was 22·0 months (IQR 20·1-23·7). 1029 (56·0%) in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 1039 (56·6%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg group, and 1083 (59·0%) in the placebo group remained on treatment until study closeout. The primary endpoint occurred in 136 (3·7%) of 3671 participants in the survodutide group and in 76 (4·1%) 1836 participants in the placebo group (HR 0·89 [95% CI 0·67-1·18; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Adverse events occurred in 1708 (93·0%) of 1836 participants with survodutide 3·6 mg, 1708 (93·1%) of 1835 with survodutide 6·0 mg, and 1571 (85·6%) of 1836 with placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with survodutide than in the placebo group (nausea occurred in 882 [48·0%] of 1836 participants in the 3·6 mg group and 900 [49·0%] of 1835 in the 6·0 mg group vs 223 [12·1%] of 1836 in the placebo group, and vomiting occurred in 582 [31·7%] participants in the 3·6 mg group and 623 [34·0%] in the 6·0 mg group vs 89 [4·8%] in the placebo group). Gastrointestinal adverse events leading to treatment discontinuations occurred in 354 (19·3%) participants in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 (20·8%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 34 (1·9%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates across treatment groups (413 [22·5%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 [20·8%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 439 [23·9%] in the placebo group). Fatal adverse events were similar across treatment groups (16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 11 [0·6%] in the placebo group) and were primarily due to cardiac disorders (six [0·3%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, seven [0·4%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and six [0·3%] in the placebo group). INTERPRETATION: In participants with obesity with established cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease or at increased risk of cardiovascular disease, survodutide was not associated with increased risk for the primary composite endpoint of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event compared with placebo. This cardiovascular safety trial provides clinicians with reassuring data that treatment with survodutide, a novel glucagon receptor-GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, is not associated with increased cardiovascular risk. FUNDING: Boehringer Ingelheim.

recs.title: Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question. METHODS: Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered. RESULTS: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month. CONCLUSIONS: In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

recs.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited. METHODS: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group). The primary outcome was survival until hospital discharge. RESULTS: A total of 144 patients were included in the intervention group, and 87 were included in the conventional group. In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002). At 6 months, a favorable neurologic outcome was reported in 51 of 141 patients (36%) in the intervention group and in 11 of 85 patients (13%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 4.22; 95% CI, 2.82 to 6.32). There were 32 adverse events in the intervention group and 11 in the conventional group. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

recs.title: What Counts in a Stroke-Prevention Strategy?: A Patient-Centered Framework for Cardiovascular Care in Atrial Fibrillation.
Adeno-Associated Virus-Induced Humanized Hypertensive Mouse Model Validates N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Angiotensinogen as a Long-Acting Antihypertensive Therapy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, yet current therapeutic strategies lack sustained efficacy and long-term stability. Our study aimed to construct a humanized rodent model for drugs development especially currently prevalent small interfering RNA medication. METHODS: A humanized hypertensive mouse model was generated by subcutaneous injection of neonatal mice with adeno-associated viruses encoding hAGT (human angiotensinogen) and hRENIN (human renin). Blood pressure was monitored weekly via tail-cuff plethysmography. Expression of hAGT and hRENIN was assessed by ELISA, Western blot, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at 4 and 6 months postinjection. Hypertension-associated comorbidities were examined through histological analysis and ELISA. A modified N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA targeting human hepatic AGT (GalNAc-siAGT) was screened and subcutaneously administered to humanized hypertensive mice, either alone or in combination with valsartan, to evaluate therapeutic efficacy. RESULTS: The dual adeno-associated virus-induced humanized hypertensive model exhibited a sustained hypertension for 6 months and manifested prevalent comorbidities, including heart failure and kidney disease. This modified GalNAc-siAGT demonstrated significant activity in knocking down hAGT both in vitro and in vivo. Only a single subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siAGT in humanized hypertensive mice led to a sustained reduction in blood pressure lasting for 2 months, accompanied by cardio- and renoprotective effects. Moreover, combining GalNAc-siAGT with the renin-angiotensin system blocker, valsartan, significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy. CONCLUSIONS: Our study validated the antihypertensive therapeutic effect of GalNAc-siAGT in a humanized hypertensive murine model while highlighting the translational potential of this model for clinical drug development.

recs.title: Aging Populations and the Rising Burden of Cardiovascular Disease.
Variability of lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction between admission, discharge, and follow-up.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Using Lp(a) concentrations measured during stable follow-up as the reference, we aimed to assess the temporal variability of Lp(a) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to explore a pragmatic strategy for Lp(a) measurement. METHODS AND RESULTS: The FRENCHIE-Lp(a) cohort enrolled consecutive adults hospitalized for AMI in 21 centres. Lp(a) mass concentration, measured at admission, hospital discharge, and 3-12 months follow-up, was analysed both as a continuous and predefined categorical variable (≤20, >20-≤50, >50-≤70, >70 mg/dL). Assuming follow-up Lp(a) as the reference, we aimed to identify the threshold values that would allow us to accurately identify patients with Lp(a) > 70mg/dL, the threshold mostly used for patient selection in phase III trials of targeted Lp(a) therapies. A cumulative threshold analysis was performed to identify the Lp(a) value below which the misclassification rate (i.e. % of patients with follow-up Lp(a) > 70 mg/dL) remained <1%. Among 1561 patients (aged 61 ± 12 years; 21.3% women), median Lp(a) was 13 mg/dL at admission and remained stable over time (median difference overtime = 0 mg/dL). However, only 68.5% of patients remained in the same Lp(a) category overtime. In patients with discharge-Lp(a) ≤37 mg/dL (72.5% of the population), only 0.97% had Lp(a) >70 mg/dL at follow-up compared to 39.9% of those with discharge-Lp(a) >37 mg/dL. CONCLUSION: Although the median Lp(a) level remained stable between admission and follow-up, one-third of AMI patients shifted within Lp(a) categories over time. Pending external validation, an exploratory two-step strategy based on Lp(a) measurement at discharge, followed by repeat testing in patients with Lp(a) >37 mg/dL, showed a misclassification rate below 1% for identifying patients potentially needing intervention. REGISTRATION: Clinical trial Number: NCT04050956.

recs.title: T wave changes during ventricular premature beats: what is the cause?
A transient modified mRNA encoding Myc and cyclin T1 improves cardiac function after myocardial injury.
recs.abstract: Myc is an evolutionarily conserved transcription factor that is necessary for the restoration of tissues in multiple regenerative species. The adult mammalian heart lacks regenerative capacity and cardiomyocytes fail to divide following damage-induced signaling. Transgenic expression of Myc and cyclin T1 can drive substantial adult cardiomyocyte proliferation to replace lost cardiomyocytes. Here, using transgenic models and a prototypical mRNA therapeutic, we show that Myc and cyclin T1 require transient induction for cardiomyocyte proliferation that leads to myocardial repair and functional recovery after myocardial infarction in mice. This research provides a strategy to translate Myc-cyclin T1 coexpression for cardiac regeneration to address serious unmet needs in the treatment of cardiovascular disease.

recs.title: Association of Clonal Hematopoiesis With Total and Cause-Specific Mortality Among Older Women.
Efficacy of empagliflozin in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction according to the presence of echocardiographic features of diastolic dysfunction in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial.
recs.abstract: AIMS: To define the impact of diastolic dysfunction (DD) on the response to empagliflozin treatment in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS AND RESULTS: Diastolic dysfunction was defined by left atrial volume index ≥34 ml/m2, the ratio of early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular tissue velocity (E/e) ≥ 13 or left ventricular mass index >115 (males) or >95 (females). We created three categories of increasing DD (0, 1, or ≥2 DD criteria at baseline) to describe the effect of DD on response to empagliflozin therapy and adverse effects. Of 5988 patients in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial, 3766 (63%) had no documented baseline DD, 1619 (27%) had one, and 603 (10%) had two or more measures. Baseline DD was associated with sex, race, ethnicity, and region and was more common with lower heart rate, DBP, body weight, and eGFR. Despite baseline DD not being significantly associated with the primary endpoint of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death within the placebo group, a progressive treatment effect across the three DD categories was seen (trend test P-value .0014), with estimated hazard ratios of empagliflozin vs placebo of 0.91 (none present), 0.64 (1 present), and 0.49 (≥2). A significant treatment-by-subgroup trend test was also observed for the total number of hospitalizations for heart failure. Both Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improvement at week 52 and safety profile were consistent across DD categories. CONCLUSION: Baseline detection of echocardiographic DD predicted improved clinical response to empagliflozin in a graded fashion, but the reasons cannot be reliably determined from this analysis.

recs.title: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
recs.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain. DESIGN: Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. SETTING: 15 thoracic centres in the UK. PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023. INTERVENTIONS: Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications. RESULTS: 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise. CONCLUSIONS: Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03677856.

recs.title: Reinitiation of Optimal Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy After Coronary Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke. METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone. RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70). CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

recs.title: Vascular Phenotypes and Recurrent Arterial Events After Nontraumatic Cervical Artery Dissection.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic cervical artery dissection (CeAD) is often approached as a localized cervicocranial vascular disorder, although overlap with fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) and other arteriopathies suggests broader vascular disease. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to determine whether head-to-pelvis imaging identifies clinically meaningful vascular phenotypes after nontraumatic CeAD and whether these phenotypes are associated with recurrent arterial events. METHODS: Consecutive adults with CeAD evaluated in an institutional vascular medicine clinic underwent head-to-pelvis computed tomography and/or magnetic resonance angiography. Patients were classified as isolated CeAD, FMD-associated CeAD (FMD-CeAD), or multiple artery aneurysm and dissection without FMD (MAAD). Outcomes were recurrent CeAD and incident extracervical artery dissection. RESULTS: Among 315 patients, 136 (43.2%) had isolated CeAD, 100 (31.7%) had FMD-CeAD, and 79 (25.1%) had MAAD-CeAD. Overall, 179 patients (56.8%) had systemic vascular abnormalities, and 125 (39.7%) had findings below the neck. Recurrent CeAD was most frequent in isolated CeAD. Incident extracervical artery dissection occurred most frequently in MAAD-CeAD. Isolated CeAD was associated with recurrent CeAD compared with FMD-CeAD (HR: 3.26; 95% CI: 1.43 to 7.43). Among patients with FMD-CeAD or MAAD-CeAD, MAAD-CeAD was associated with incident extracervical artery dissection after adjustment for age at index CeAD (HR: 3.75; 95% CI: 1.17-12.00; P = 0.026), with similar results after additional adjustment for baseline aneurysm. CONCLUSIONS: Head-to-pelvis imaging identified frequent extracervical vascular abnormalities in patients with CeAD and phenotypes with distinct recurrent-event patterns. These findings support a cardiovascular arteriopathy framework for CeAD and provide a rationale for prospective studies of phenotype-guided imaging, genetic evaluation, counseling, and surveillance.

recs.title: Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Closure Device Utilization Among Medicare Beneficiaries.
Early Change in Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain and Long-Term Cardiovascular Outcomes in Fabry Disease: A Prognostic Tool for Enzyme Replacement Therapy.
Left ventricular arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy presenting as a "hot phase" mimicking acute myocarditis.
Comparison of Outcomes Between Men and Women Treated With Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Oral Anticoagulation After Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: An OPTION Subanalysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Women sex is an established, nonmodifiable risk factor for adverse outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has been proposed as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with AF; however, there are limited data on sex-based outcomes of LAAC following catheter ablation. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare outcomes of LAAC vs OAC after AF ablation in men and women. METHODS: Patients with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 in men and ≥3 in women were randomized 1:1 to either ablation + LAAC or ablation + OAC. The primary safety endpoint was nonprocedural major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding at 36 months. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, or systemic embolism at 36 months. RESULTS: The study included 1,053 men and 546 women. LAAC and OAC demonstrated comparable primary efficacy events in men (HR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.56-1.65; P = 0.88) and women (HR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.41-1.62; P = 0.55), with no treatment-by-sex interaction (P interaction = 0.71). Procedural complication rates were similar at 2.3% in men and 3.7% in women with only 1 pericardial effusion in each group, not related to the index LAAC procedure. At 36 months, the primary safety endpoint was significantly lower in the device group among men (HR: 0.34; 95% CI: 0.23-0.50; P < 0.0001). In women, a similar but nonsignificant trend was observed (HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.42-1.09; P = 0.11), with a significant treatment-by-sex interaction (P interaction = 0.02). No significant difference was seen in the secondary safety endpoint across both treatment arms for either sex. CONCLUSIONS: In this prespecified analysis of the OPTION (Comparison of Anticoagulation With Left Atrial Appendage Closure After AF Ablation [OPTION]) trial, stroke, systemic embolism, and mortality outcomes were not significantly different between LAAC and OAC following AF ablation in either men or women. Compared with OAC, LAAC demonstrated a greater magnitude of major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding reduction in men as compared with women. (Comparison of Anticoagulation With Left Atrial Appendage Closure After AF Ablation [OPTION]; NCT03795298).

recs.title: Advanced Age in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock by Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Status.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although advanced age is associated with worse outcomes, associations across out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) strata remain incompletely characterized. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between octogenarian status and in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI-related CS (AMI-CS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to examine this association in analyses stratified by OHCA status. METHODS: We analyzed patients with AMI-CS enrolled in the multicenter Kanagawa-ACuTe cardIoVascular rEgistry who underwent PCI. Octogenarian status (≥80 years) was the primary exposure. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with in-hospital mortality, with additional analyses stratified by OHCA status. RESULTS: Among 658 patients, 177 (26.9%) were octogenarians, and 279 (42.4%) died during hospitalization. Octogenarian status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.32-3.48; P = 0.002). In stratified analyses, octogenarian status was associated with higher mortality among patients without OHCA, whereas no statistically significant association was observed among those with OHCA. The interaction between octogenarian status and OHCA was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.422). Higher heart rate, unmeasurable heart rate, higher serum creatinine, and lower serum albumin were independently associated with mortality. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.

recs.title: Cardiac electrophysiology procedures must be performed exclusively by trained electrophysiologists: A statement from the Heart Rhythm Society and Heart Rhythm Advocates.
recs.abstract: The exponential growth of clinical cardiac electrophysiology (CCEP) as a subspecialty has created an important unresolved question in contemporary cardiovascular medicine: Who is qualified to perform electrophysiology (EP) procedures? As nonelectrophysiologists increasingly perform procedures that require the nuanced expertise of a trained or board-certified CCEP (eg, permanent pacemaker implantation, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation, cardiac resynchronization therapy, and transvenous lead extraction), the consequences for patient safety, procedural outcomes, and health system efficiency have become impossible to ignore. This article presents a comprehensive, evidence-based argument that cardiac EP procedures must be performed exclusively by physicians who have completed accredited fellowship training in CCEP. We draw upon peer-reviewed outcome data, guideline-derived training standards from the Heart Rhythm Society, the American College of Cardiology, and American Heart Association, including the newly published 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/Heart Rhythm Society Advanced Training Statement on Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology, as well as registry analyses spanning hundreds of thousands of patients to substantiate our position. The risks associated with suboptimal operator training are not theoretical; they are measurable, costly, and potentially fatal. The evidence presented demonstrates that operator specialization in EP is among the most powerful independent predictors of procedural safety and long-term outcomes and can be as important as institutional volume in many analyses. We call upon hospital credentialing committees, national medical societies, payers, regulatory bodies, and policymakers worldwide to establish and enforce a definitive standard: only trained CCEPs should implant and manage cardiac implantable electronic devices, perform catheter ablation procedures, execute transvenous lead extraction, and conduct formal EP studies.

recs.title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction. METHODS: This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates. RESULTS: Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

recs.title: SUDDEN CARDIAC ARREST IN NEW SOUTH WALES (NSW), AUSTRALIA: A DATA LINKAGE STUDY.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a global health challenge. Routinely collected health data represents a potential source of data to identify SCA. OBJECTIVE: Evaluate whether routinely collected health data can retrospectively identify community-based SCA (1-50 years) in NSW. METHODS: Potential SCA cases (aged 1-50yrs; occurring in NSW; cardiac-related ICD-9/10/SNOMED codes) were identified by the Centre for Health Record Linkage (CHeReL) in the NSW Ambulance OHCA Register (OHCAR) and NSW Emergency Department Data Collection (EDDC). Probabilistic data linkage was undertaken between ambulance, hospital and mortality datasets. External causes were excluded at case identification in ambulance records. Cardiac aetiology was assigned where a cardiac diagnosis appeared in hospital admission or cause of death records. RESULTS: From 1.7 million linked records, 13,345 presumed SCA cases were identified; 54% had cardiac aetiology and 83% were fatal. Cardiac cases were older than non-cardiac cases (median 42 vs 37 years, p < 0.001) and more likely to be admitted to hospital (58% vs 7%, p < 0.001). Within cardiac cases, rhythm-related and structural diagnoses dominated in 1-11 year olds, while ischaemic disease dominated in 35-50 year olds. Older cardiac cases were more likely to die pre-hospital (adjusted OR 3.56, 95% CI 2.66-4.85, for 35-50 vs 1-11 years). CONCLUSIONX: Multi-source administrative data linkage identifies age-related patterns in SCA aetiology and clinical trajectory. Findings extrapolated nationally suggest approximately 370 cardiac SCA deaths per year in Australians aged 1 to 35, a substantial burden that could be tracked through routine data linkage.

recs.title: Leaders in Cardiology: Charalambos Antoniades.
Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
recs.abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation's largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non-Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.

recs.title: Continuous Rhythm Monitoring and CIED Use in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement.
Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Review.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Acute ischemic stroke, caused by thrombotic or embolic occlusion of a cervical or cerebral artery, leads to neurologic injury due to sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain. Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death and accounts for about 85% of strokes in the US. OBSERVATIONS: Symptoms of acute ischemic stroke vary based on the area of the affected brain. Common presentations include sudden arm or leg weakness, aphasia or slurred speech, sudden loss of balance or coordination, sudden visual difficulties, and/or facial drooping. Patients with suspected stroke should be transported to the nearest emergency department for urgent brain imaging, typically noncontrast computed tomography (CT). Based on 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines, first-line therapy for patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5 hours from symptom onset with disabling symptoms (eg, affecting the ability to perform activities of daily living) is intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase) in those without intracranial hemorrhage or other contraindications to thrombolysis. The treatment window can be extended to 9 hours-and up to 24 hours in patients with large vessel occlusion (eg, involving the internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery [M1 segment]) who are unable to receive thrombectomy-based on identification of salvageable tissue using perfusion imaging with CT perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging. In appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, pooled randomized trial data show an approximately 10% absolute increase in the probability of a better functional outcome with intravenous thrombolysis. Based on 2026 AHA/ASA guidelines, endovascular thrombectomy, which involves clot removal with an intra-arterial mechanical device, is recommended for patients with large vessel occlusion within 6 hours of stroke onset (class 1 recommendation) and is recommended in selected patients with large vessel occlusion within 24 hours of last known well (class 1 recommendation). Endovascular therapy should be performed after intravenous thrombolysis unless patients have contraindications to thrombolytic therapy. Compared with medical management, which includes intravenous thrombolysis when indicated, endovascular thrombectomy produces an approximately 20% absolute increase in functional independence. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Acute ischemic stroke causes substantial disability and mortality. First-line therapy for patients with disabling acute stroke symptoms is intravenous thrombolysis (if no contraindications) within 4.5 hours of stroke onset and up to 24 hours in carefully selected patients not receiving mechanical thrombectomy; for large vessel occlusions, mechanical thrombectomy may be performed up to 24 hours after stroke onset in eligible patients.

recs.title: Catheter Ablation in Atrial Fibrillation With Prior Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack: Insights From the CABANA Trial.
Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle. INTERVENTION: ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time. RESULTS: Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877.

recs.title: Tirofiban Prevents Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in Aged Mice.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Microthrombi formation in the cerebral microvasculature has been demonstrated in animal models of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) as well as autopsy studies of patients with aneurysmal SAH, and microthrombi are thought to contribute to delayed cerebral ischemia and poor neurological outcomes. Our hypothesis was that treatment with tirofiban, an antiplatelet drug that inhibits glycoprotein IIb/IIIa, would reduce microthrombi formation and the subsequent sequalae, delayed cerebral ischemia, in aged mice. METHODS: SAH was induced via endovascular perforation in male mice, and blood injection in female mice, followed by treatment with either tirofiban or saline. Mice underwent daily neurological assessment for 6 days and then were euthanized. Magnetic resonance imaging scans were obtained on days 2, 4, and 6 after SAH to identify infarcted tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging perfusion and laser speckle contrast imaging were performed to evaluate cerebral perfusion. Postmortem microthrombi formation in the cerebral microvascular was quantified. RESULTS: Tirofiban treatment in male mice, compared with saline, led to reduced microthrombi formation, and prevented delayed infarct growth and neurological decline. In female mice, significant neurobehavioral improvements were observed, which corresponded with fewer brain microthrombi. No female mice had infarction, nor was delayed cerebral ischemia detected in any female mouse. CONCLUSIONS: After SAH in mice, treatment with tirofiban reduces both cerebral microthrombi formation and delayed infarct growth leading to a subsequent improvement in neurological outcomes.

recs.title: Vasodilation in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: right patient, right time?
Endothelial KLK8 Promotes Diabetic Nephropathy via a LIFR Dependent Mechanism.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The molecular pathways in endothelial cells (ECs) in diabetic nephropathy (DN), a primary microvascular complication of diabetes, remain unclear. Tissue KLKs (kallikrein-related peptidases) participate in pathophysiological processes in ECs. We aimed to explore the roles of endothelial KLKs in DN and define the underlying mechanisms. METHODS AND RESULTS: Renal KLK8 was the most highly upregulated KLK in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice and cultured glomerular ECs (GECs) upon high glucose treatment. C57/BL6 background global (Klk8-/-) and endothelial Klk8 knockout (Klk8ΔEC) mice, as well as DBA/2J mice with endothelial Klk8 knockdown, displayed improved albuminuria, mesangial matrix expansion, and glomerulosclerosis caused by streptozotocin compared with the corresponding wild-type mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing showed that many pathways linked to DN in ECs, mesangial cells, and tubule cells were reversed in Klk8ΔEC mice. Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition caused by streptozotocin was extensively improved in Klk8ΔEC mice, which was confirmed in Cdh5CreERT2+/--mT/mG+/- mice with endothelial Klk8 knockdown. Proteome coupled with other approaches revealed that KLK8 cleaved SDC4 (syndecan-4), which contributed to the loss of glycocalyx integrity in GECs during DN progress. Lifr was one of the key genes in ECs and mesangial cells regulated by endothelial Klk8 during DN progress. Endothelial KLK8 upregulated LIFR (leukemia inhibitory factor receptor) expression through PLC (phospholipase C)/ERK (extracellular signal-regulated kinase)/RUNX1 (runt-related transcription factor)1 pathways, and upregulated LIFR contributed to high glucose-induced GEC dysfunction and MC activation. Knockdown of Lifr ameliorated hallmark features of DN and improved endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and SDC4 expression in the glomeruli of diabetic mice. LIFR was upregulated in GECs and mesangial cells in patients with DN. Circulatory LIF (leukemia inhibitory factor), KLK8 and soluble SDC4 levels were increased in patients with DN, and KLK8 level was positively correlated with LIF, soluble SDC4 and creatinine levels. CONCLUSIONS: Endothelial KLK8 promotes GEC dysfunction and abnormal crosstalk with mesangial cells through a LIFR-dependent signaling in DN, which immediately highlights therapeutic targets for DN.

recs.title: Multiple Traumas Accelerate the Transition From Cardiovascular Disease to Depression: A Multistate Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumas are risk factors for both cardiovascular disease (CVD) and depression. However, the specific impacts of trauma on the critical transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression and mortality remain scarce. METHODS: Using data from the UK Biobank cohort (N=138 036), we constructed multistate models to investigate the associations of childhood trauma, adult trauma, and lifetime trauma with the transitions between health states. Specifically, we modeled transitions from a healthy state to incident CVD, further to subsequent depression, and ultimately to death. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 14 278 participants developed incident CVD, with 679 developed subsequent depression and 4144 dying. Trauma was positively associated with the dynamic disease progression: the transition from baseline to incident CVD showed significantly elevated hazards for multiple childhood traumas (hazard ratio [HR], 1.294 [95% CI, 1.170-1.432]), adult traumas (HR, 1.145 [95% CI, 1.071-1.225]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.632 [95% CI, 1.528-1.742]) compared with no trauma exposure. Similarly, the transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression demonstrated increased risks for multiple childhood traumas (HR, 2.260 [95% CI, 1.661-3.075]), adult traumas (HR, 1.950 [95% CI, 1.510-2.518]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.608 [95% CI, 1.245-2.078]) versus no trauma exposure. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that exposure to multiple traumas significantly increases the risk of developing depression following an incident CVD diagnosis. This underscores the urgent need for clinical and public health interventions targeting multiple traumas to mitigate the risk of CVD and depression progression, thereby improving outcomes.

recs.title: Effects of Sotatercept on Cardiac Structure and Function in Combined Post- and Precapillary Pulmonary Hypertension in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: Analysis of the CADENCE Study.
Evaluating the Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Paradox in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia is an established cardiovascular risk factor. However, studies in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed an association between low low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and increased mortality, termed the "LDL-C paradox." This study examined the impact of LDL-C on clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF and identify distinct hypocholesterolemia subgroups using latent class analysis. METHODS: Consecutive patients with HFrEF (left ventricular EF <40%) from national registries (2016-2022) were stratified by LDL-C quartiles, with the lowest quartile ≤1.73 mmol/L. Latent class analysis was performed to identify subsets of patients in the lowest quartile. Outcomes included 1-year all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, readmission, and composite end points. RESULTS: Among 2188 patients, the lowest LDL-C quartile had higher 1-year all-cause mortality than Quartile 2 and 3 (P<0.05) but not Quartile 4, with no intergroup differences in cardiovascular mortality, readmissions, or composite outcomes between groups. Latent class analysis identified 2 hypocholesterolemia subgroups: pathological and nonpathological hypocholesterolemia. The pathological subgroup was older, lower weight, with higher comorbidity burden. Compared with patients with hypercholesterolemia, the pathological hypocholesterolemia subgroup had higher 1-year all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.14 [95% CI, 1.17-2.69], P<0.001), cardiovascular mortality (adjusted HR, 1.93 [95% CI, 1.46-2.54], P<0.001), and composite end points (adjusted HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.01-1.30], P=0.037), and the subgroup with nonpathological hypocholesterolemia showed comparable outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: A distinct subset of patients with HFrEF with low LDL-C demonstrates different clinical characteristics (older and higher comorbidity burden) and poorer outcomes, potentially elucidating the "LDL-C paradox" cause in patients with HFrEF.

recs.title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies. METHODS: In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. RESULTS: The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (Pinteraction=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups. CONCLUSIONS: Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04626973.

recs.title: BPR-30901649, An Angiotensinogen-Targeting Small Interfering RNA, Achieves Ultra-Durable Target Silencing and Sustained Blood Pressure Reduction Through 20 Weeks in Hypertensive Non-Human Primates.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension affects over 1.3 billion adults worldwide, and poor adherence to daily oral therapy contributes to inadequate blood pressure (BP) control. We characterized BPR-30901649, a liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) against angiotensinogen (AGT), hypothesizing that its optimized design would confer greater potency and durability than an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark. METHODS: BPR-30901649 was selected through in vitro and in vivo screening in HepG2 cells and human AGT (hAGT) transgenic mice. Off-target risk was assessed by RNA sequencing in primary human hepatocytes. Pharmacodynamics were evaluated in hAGT mice after single and repeat subcutaneous (SC) dosing, and in hypertensive cynomolgus monkeys given a single SC dose of 1.5 or 3.0 mg/kg, with serum AGT and systolic BP (SBP) monitored for 20 weeks. Investigational New Drug (IND)-enabling toxicology was conducted in rats and nonhuman primates (NHPs). RESULTS: RNA sequencing indicated low off-target risk. In hAGT mice, BPR-30901649 produced significantly deeper serum AGT knockdown than the benchmark. In hypertensive NHPs, a single SC injection produced rapid, dose-dependent, and sustained AGT suppression; at week 20, SBP remained reduced by 14.2% (20.3 mm Hg) and 17.3% (25.3 mm Hg) in the low- and high-dose groups, respectively. In repeat-dose toxicology, the no-observed-adverse-effect level was 100 mg/kg in NHPs. CONCLUSIONS: BPR-30901649 surpassed an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark in vivo and showed a wide preclinical safety margin, supporting its clinical development as a potential twice-yearly therapy for hypertension.

recs.title: Syncope with right bundle branch block without left hemiblock: lower risk, but not benign.
Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results. METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points. RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

recs.title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 is hypothesized to be a therapeutic target for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Whether neutralizing interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab, a monoclonal antibody, reduces the risk of adverse cardiovascular events remains unknown. METHODS: We conducted a multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation (defined by a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [CRP] level of ≥2 mg per liter). Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ziltivekimab (15 mg once monthly) or placebo.
