The primary efficacy end point was a 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). This composite end point included death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke. RESULTS: A total of 6376 patients were included in the full analysis population: 3184 were assigned to receive ziltivekimab and 3192 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 69.4 years, and 27.5% were women. At 24 months, the between-group difference in the median percent change in the levels of inflammatory biomarkers among patients receiving ziltivekimab as compared with those receiving placebo was -76 percentage points for free interleukin-6 and -64 percentage points for high-sensitivity CRP. During a median follow-up of 33 months, a primary end-point event occurred in 561 patients (17.6%) in the ziltivekimab group and in 565 patients (17.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.11; P = 0.84). Serious adverse events occurred in 54.6% of the patients in the ziltivekimab group and in 54.8% of those in the placebo group; serious infections occurred in 20.4% and 17.9%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation, a strategy of lowering interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab did not result in a lower risk of cardiovascular events than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; ZEUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05021835.).

recs.title: ANGPTL4 Inhibition in Adults with Elevated Triglyceride Levels.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) inhibits lipoprotein lipase and regulates triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism. MAR001 is a monoclonal antibody against ANGPTL4 that is being evaluated for lowering triglyceride levels. METHODS: We conducted a two-part, phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. In part A, the focus of this report, we enrolled adults who had a nonfasting triglyceride level of at least 175 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 35 mg per deciliter at initial screening, followed by a fasting triglyceride level of at least 150 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 30 mg per deciliter on confirmatory screening. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive MAR001 at a dose of 300, 450, or 900 mg or matching placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 24 weeks. The primary end point was the percent change from baseline in the fasting triglyceride level at week 12, reported as the difference between each MAR001 dose group and the placebo group (placebo-adjusted change). RESULTS: A total of 236 participants were enrolled in the trial, with 177 assigned to receive MAR001 and 59 to receive placebo; a total of 235 participants received at least one dose of MAR001 or placebo and were included in the primary efficacy analyses. The mean age of the participants was 60.4 years, and 39% were women. The median triglyceride level at baseline was 249.5 mg per deciliter (interquartile range, 210.0 to 313.0). At week 12, in an intention-to-treat analysis, the placebo-adjusted least-squares mean percent changes in the fasting triglyceride level were -39.1 percentage points, -40.5 percentage points, and -45.3 percentage points for the 300-mg, 450-mg, and 900-mg doses, respectively (P<0.001 for all comparisons). Adverse events occurred in 123 of 177 participants (69%) in the pooled MAR001 group and in 45 of 58 participants (78%) in the placebo group. CONCLUSIONS: Inhibition of ANGPTL4 with MAR001 significantly reduced fasting triglyceride levels at 12 weeks. (Funded by Marea Therapeutics; TYDAL-TIMI 78 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT07028749.).

recs.title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer.
recs.abstract: Flower-Win/Lose signaling underlies a tumor-host fitness conflict in ovarian cancer, in which tumor-derived exosomal Tu-stroma reduces the fitness of surrounding host cells, favoring tumor expansion within host tissues. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most prevalent histotype of epithelial ovarian cancer and leading cause of ovarian-cancer-related mortality, arises from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), a noninvasive precursor typically identifiable only by histopathologic examination of excised fallopian tube tissue. Here we evaluated Tu-stroma, a tumor-associated long noncoding RNA enriched in serum extracellular vesicles (EVs), as a circulating biomarker in STIC and early-stage HGSC, representing the earliest histopathologically defined phases of disease. Tu-stroma was quantified in serum EVs from 506 individuals with histologically normal adnexa, benign-adnexal lesions, isolated STIC and HGSC across International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stages I-IV. Normalized EV Tu-stroma ΔCT values were elevated in STIC (n = 43) and HGSC (n = 232) versus controls (n = 143) and benign-adnexal lesions (n = 88), including premenopausal women (controls = 57, benign = 34, STIC = 32, HGSC = 88). In paired receiver operating characteristic analyses, Tu-stroma showed higher discrimination than cancer antigen 125 (CA125) for STIC versus controls (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.99 versus 0.59, P < 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.99 versus 0.31, P < 0.001), and for HGSC versus controls (AUC = 0.99 versus 0.96, P = 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.98 versus 0.84, P < 0.001). Tu-stroma showed no systematic elevation across inflammatory or physiologic comparators (n = 116) or nonovarian malignancies (n = 160), each assessed against healthy controls (n = 100), supporting disease-context specificity. Modeled risk-enriched contexts yielded predictive values compatible with intended-use populations. These findings identify Tu-stroma as a candidate EV-RNA marker associated with pre-invasive and early HGSC biology. Prospective evaluation in consecutively enrolled real-world cohorts is required to validate diagnostic performance, predictive value and clinical utility.

Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease in a Primary Care Population of Young Adults by Disaggregated Race and Ethnicity.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States, with well-documented racial and ethnic disparities. Data are limited on incidence among patients aged <50 years, particularly within disaggregated Asian and Hispanic subgroups and individuals identifying with multiple racial or ethnic groups. We estimated CVD incidence rates for these groups and assessed whether disparities are explained by other clinical and demographic risk factors. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Sutter Health Electronic Health Record data (2010-2024) for adults aged 18 to 49 years with at least 2 primary care visits and a 2-year observed baseline period free of CVD. Incident CVD was defined as myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. We estimated incidence rates, applied age and sex standardization, and fit Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for additional risk factors. RESULTS: In a cohort of 1 178 551 patients, incidence was 1.14 cases per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 1.12-1.17). After standardization, Pacific Islander individuals (hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 2.29-3.52]) and non-Hispanic Black individuals (HR, 2.82 [95% CI, 2.58-3.06]) had the highest incidence. Within the Asian group, Filipino individuals had the highest incidence (HR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.42-1.79]). Hispanic subgroups showed less heterogeneity. Elevated HRs persisted among some groups after adjustment with Cox models. CONCLUSIONS: Young adult CVD incidence varied across racial and ethnic subgroups. Elevated risk persisted in several groups after adjustment, consistent with the influence of unmeasured social drivers. These findings support collection of granular racial and ethnic data and validation of existing risk prediction tools in young adult subgroups.

recs.title: Dapagliflozin for Renal Protection in Heart Transplant Recipients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Progressive kidney disease is common in heart transplant recipients due to calcineurin inhibitor exposure and pre-existing comorbidities. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors may attenuate the decline in kidney function, but evidence in heart transplant recipients is limited. METHODS: The DAPAgliflozin for Renal protection in Heart Transplant recipients (DAPARHT) trial is a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted at six heart transplant centers in Northern Europe. We randomized adult heart transplant recipients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥25 mL/min/1.73 m² at least one year after transplantation 1:1 to receive dapagliflozin 10 mg or matching placebo once daily. The primary endpoint was the slope of the eGFR from 2 weeks after treatment initiation to the end of the 12-month blinded treatment period. RESULTS: Between June 2022 and September 2025, we randomized 430 participants, of whom 217 were allocated to dapagliflozin and 213 were allocated to placebo. We included the 424 patients with at least one eGFR measurement after baseline in the full analysis set. Their mean age was 53 ± 14 years and 29& were women. The eGFR at baseline was 67 ± 22 mL/min/1.73 m2. The median time from transplantation was 7 (3 - 13) years. Dapagliflozin improved the chronic slope of the eGFR compared with placebo. The change in the eGFR from 2 weeks to 12 months after treatment initiation was 2.0 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.0 - 3.1) mL/min/1.73 m2 in the dapagliflozin group and 0.3 (95% CI -0.8 - 1.4) mL/min/1.73 m2 in the placebo group for a between-group difference of 1.7 (95% confidence interval 0.1 - 3.3) mL/min/1.73 m²; p = 0.03. There were no unexpected safety signals and similar rates of adverse events, including infections, between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In heart transplant recipients, dapagliflozin, compared with placebo, improved the slope of the eGFR from 2 weeks to 12 months of treatment.

Mitochondrial DNA in cardiovascular disease.
recs.abstract: Genetic contributions to cardiovascular disease (CVD) are typically examined through nuclear DNA, yet mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is increasingly recognized as a critical, often overlooked determinant of cardiovascular risk. Given the heart's reliance on mitochondrial energy production, mitochondrial dysfunction and mtDNA alterations have emerged as important contributors to CVD pathogenesis. This review examines current evidence linking mtDNA variants, including heteroplasmy and deletions, mtDNA copy number (mtDNA-CN) dynamics, and haplogroup background to major CVD phenotypes, with particular emphasis on atherosclerosis, cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, stroke, hypertension, and heart failure. We conducted a comprehensive PubMed search, prioritizing human population-based and clinical studies, supplemented by key experimental data informing mechanisms. Evidence is strongest for roles of mtDNA variants and heteroplasmy in cardiomyopathies/heart failure, as well as hypertension by impairing mitochondrial energy production and generating harmful oxidants, creating a continuous cycle of mitochondrial injury with further mtDNA damage, besides additional contributions from mtDNA-CN, large deletions, and mitochondrial haplogroups. Mechanistically, mtDNA abnormalities may promote vascular inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered immune signalling; the inflammatory response is a central pathogenic driver of cardiovascular disease, directly promoting atherosclerotic plaque instability, adverse myocardial remodelling, and the progression of heart failure. We subsequently evaluate the evidence for each CVD phenotype in relation to these mtDNA markers. Lastly, current knowledge gaps, methodological challenges, and future research priorities are discussed to support the integration of mtDNA into cardiovascular research and precision medicine.

Trevogrumab (anti-GDF8) with or without garetosmab (anti-activin A) for prevention of muscle loss during semaglutide-induced weight reduction in people with obesity (COURAGE): a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rapid weight loss, as induced by GLP-1 receptor agonists, is accompanied by pronounced muscle loss. GDF8 (myostatin) and activin A (ActA), acting via ActRIIA/B receptors, are negative regulators of muscle mass. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of antibodies blocking GDF8 (trevogrumab) and ActA (garetosmab) on semaglutide-induced weight and muscle loss. METHODS: COURAGE is a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial. This multicentre (60 sites), US-based trial enrolled participants aged 18-80 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). In part A, participants were treated for 26 weeks with semaglutide (titrated to 2·4 mg subcutaneously weekly) in addition to a randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) concomitant treatment: placebo, trevogrumab 200 mg, trevogrumab 400 mg, or trevogrumab 400 mg and garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Trevogrumab was administered subcutaneously weekly and garetosmab was administered intravenously every 4 weeks. Part A also included a subsequent semaglutide withdrawal period, at which point participants (randomly assigned at baseline 1:1 within each group) received either trevogrumab 400 mg or placebo for an additional 26 weeks. In part B, participants were treated with semaglutide for 52 weeks and randomly assigned (1:2:2) to concomitant treatment with placebo, trevogrumab 25 mg, or trevogrumab 75 mg. Groups were stratified according to sex, BMI (<35 kg/m2vs ≥35 kg/m2), and participation in an exploratory MRI substudy assessing thigh muscle volume. Study participants, the principal investigators, and study site personnel were masked to all randomisation assignments throughout the study. Primary endpoints were percent change in lean mass, fat mass, and bodyweight from baseline to week 26 (part A) or week 52 (part B). Efficacy and safety analyses were done in all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of a study drug (efficacy, as randomly assigned; safety, as treated). COURAGE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299098, and is currently active, not recruiting. FINDINGS: 975 participants were enrolled between June 21, 2024, and April 14, 2025. Mean age was 49·0 years (SD 13·2) and mean BMI was 36·7 kg/m2 (SD 5·0); 627 (64%) of 975 participants were female and 348 (36%) were male. In part A (n=605, of whom n=599 received at least one dose of study drug), a substantial decrease in lean mass was observed in the semaglutide plus placebo group at week 26 (-6·6% [95% CI -7·4 to -5·7]); the estimated treatment difference (ETD) versus semaglutide plus placebo was +3·1% (95% CI 1·9 to 4·3) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg, +2·7% (1·5 to 4·0) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg, and +4·5% (3·1 to 5·9) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg. In part B (n=376), lean mass percent change from baseline to week 52 for semaglutide plus placebo was -7·3% (-8·8 to -5·8); the ETD versus semaglutide plus placebo was +1·5% (-0·3 to 3·3) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 25 mg, and +3·1% (1·3 to 4·9) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 75 mg. Change from baseline in fat mass in part A was -15·6% (-17·4 to -13·9) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg group (-3·4% [-5·9 to -0·9]) and the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-11·7% [-14·4 to -9·0]) in part A. No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in fat mass compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Percent change in bodyweight in part A was -10·6 (-11·6 to -9·7) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant for the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-2·7 [-4·1 to -1·2]). No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in bodyweight compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Semaglutide plus trevogrumab (25 mg, 75 mg, 200 mg, or 400 mg) was generally well tolerated with a safety profile similar to semaglutide plus placebo; however, semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg had a high incidence of serious adverse events (14 [9%] of 149) and treatment discontinuations (48 [32%] of 149). Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most commonly reported, and they occurred with similar incidence across treatment groups. Muscle spasms occurred more frequently in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (61 [41%] of 149) compared with the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg or 400 mg groups (23 [8%] of 299) and semaglutide plus placebo groups (seven [5%] of 151). Most adverse events were mild to moderate in severity. Two deaths occurred during the study, both in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group; a causal association between treatment and these events was not identified. INTERPRETATION: This study establishes proof of concept for GDF8 inhibition by trevogrumab alone as a generally well tolerated strategy to preserve lean mass during GLP-1 receptor agonist-induced weight loss. Although the addition of ActA inhibition by garetosmab further improved body composition and weight loss, the combination did not have favourable safety and tolerability. Further study is required to understand whether improved body composition during weight loss might preserve physical function and overall metabolic health. FUNDING: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

recs.title: Modified Posterior Wall Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: the BOX-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: AIMS: The efficacy of left atrial posterior wall isolation (PWI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is controversial. We propose a modified left atrial posterior wall ablation strategy. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of modified posterior wall ablation in patients with persistent AF who underwent first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicenter, single-blind randomized trial, 276 patients with persistent AF were assigned 1:1 to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) with (BOX+) or without modified posterior wall ablation (BOX-). Seven participants withdrew, leaving 269 (BOX+, n=139; BOX-, n=130) for primary endpoint analysis. The primary endpoint was freedom from any documented atrial arrhythmia lasting > 30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs after a 3 -month blanking period. At 12-month follow-up, the primary endpoint occurred in 120 of 139 patients (86.3%) in the BOX+ group and 113 of 130 (86.9%) in the BOX- group (hazard ratio 1.046, 95% CI, 0.54 - 2.01; P = 0.894). The BOX+ group exhibited longer procedure time and ablation time. Acute successful PWI was achieved in 91 (65.5%) patients assigned to BOX+. In a nonprespecified, post-randomization analysis, arrhythmia-free survival was 93.4% in patients with acute successful PWI, 72.9% in those with attempted but unsuccessful PWI, and 86.9% in controls without attempted PWI (overall log-rank P=0.002). Adverse events were similar between groups. CONCLUSION: Routine addition of modified posterior wall ablation did not improve overall outcomes of first-time ablation in persistent AF. However, achieving successful PWI was associated with significantly lower recurrence.

recs.title: Diet-Driven Modulation of the Gut Microbiome to Enhance Neuroplasticity and Cognitive Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
recs.abstract: Cognitive impairment and limited neuroplastic recovery remain major contributors to long-term disability following ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence suggests that stroke-induced disruption of the gut-brain axis, characterized by microbiome dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolite signaling, may influence post-stroke inflammation, synaptic remodeling, and cognitive outcomes. Diet is a key modifiable determinant of gut microbiome composition and metabolic output, yet its role in post-stroke neuroplasticity has not been comprehensively synthesized. This narrative review examines dietary interventions with mechanistic or translational relevance to ischemic stroke recovery, including Mediterranean dietary patterns, ketogenic diets, high-fiber and prebiotic-enriched diets, probiotic and synbiotic supplementation, and intermittent fasting or caloric restriction. We summarize evidence linking diet-induced microbiome modulation to neuroinflammatory regulation, short-chain fatty acid signaling, microglial activity, mitochondrial function, and synaptic plasticity. Shared and diet-specific pathways are discussed, along with current limitations of the evidence base and barriers to clinical translation. Collectively, available data support a biologically plausible role for targeted dietary modulation of the gut microbiome as an adjunctive strategy to enhance cognitive recovery and neuroplasticity after ischemic stroke. Further well-designed clinical studies integrating microbiome profiling, neuroimaging, and cognitive outcomes are needed to define therapeutic potential and guide implementation in stroke rehabilitation. Among these dietary interventions, Mediterranean, high-fiber, and prebiotic-enriched diets currently have the strongest available evidence, while ketogenic and intermittent fasting approaches remain the least supported based on existing clinical and translational evidence.

recs.title: Piezo1 Responsiveness in Muscle Afferents and Mechanoreflex in Diabetic Rats.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Abnormal mechanoreflex function from skeletal muscle significantly contributes to the heightened circulatory response during exercise in type 2 diabetes (T2DM). However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesized that the abnormal cardiovascular responses in T2DM are mediated by mechanoreflex-induced exaggerations resulting from enhanced Piezo1-mediated mechanosensitivity of muscle afferents. METHODS: T2DM rats (Sprague-Dawley rats) were given a high-fat diet in combination with a low dose of streptozotocin. Using an in vivo decerebrated rat model and an ex vivo single-fiber recording preparation, we measured muscle mechanoreflex responses, mechanosensitivity of muscle afferents, and Piezo1-mediated responses. Piezo1 protein levels in the membrane fraction were detected by Western blotting in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells. RESULTS: Blood pressure and sympathetic nerve activity responses to mechanoreflex activation, as well as group IV muscle afferent firing to mechanical stimulation and the Piezo1 agonist (Yoda1), were significantly greater in T2DM rats. More importantly, Piezo1 agonist-induced blood pressure changes and group IV afferent firing were significantly potentiated by administration of lipopolysaccharide, a gut-derived inflammatory endotoxin. Furthermore, lipopolysaccharide significantly increased Piezo1 protein in the cell membrane, which was attenuated by a PKA (protein kinase A) inhibitor. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that activation of the lipopolysaccharide-Piezo1 pathway may contribute to enhanced responsiveness of group IV muscle afferents and may be associated with exaggerated circulatory responses to muscle mechanoreflex activation in T2DM.

recs.title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Recurrent Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The definition of very high risk from the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology 2018 and 2026 cholesterol guidelines may oversimplify heterogeneity in recurrent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. OBJECTIVES: We developed a prediction model for recurrent ASCVD and compared its performance with the 2018 cholesterol guideline. METHODS: We used electronic health records from Kaiser Permanente Southern California (KPSC) for model development and the REGARDS (Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke) cohort for external validation. We included adults with a prior ASCVD and followed them for recurrent ASCVD or up to 10 years. We used elastic net regularization for predictor selection and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model for model development. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity compared with the 2018 guideline. RESULTS: Among 70,310 and 5,239 adults from KPSC and REGARDS, 17,344 and 1,185 experienced recurrent ASCVD during the median (Q1, Q3) follow-up of 6.1 (2.5, 10) and 8.3 (4.0, 10) years, respectively. Time-dependent area under the curves were 0.68 (95% CI: 0.66-0.69) in KPSC and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.65-0.69) in REGARDS. Compared with the 2018 guideline, using a 5-year 15% risk threshold, the model classified a similar proportion of patients as high risk and improved sensitivity from 64% (95% CI: 62%-66%) to 73% (95% CI: 71%-75%) in KPSC and from 69% (95% CI: 65%-72%) to 73% (95% CI: 69%-76%) in REGARDS; specificity remained similar in KPSC (51% and 52%) and improved in REGARDS (from 45% to 50%). CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the 2018 cholesterol guideline, the new model improves identification of individuals at very high risk of recurrent ASCVD, supporting more personalized treatment decisions.

recs.title: Reframing disease elimination: an update from the Lancet Commission on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
recs.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

recs.title: Electrocardiographic and Echocardiographic Markers of Atrial and Ventricular Remodeling Allow Identification of Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac sarcoidosis (CS) is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of systemic sarcoidosis. Although positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging provide high diagnostic accuracy, they are unsuitable for first-line screening. Widely available modalities such as electrocardiography (ECG) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) focusing only on ventricular abnormalities show limited sensitivity. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate whether a combined diagnostic model integrating ECG and TTE parameters, emphasizing atrial and ventricular remodeling, can accurately identify patients with CS. METHODS: We prospectively included 252 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven sarcoidosis. CS was defined by characteristic findings on PET-CT or cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. A comprehensive set of atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE parameters was analyzed. Diagnostic models were constructed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and discriminative performance was assessed. RESULTS: CS was identified in 37 (14.7%) patients. On ECG, prolonged P-wave duration, prolonged QRS duration, and reduced T-wave amplitude in lead aVR were independently associated with CS. On TTE, increased left atrial volume index, increased left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, and impaired left ventricular global longitudinal strain emerged as significant predictors. ECG- and TTE-based models showed comparable discrimination for CS identification (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.87 for both). A combined ECG/TTE model, driven primarily by QRS duration, left atrial volume index, and left ventricular global longitudinal strain, achieved the highest diagnostic performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.90). CONCLUSIONS: An exploratory multimodal, noninvasive approach integrating atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE markers provides high diagnostic accuracy for identifying CS and may serve as a pragmatic screening and triage tool to guide referral for advanced cardiac imaging. Clinical Trial Registration DRKS00031557 on drks.de (German Clinical Trials Register).

recs.title: Comprehensive m6A landscape from direct RNA sequencing reveals SYNPO2L RNA isoform regulation mechanisms in heart failure.
recs.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that epitranscriptomic regulation, particularly the m6A modification, contributes to heart failure progression. However, modification dynamics are not yet mapped and studied at base resolution and transcript isoform level. Here we use Nanopore direct RNA sequencing to profile m6A remodeling at transcriptome-wide and site-specific resolution in a mouse heart failure model. We identify thousands of differentially methylated sites with distinct sequence motifs and associations with RNA regulatory and cardiac function processes. Cross-species comparison reveals conserved m6A regulatory features in mouse and human heart failure. Isoform-resolved analysis further uncovers co/posttranscriptional regulation events involving isoform switching and m6A regulation in the SYNPO2L transcript. Mechanistically, m6A modification, alternative promoter usage and associated regulatory elements collectively explain this observation. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive, high-resolution characterization of m6A landscape and its remodeling in heart failure. Isoform-level regulation exemplifies an underappreciated shaping of RNA expression and modification.

recs.title: Sex Differences in Quantified Mitral Regurgitation-Reply.
Digital Health Intervention to Optimize Heart Failure Management After Hospital Discharge in Brazil (OPT-HF): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Barriers to optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure include infrequent clinical visits, clinician inertia, and poor patient knowledge. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may mitigate these barriers, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated whether a DHI would improve GDMT use and other outcomes in Brazil. METHODS: We enrolled adults admitted for heart failure with ejection fraction <50% and GDMT gaps (≥1 GDMT class not started or ≥2 classes ≤50% target dose) across 5 Brazilian public hospitals from November 2023 to August 2025. Participants were randomized to usual care or the DHI comprising a patient-facing app linked to a provider dashboard, supporting nurse-led remote monitoring, cardiologist teleconsultations, and self-care education. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mean heart failure GDMT score (0-12) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included differences in health status, self-care, hospitalization rates, and all-cause mortality. Intention-to-treat analyses used baseline-adjusted linear regression and estimated risk ratios. RESULTS: Among 154 randomized patients (DHI: 87; usual care: 67), mean age was 65±14 years; 62% were male, 66% were Black, 44% had ≤4 years of education, and 68% were New York Heart Association class III/IV. Primary outcome data were available for 141 participants (91.6%; DHI: 81; usual care: 60). Mean GDMT scores increased from 7.2 in both groups to 10.5 with DHI versus 7.5 with usual care at 90 days (changes: +3.3 versus +0.3 points; adjusted difference, 3.01 [95% CI, 2.30-3.73]; P<0.001). A borderline difference was observed in health status (7.89; P=0.052). Improvements were observed in self-care (β=14.79 [95% CI, 9.78-19.81]; P<0.001). Fewer participants were hospitalized with DHI than usual care (9/87 [10.3%] versus 15/67 [22.4%]; risk ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.21-0.99]; P=0.048), with no statistically significant difference for deaths. CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalized for heart failure in Brazil, a context-adapted DHI improved GDMT use, self-care, and reduced hospitalizations. These findings provide early randomized evidence supporting DHI for GDMT optimization in low-resource settings. REGISTRATION: URL: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-10vpf9bm; Unique identifier: U1111-1295-1864.

recs.title: Association Between Stroke Subtype and Outcomes of Edaravone Dexborneol: A Subgroup Analysis of the EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of edaravone dexborneol among acute ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear. We evaluated its association with clinical outcomes by stroke subtype. METHODS: This secondary analysis of the prospective EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) study included patients with acute ischemic stroke treated at 72 Chinese stroke centers from December 2022 to October 2023. Patients were classified as having large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) or non-LAA stroke and grouped by edaravone dexborneol use. Primary outcomes were 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 or 1 and 0 to 2 and ordinal mRS shift. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality, intracranial hemorrhage, and in-hospital adverse events. RESULTS: Among 4401 patients, 1061 (24.1%) had LAA and 3340 (75.9%) had non-LAA stroke; the median age was 65 years, and 66.8% were men. Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in the non-LAA group, including higher odds of achieving mRS 0 or 1 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.25 [95% CI, 1.06-1.47]), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.15-1.71]), and a favorable mRS shift (aOR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.12-1.46]; all P<0.05). No significant functional benefit was observed in the LAA group of mRS 0 or 1 (aOR, 0.91; P=0.50), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 0.88; P=0.43), or mRS shift (aOR, 0.92; P=0.50). Significant interactions were observed between edaravone dexborneol and stroke subtype (P for interaction=0.03 for mRS 0 or 1, P=0.005 for mRS 0 to 2, and P=0.009 for favorable mRS shift). Safety outcomes were comparable between treatment groups. CONCLUSIONS: Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in non-LAA but not LAA stroke.

Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain. METHODS: A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007). CONCLUSIONS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

High on the Heart? Cannabis Use and Cardiovascular Disease: A Systematic Review.
recs.abstract: Cannabis use has increased substantially over the past 2 decades following shifts in public perception, legalization, and medical usage. Although neurological and psychiatric effects are well known, the cardiovascular effects of cannabis exposure are largely understudied. This review evaluates the cardiovascular effects of cannabis use by examining clinical evidence, epidemiological data, and underlying biochemical mechanisms. This review examines cannabis-related cardiovascular conditions, including atherosclerosis, arrhythmias, heart failure, and stroke. The analysis focused on cannabinoid composition, route of administration, frequency of use, and cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence indicates that acute and high Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol/cannabidiol ratio cannabis use is associated with increased risks of various cardiovascular outcomes, especially among younger individuals without cardiovascular risk factors. Given rising use and increasing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol potency, clinicians must routinely assess cannabis exposure when evaluating cardiovascular disease, especially in younger patients. Future research must prioritize the development of standardized exposure metrics in cannabis-related cardiovascular disease research, thus allowing clinicians and patients to better understand the cardiovascular risks of cannabis use and initiate effective cessation strategies.

recs.title: Sacubitril/valsartan for radiation-induced heart disease in children: preclinical and clinical findings.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) is a life-threatening sequela for cancer survivors. A proactive preventive strategy is urgently needed but remains elusive, particularly for the vulnerable paediatric population where prospective data are scarce. To address this gap, this study aimed to evaluate the prophylactic efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan against RIHD in children through a comprehensive translational research pipeline. METHODS: A prospective observational study was first conducted in 40 paediatric solid tumour patients, comparing cardiac function before and 1 week after radiotherapy, with 80 healthy controls. A juvenile rat RIHD model was then established, in which the efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan was assessed and validated through longitudinal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, histopathology, bulk RNA-seq, and single-nucleus RNA-seq. Finally, a prospective clinical cohort (n = 15 sacubitril/valsartan, n = 15 control) was conducted in paediatric patients post-radiotherapy, with a 12-month follow-up for efficacy and safety. RESULTS: In paediatric patients, radiotherapy significantly impaired biventricular function, notably reducing left ventricular global longitudinal strain, and mean heart radiation dose was significantly correlated with cardiac function impairment. In juvenile rats, sacubitril/valsartan attenuated pathological ventricular wall thickening, myocardial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, and perfusion deficits. Mechanistically, it mitigated endothelial cell damage and immune cell activation, promoted a macrophage phenotypic shift from M1 to M2, suppressed fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, and broadly attenuated pro-fibrotic and inflammatory cell-cell communication. In the clinical cohort, sacubitril/valsartan significantly improved left ventricular global longitudinal strain and aortic compliance vs controls, with a favourable safety profile. CONCLUSIONS: This first-in-kind translational study demonstrates that early prophylaxis with sacubitril/valsartan is a feasible and effective strategy to mitigate radiation-induced cardiotoxicity in children. These findings, underpinned by multi-modal validation from bench to bedside, challenge the reactive management paradigm in paediatric cardio-oncology and establish a foundational evidence base for a new standard of proactive heart care in childhood cancer survivors.

recs.title: Inflammation and early atherosclerosis beyond traditional risk factors: an imaging study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Understanding how inflammation contributes to subclinical atherosclerosis (SA) plaque burden, beyond the impact of established cardiovascular risk factors, holds significant implications for the success of preventive strategies focused on the reduction of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The aim of this study was to investigate the relative contribution of inflammation, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDLc), and systolic blood pressure (SBP), as determinants of SA plaque burden in a cohort of middle-aged, asymptomatic individuals, using non-invasive imaging techniques. METHODS: Participants from the Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis (PESA) study (median age 45 years) underwent longitudinal screening every 3 years (baseline, 3- and 6-year visits) involving serial blood testing [including white blood cell (WBC) count, fibrinogen, oxidized LDLc, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein], physical examinations and imaging assessments with three-dimensional vascular ultrasound of peripheral arteries, and coronary artery calcium quantification. Global plaque volume (GPV, mm3; bilateral carotid plus femoral plaque burden) at 6-year follow-up was the primary outcome. Multivariable linear regression and proportional odds models determined the link of GPV to both inflammatory markers and established cardiovascular risk factors. RESULTS: Of the 3471 participants, 58% had SA (GPV >0 mm3) at 6-year follow-up. WBC count had the strongest statistical associations with 6-year SA burden after adjusting for age, sex, baseline LDLc, and mean SBP, with an estimated 32.6% increase in GPV per one standard deviation (SD) increase in WBC (Z = 7.33, P < 1 × 10-10). GPV at 6 years increased 40.9% per one SD increase in baseline LDLc and 42.7% per one SD increase in mean SBP (Z = 8.80 and Z = 7.97, respectively, both P < 1 × 10-10; their SDs were 29.4 mg/dL and 11.5 mmHg, respectively), followed by fibrinogen (16.8% increase in GPV per one SD increase, Z = 3.91, P < .0001). High-sensitivity C-reactive protein was not predictive of greater GPV at 6 years (Z = 1.36, P = .174). For WBC, the marked trend in risk occurred only at levels above its median. Similar patterns were observed for separate analyses of carotid and femoral plaque volumes, and coronary artery calcium. Increasing levels of WBC and fibrinogen were also associated with a greater anatomical spread of disease. CONCLUSIONS: Inflammation contributes to SA burden, as assessed by direct plaque quantification, beyond the effects of LDLc and SBP. These findings indicate that inflammation, captured through the use of systemic inflammatory markers, is a risk factor relevant across the entire continuum of atherosclerosis, exerting a deleterious impact comparable to that of LDLc and SBP.

Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses. METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes. CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

recs.title: Long-Term Prognostic Value of Scar Characteristics in Cardiac Magnetic Resonance to Predict Appropriate Therapies in Primary Prevention.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) provides unique insights into ventricular arrhythmogenic substrate, although few studies have analyzed its long-term value in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) for primary prevention. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the role of LGE characteristics in stratifying arrhythmogenic risk in patients with ICD implantation for primary prevention over long-term follow-up. METHODS: This was a prospective study, between 2011 and 2017, in which 226 patients who underwent LGE CMR before ICD implantation for primary prevention were consecutively enrolled. Dedicated software (ADAS 3D) was used to quantify LGE, border zone, core, and conducting channels (CCs). RESULTS: The median age was 62.9 years (Q1-Q3: 55.4-68.5 years), with 52% of participants (n = 104) with ischemic cardiomyopathy and a median MADIT (Multicenter Automatic Defibrillator Implantation Trial) score of 54 (Q1-Q3: 42-64). After a median follow-up period of 8.1 years (Q1-Q3: 6.2-10 years), 59 patients (29.5%) reached the primary endpoint (appropriate ICD therapy). LGE mass >10 g (HR: 3.58; 95% CI: 1.29-9.93; P = 0.014), CCs (HR: 3.42; 95% CI: 1.69-6.96; P = 0.009), and the presence of both LGE mass >10 g and CCs (34.92% vs 5.55%; HR: 4.65; 95% CI: 1.46-14.8; P = 0.009) were strongly associated with the primary endpoint. Patients without CCs and with LGE mass < 10 g had a very low rate of appropriate therapies (negative predictive value = 92%). LGE parameters remained independently associated with the primary endpoint after adjustment for MADIT score. CONCLUSIONS: The characteristics of potential arrhythmia substrate assessed using LGE CMR are potent predictors of ventricular arrhythmias after ICD implantation for the primary prevention of sudden death.

Association of Stroke Severity With Efficacy of Early Tirofiban Infusion After Intravenous Thrombolysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aims to assess the effects of stroke severity at admission on the efficacy and safety of early tirofiban infusion following intravenous thrombolysis in patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke using data from the ASSET-IT (Advancing Stroke Safety and Efficacy Through Early Tirofiban Administration After Intravenous Thrombolysis) trial. METHODS: All 832 patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke from the ASSET-IT database were included in this exploratory post hoc analysis. The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were an excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-1 at 90 days) and intracranial hemorrhage. RESULTS: Among the 832 patients included, the median age was 69 (interquartile range, 59-76) years, 531 (63.8%) were men, 367 (44.1%) had minor stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6), and 465 (55.9%) had moderate-to-severe stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≥6). There were significant interactions between the primary efficacy and safety outcomes (Pinteraction=0.008, Pinteraction=0.03; respectively). We observed that among patients with NIHSS score ≥6, tirofiban markedly increased odds of achieving an excellent functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 2.13 [95% CI, 1.44-3.17]; P<0.001) without significantly increasing the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.37-2.09]; P=0.77). In contrast, no significant benefit was observed in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6 group (adjusted odds ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.64-1.63]; P=0.94) but there was a significant increase in the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 6.51 [95% CI, 1.42-62.03]; P=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Early tirofiban infusion may be more beneficial for patients with moderate-to-severe stroke treated with intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of onset, while simultaneously suggesting an increased potential risk of intracranial hemorrhage in minor stroke. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06134622.

Thymectomy Extent, Immune Recovery, and Infectious Burden After Neonatal Cardiac Surgery.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neonatal cardiac surgery frequently requires thymectomy, but the consequences of extensive thymic removal remain uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 105 neonates undergoing sternotomy (2015-2024), comparing infections and 6-month lymphocyte recovery after partial versus total thymectomy, with Firth regression adjusted for bypass duration and surgical era. Separate cohorts underwent paired plasma biomarker (n=8) and whole-blood RNA sequencing (n=4) analysis before and after thymectomy. RESULTS: Among 105 neonates, 27 underwent partial and 78 total thymectomy. Multiple infections occurred in 2 of 27 (7%) after partial and 23 of 78 (30%) after total thymectomy (P=0.02); after adjustment for bypass duration and surgical era, the association was not statistically significant (Firth-adjusted odds ratio, 2.99 [95% CI, 0.82-15.85]; P=0.10). Median lymphocyte count decreased after total but increased after partial thymectomy (change, -0.8 versus +0.9×103/μL; P=0.011). Tumor necrosis factor-α decreased in all 8 biomarker participants (unadjusted P=0.0078). RNA sequencing in 4 patients (2 partial, 2 total thymectomy) identified 835 differentially expressed genes; pre-T-cell receptor α decreased in all 4 pairs (log2 fold change, -2.50; adjusted P=6×10-6). CONCLUSIONS: Total thymectomy was associated with reduced 6-month lymphocyte recovery and higher unadjusted odds of multiple infections. The infection association was not statistically significant after adjustment, and few events (2 of 27 after partial thymectomy) limit precision and cannot exclude a clinically important effect; these findings are hypothesis-generating. Biomarker and transcriptomic findings are exploratory and cannot distinguish thymectomy from surgery, maturation, or postoperative recovery. Prospective studies are underway to evaluate thymic preservation and autologous reimplantation.

Intraoperative Hypotension and Risk of Cuff Blood Pressure Inaccuracy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypotension is associated with cardiovascular complications and mortality, making accurate blood pressure (BP) monitoring essential. However, the accuracy of noninvasive oscillometric cuff BP (Cuff BP) during hypotension is uncertain. We examined the association between intraoperative hypotension and Cuff BP inaccuracy. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort included 22 812 adults undergoing noncardiac surgery from April 2013 through November 2023, with 348 888 simultaneous Cuff BP and invasive arterial BP (Arterial BP) pairs. Pairs with arterial systolic BP >120 mm Hg or diastolic BP >80 mm Hg were excluded to focus on the hypotensive range. Hypotension was defined as arterial mean arterial pressure (MAP)<65 mm Hg and categorized as mild (55 to <65), moderate (45 to <55), or severe (35 to <45 mm Hg). Cuff BP inaccuracy was defined as an absolute MAP difference >10 mm Hg from Arterial BP. Multivariable generalized estimating equation models estimated adjusted odds ratios and 95% CIs. RESULTS: Compared with normal MAP (≥65 mm Hg), hypotension was associated with higher odds of Cuff BP inaccuracy (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 [95% CI, 1.40-1.50]). Adjusted odds ratios increased with severity (P value for trend <0.001): 1.28 (95% CI, 1.24-1.32) for mild, 2.33 (95% CI, 2.20-2.46) for moderate, and 7.00 (95% CI, 6.13-8.00) for severe hypotension. Sensitivity for correct MAP classification decreased from 87.4% for normal MAP to 32.6%, 20.2%, and 9.6% for mild, moderate, and severe hypotension. CONCLUSIONS: We found a significantly higher risk of Cuff BP inaccuracy in patients with intraoperative hypotension, supporting cautious interpretation of Cuff BP during intraoperative hypotension.

recs.title: Myeloid deficiency of the PRC2 complex protein JARID2 promotes foam cell formation through elevated plasma lipids without altering atherosclerosis progression.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease in which macrophages drive plaque development, progression, and eventual destabilization. Epigenetic modulation of macrophages may offer a promising approach to reduce disease progression and residual inflammatory risk that persists despite lipid-lowering therapy. EZH2, the catalytic subunit of PRC2 responsible for depositing H3K27me3, a histone modification associated with gene silencing, is pro-atherogenic in macrophages, while the contribution of PRC2 co-factors remains unexplored. We found the co-factor Jumonji AT-Rich Interactive Domain 2 (JARID2) to be upregulated in unstable human atherosclerotic plaques, prompting us to investigate its role in atherosclerosis. METHODS: To investigate the role of macrophage Jarid2 in atherosclerosis, we generated myeloid-specific Jarid2-deficient mice (Jarid2del; LysMCreJarid2fl/fl). Bone marrow from Jarid2del or control (Jarid2wt) mice was transplanted to Ldlr-/- recipients, followed by a high cholesterol diet for 9 weeks to induce atherosclerosis. RESULTS: Myeloid Jarid2 deficiency modestly increased plasma cholesterol and triglyceride levels and enhanced foam cell formation. Despite increased plasma lipid levels, atherosclerotic lesion size and composition remained unchanged. Single-cell RNA sequencing of aortic arch plaques revealed that Jarid2 deficiency has both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects in multiple myeloid subsets. Together, the elevated plasma lipid levels and mixed context-dependent inflammatory phenotype suggest that opposing, potentially compensatory mechanisms counterbalance each other, resulting in no net change in overall plaque size. CONCLUSIONS: JARID2 is upregulated in unstable human atherosclerotic plaques, whereas myeloid Jarid2 deficiency in mice modestly elevates plasma lipid levels and promotes foam cell formation without affecting atherosclerosis progression.

Skeletal Muscle sEVs Mediate Exercise-Induced Cardioprotection in I/R Injury.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise training has been demonstrated to provide direct endogenous cardioprotection and to reduce cardiovascular disease risk. Skeletal muscle functions not only as an organ for movement but also as a vital secretory organ. However, how muscle-heart crosstalk contributes to exercise-induced cardioprotection remains largely unclear. Here, we investigated the cardioprotective effects of exercise-induced small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) derived from skeletal muscle in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury in mice. METHODS: An adeno-associated virus 8-dMCK (double-muscle creatine kinase)-CD63-EGFP (enhanced green fluorescent protein) reporter system was used to track skeletal muscle-derived sEVs in the heart of mice after 4 weeks of exercise. To determine whether sEVs from exercised skeletal muscle mediate cardioprotection, cardiac sEV abundance was increased by intramyocardial injection and decreased by generating skeletal muscle-specific Rab27a knockout mice. The molecular mechanism was elucidated by profiling sEV-enriched microRNAs and validating their functions in cardiomyocytes and mouse MI/R injury models. The translational potential was then assessed in human exercise cohorts. Finally, the therapeutic efficacy was evaluated using miRNA agomirs and adeno-associated virus 8-mediated, skeletal muscle-specific overexpression of miRNAs in MI/R injury models. RESULTS: Exercise promoted the entry of skeletal muscle-derived sEVs into the heart. Skeletal muscle-derived sEVs from exercised mice significantly attenuated MI/R injury by reducing cardiomyocyte apoptosis and improving mitochondrial respiration. Exercise-mediated protection against MI/R injury was attenuated after inhibiting the secretion of sEVs from skeletal muscle. Mechanistically, exercise-enriched sEVs delivered miR-451a and miR-143-3p to cardiomyocytes, thereby modulating the PERK (protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase)-ATF4-CHOP stress-response pathway and the USP46/P53 axis, thus reducing cardiomyocyte death. Skeletal muscle-specific overexpression of miR-451a/143-3p recapitulated the cardioprotective effects of exercise in vivo. Furthermore, exercising humans also showed elevated levels of miR-451a/143-3p in their skeletal muscle and circulating sEVs. CONCLUSIONS: Our study reveals a novel exercise-induced cardioprotective mechanism via muscle-heart crosstalk, highlighting a promising therapeutic approach for treating cardiovascular disease.

recs.title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored. METHODS: Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA. RESULTS: A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P<0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P=0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P<0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort (P<0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement (P=0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement (P=0.08). CONCLUSIONS: Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending external validation.

recs.title: Rationale and Design of a Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Trial: LEAP-Block.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrioventricular block with normal cardiac function is common with right ventricular pacing, which raises risks of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and symptomatic heart failure in some patients with high pacing burden. Left bundle-branch area pacing demonstrates protective potential to reduce the risk of heart failure on the basis of observational studies. Evidence from a large multicenter randomized controlled trial remains limited. METHODS: The LEAP-Block (Impact of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Atrioventricular Block) study is a prospective multicenter, investigator-initiated randomized controlled trial aiming to verify the hypothesis that left bundle-branch area pacing might have superior impact to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in patients with atrioventricular block requiring high burden of ventricular pacing and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%. A total of 484 patients will be randomized to either left bundle-branch area pacing or right ventricular pacing (1:1). The primary end point is the composite events of all-cause death, heart failure events, and upgrade to biventricular pacing-delivered cardiac resynchronization therapy during at least 24 months of follow-up. Secondary end points include changes in echocardiographic, electrocardiographic, and pacing parameters and device-related complications. CONCLUSIONS: The LEAP-Block study aims to compare the impact of left bundle-branch area pacing versus conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved cardiac function with respect to midterm clinical outcomes. This trial will provide high-quality evidence for the selection of optimal pacing strategies in clinical practice. REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT04730921.

recs.title: ZEB1-Driven GLS1 Transcription Promotes Macrophage Glutamine Metabolism in PAH.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The transcriptional mechanisms governing macrophage glutamine metabolism in pulmonary arterial hypertension remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of ZEB1 (zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1)-mediated transcriptional regulation in macrophage metabolic reprogramming and the development of pulmonary arterial hypertension. METHODS: Clinical samples and multiomics data sets were analyzed to characterize ZEB1 expression in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Myeloid-specific ZEB1 conditional knockout mice were subjected to hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension. Transcriptomic sequencing, metabolomic profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and coimmunoprecipitation were integrated to define ZEB1-dependent molecular, metabolic, and inflammatory programs in pulmonary and bone marrow-derived macrophages. Therapeutic potential was further evaluated using pharmacological interventions and adenoviral ZEB1 silencing in monocrotaline-induced pulmonary hypertension in rats. RESULTS: ZEB1 was upregulated in pulmonary arterial hypertension and enriched in recruited disease-associated macrophages. Myeloid-specific ZEB1 deletion attenuated macrophage inflammation, pulmonary vascular remodeling, and right ventricular dysfunction. Mechanistically, ZEB1 bound the GLS (glutaminase) promoter and recruited BRD4 (bromodomain-containing protein 4), enhancing histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation at the GLS promoter and promoting GLS transcription and glutamine metabolic reprogramming. Restoration of GLS partially reversed the metabolic and inflammatory effects of ZEB1 deficiency. Pharmacological targeting of ZEB1, combined BRD4 and GLS inhibition, and adenoviral ZEB1 silencing ameliorated experimental pulmonary hypertension. CONCLUSIONS: ZEB1 promotes macrophage glutamine metabolic reprogramming by recruiting BRD4 and enhancing histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation-dependent GLS transcription. This ZEB1-driven metabolic program promotes macrophage inflammation and pulmonary vascular remodeling, identifying the ZEB1-BRD4-GLS regulatory axis as a potential therapeutic target in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
